0.en: 2. [Assessment of the] Deliberations in the Assembly of the Estates of the Kingdom of Württemberg in the Years 1815 and 1816. XXXIII issues.124)
0.zh: 2. [评述]符腾堡王国等级议会会议中的审议（1815 与 1816 年）。XXXIII 期。124)

en: The undertaking, begun two and a half years ago, of completing a German monarchy such as we have seen arise in our times, by the introduction of a representative constitution, has from its beginning aroused so general an interest in the German public that nothing could have happened to it more agreeable than that the deliberations of the Württemberg assembly of the estates should have been made publicly known.
In place of the hopes which accompanied the beginning and the progress, at the end success and judgement must show themselves.

The 33 issues to which this consideration is at first limited do not indeed yet contain the completion of the main purpose, but they form in that respect a historical whole, insofar as on the one hand they present the course of events up to the death of the king, who founded the monarchy and also began the second step, that of its inner free constitution, and the peculiar development of this event could in its main features be regarded as belonging to his reign; - on the other hand the work on the part of the estates appears as a completed one, insofar as a committee appointed by them for this purpose finished with its draft of a constitution, which has likewise appeared in print.
zh: 那项始于两年半以前的事务——通过引入代议制宪法，把我们在我们时代目睹其诞生的一个德意志君主国完成——从一开始就激起了德国公众如此普遍的兴趣，以至于对它而言，再没有什么比符腾堡等级会议的审议被公之于众更令人快慰的了。
伴随开端与进程的那些希望，在结尾处必须由成果与评判来替代。

这一评述起初所限定的 33 期，确实尚未包含主要目的完成；但就此而言它们构成一个历史整体：一方面，它们呈现了直到那位国王去世为止的历程——正是他创建了君主国，并且也已迈出了第二步，即在内部自由地组建君主国；这一事件本身特有的发展，就其主要轮廓而言，可以被视为属于他的统治；另一方面，等级议会方面的工作则显得是一件已完成的事情，因为由他们为此委派的委员会已连同其宪法草案一道完成，而该草案同样已经付印。

en: These deliberations do indeed present at first only one side of the works of that attempt, namely the public works, in so far as they enter the assembly of the estates; the inner history of the labours of the cabinet and the ministry, as well as what took place among the people outside the assembly, the possible outward purposes and activities of the members of the estates, in short whatever one is otherwise accustomed to reckon among the secret connection of events and actions, is veiled here.

The interest of the public has, however, of itself been directed above all to the public part of the deliberations, which in any case has above all the character of furnishing the worthy materials of history.

The so-called secret motive powers and intentions of individual persons, anecdotes and subjective influences were held to be the most important in a psychological view of history which was still popular not long ago.

This view, however, has now gone out of credit, and history strives again after its dignity, to present the nature and the course of the substantial thing and to give recognition to the characters of the acting persons from what they do; the conviction has become more general that neither the thing nor the characters emerge in their solidity and are to be recognised from accidents.
zh: 这些审议固然首先只呈现出那场尝试的工作的一个方面，即那些进入等级会议的公开工作；内阁与各部的工作的内在历史、以及在会议之外于人民中所发生的一切、等级议会成员可能有的外在目的与活动，总之一切通常被归入事件与行动之隐秘联系的东西，在这里都被遮蔽了。
不过公众的兴趣本来就自然而然地主要指向了审议的公开部分；而这一部分本来就主要具有提供历史之可敬素材的性质。
在一种不久之前还颇为流行的心理学式的历史观中，个别个人的所谓隐秘动力与意图、轶事与主观的作用，被认为是最为重要的。
然而这种观点如今已不再被采信，历史又重新追求自己的尊严：呈现实质之事的本性与其进程，并从行动者们所做的事情上让人认出他们的品格；人们更为普遍地确信：无论那件事本身还是那些品格，都不可能从偶然情形中以其扎实面目浮现出来并被认出。

en: The historical events which we here see before us have the peculiar charm that they do not contain so considerable a part of the past as a history of more distant times; the great purposes and interests, as well as the smaller peculiarities and outward trivialities, still have a present.

The concepts regarding the object of the interest which we have to bring with us to this event, we may not demand from any more distant age, not even from that of cultivated Greece and Rome; they are peculiar to our own time.

Then we see these ideas about the state constitution and in particular about the admission of a share in it, by which an influence in it and a public life are granted to the people, not here as the thoughts of one writer compared with the thoughts of another, but a German government and a German people engaged in the spiritual work about these objects and occupied with the thoughts in the rebirth of a reality.
zh: 我们在这里所看到的历史事件有一种独特的魅力：它们所包含的往昔并不像更遥远时代的历史那样占据如此可观的一段；那些重大的目的与利益，以及那些较小的特殊之处与外在的琐屑，如今仍然在场。
我们必须随身带到这里来的、关于所关心之对象的概念，我们不能向任何更遥远的时代去索取——连文明希腊与罗马的时代也不能；它们是我们这个时代所独有的。
于是我们在这里看到的这些关于国家宪法的、尤其是关于让人民分享其中一份、从而使人民得以对它有所参与并被赋予一种公共生活的观念，并不是一位作者的思想与另一位作者的思想相比较，而是看到一个德意志政府和一个德意志人民正围绕这些对象从事精神上的工作，并且在一个现实的重生中忙于这些思想。

en: The time had brought for Württemberg a new task and the demand for its solution, the task of establishing the Württemberg lands into a state.

After the absurdity of the institution called the German Empire - which was, to put it most aptly, designated by a historian with at least some wit as the constitution of anarchy - had finally reached its deserved and, in its outward form and manner, appropriate ignominious end, the former Württemberg not only received an enlargement by more than double of its previous extent, but this whole, whose parts had previously been German imperial fiefs, the part which had constituted the duchy having been also a Bohemian afterfief, threw off this subordination, entered with the royal dignity of the prince into sovereignty and into the position of a state, - one of the real German realms which occupy the place of the nothingness which had borne only the empty name of an empire.
zh: 时代为符腾堡带来了一项新的任务以及解决它的要求：把符腾堡领地建为一个国家。

在那个被称为「德意志帝国」的设置之荒谬（一位至少还算有才情的史家大概最恰当地把它称作无政府状态的组建）终于迎来了它应得的、而且在外在形式与方式上与它相称的可耻结局之后，原来的符腾堡不仅得到了比其原有疆域大出一倍以上的扩张，而且这个整体——其各部分此前是德意志帝国的采邑，其中构成公爵领地的那个部分同时还是波希米亚的附属采邑——也摆脱了这种从属，以君主的王家尊位进入主权地位，进入一个国家的地位——它属于那些真正的德意志国，它们占据了那个徒具帝国空名的虚无之物的位置。

en: Such epochs are rarest of all, and no less rare are the individuals to whom fate allotted the distinguished lot of founding states.

The history of these few is usually lost in a grey prehistory and in a state of wild, at least still little-cultivated customs, where indeed a state had come about outwardly, but the inner arrangement lay in the simple habits of the people and in the character of the chief.

The historical origin of articulated constitutions has been spread out over a long series of centuries; to the few main features which lay at the basis, the need of the moment, distress and the force of circumstances gave each time a development and additions at some single point.

The point of view about which the nearer labours of this formation turn is quite simple; on the one hand they are the efforts of the government to master the power and the presumptions of the aristocratic intermediate member and to win for the state its rights against it, on the other hand the efforts of the third estate, which often also calls itself the people, against the same intermediate power, sometimes also against the government itself, to win and force for itself the rights of citizenship.

Thus a constitution, viewed in overview, shows itself as arisen as an aggregate, the development having advanced unevenly, individual parts having remained behind, others having been extended into troublesome excrescences, so that such a constitution resembles an old house whose simple basic form a long series of owners, in accordance with the enlargements of the family and the need of the moment, has transformed into a collection of annexes and corners which have their individual conveniences but together make up an irregular and unintelligible whole.

The intellectual culture of the time has given the idea of a state and thereby of its essential unity, and a twenty-five-year reality which has just elapsed and was for the most part terrible has given the contemplation of the manifold attempts to grasp the idea, and a precious and complete experience.

The favour of circumstances finally granted to the ruler of Württemberg in this also the third thing, the external conditions, and moreover the distinguished advantage that he did not find the aristocratic middle class in the shape of an already fixed obstacle in a privileged nobility of the land, but that this element now seemed to be first of all only to be taken up.
The king thus seemed to be placed in the position unique in history of being able to give a constitution from a single casting.
zh: 这样的时代极其罕见，而那些被命运赋予建国这一卓越使命的个人也同样罕见。
这少数人的历史大多失落在一片灰暗的史前时代与一种野蛮的、至少还谈不上文明的习俗状态之中：在那里对外而言固然已经形成了一个国家，但内部的安排却仍然在于民众朴素的习俗和首领的性格之中。
有结构、有层次的宪法的历史形成被拉长在绵延数百年的系列之中；对于作为基础的那少数几项主要特征，时代的需要、困境以及情势的强力，每一次都在某一个单独之点上赋予了它发展与增添。
这一形成过程的种种较切近的努力所围绕的观点，是相当简单的：一方面是政府为压服贵族这一中间环节的权力与僭越、并为国家争得针对这一环节的权利而作的努力；另一方面则是第三等级——它往往也以人民自居——针对同一中间权力、有时也针对政府本身，为自己争取并强行取得公民权利而作的努力。
这样，一部宪法从总体上一看便显示为作为聚合体而形成：其发展并不均衡推进，个别部分掉队，另一些则扩展成了碍事的旁枝，于是这样的宪法就如同一座老房子——它那简单的基本形式被一长串占有者按照家室的扩张与一时的需要，变成了一堆附属的搭建与转角，各有各的便利，合在一起却构成一个不匀整而又不可理解的整体。
时代的精神教养给出了国家、从而也给出了国家之本质统一性的观念；而一段刚刚过去的、二十五年的、通常来说极为可怕的现实，则给出了对把握这一观念之种种尝试的观照，以及一份宝贵而完整的经验。
最后，情势的恩惠还在这方面给了符腾堡的统治者第三样东西，即外在的条件；而且还给了他一个出色的便利：他所面对的并不是以享有特权的地方贵族之形态早已确定下来的贵族中间阶层这一障碍，而是这个成分眼下似乎才刚刚要被接纳进来。
国王由此似乎被置于历史上独一无二的位置上：能够一气呵成地给出一部宪法。

en: Of the sovereignty attained, one side, the existence and recognition of the new Württemberg state towards the outside, was accomplished.

The first time of their origin fell into circumstances in which everything was imperiously called up for the outward establishment and maintenance, so that inwardwards the means had to be gathered together by a vigorous ministerial government and made ready for use in a firm hand.
Now the time had come in which not only the power of the state, but also its will could become alive.

The good fortune and the efforts of the European governments and their peoples had achieved it to free the sovereignty of the German realms from the limitation under which it still lay, and thereby brought about the possibility of first promising to the peoples free constitutions.

But a higher necessity than lies in the positive bond of a promise lies in the nature of the concepts which have become a general conviction and which attach to a monarchy the determination of a representative constitution, of a lawful state and of an influence of the people in legislation. - Friedrich II. now also took this second step, of creating the monarchical state inwardly.
zh: 在已经取得的主权之中，有一面——新符腾堡国家在对外的存在与被承认——已经完成。
它们最初成立的那段时期，落在这样的情势之中：一切都被强行征调去用于对外的建立与维持，因此对内的诸般手段必须由一个有力的各部政府聚集起来，并在稳固的掌握中准备好以供使用。
如今，时代到来，在这里不仅国家的权力，而且国家的意志也能活起来。
欧洲各国政府与其人民的幸运与努力已经成就了一件事：把德意志诸国的主权从它此前所处的限制中解放出来，并由此带来了可能性——先向各民族许诺自由的宪法。
然而，比许诺的正面束缚中更高的必然性，还在于那些已成为普遍确信的概念的本性：这些概念把代议制宪法、一种合于法度的状态、以及人民在立法中的参与这一规定系于君主制之上。——弗里德里希二世于是也迈出了这第二步：在内部造就君主国。

en: The promise could be fulfilled in a manner which could be considered the wisest, indeed even the most legal, but which would have been the most perfidious counsel the ministers could have given.

When the princes of the new realms had wanted to deceive their peoples thoroughly and to acquire, so to speak, honour before God and men, they would have given their peoples back the so-called old constitutions; - honour before God and the world - for, according to so many public voices and in particular also according to the history at hand, one might think that the peoples had flocked into the churches and sung loud Te Deums. - For the shade of Machiavelli the princes would have won the glory of the fine policy of the Augusti and the Tiberi, who likewise left standing the forms of the preceding state, then a republic, although this thing was no more and could irrevocably no longer be, - a standing-on and a deception into which their Romans entered and by which the establishment of a rational monarchical state, whose concept the Romans had not yet found, became impossible. - This policy lay so much the nearer to our princes if, out of the experience of the last twenty-five years, they compared the dangers and horrors which are linked to the creation of new constitutions and of a reality starting from thought with, on the other hand, the harmless tranquillity and nullity into which the institutions of the former estates' constitutions had degraded themselves, - if they connected with this nullity already present the further reflection how those institutions, in the quite different situation which had come about, like the Roman institutions which Augustus and Tiberius left standing, entirely lost the little sense and consequence which they seemed still able to have in a German imperial fief.
zh: 那项承诺倒是可以以一种方式兑现——这种方式可以被看作是最明智的，甚至被说成是最合乎法权的；但它也会是部长们所能提出的最背信弃义的谋划。

如果新近诸国的君主们想要彻底欺骗自己的人民，并且想要在上帝与世人面前——也就是在上帝与世界面前——赢得荣誉，那么他们就会把所谓旧的宪法归还给人民；——在上帝与世界面前赢得荣誉——因为按照这么多公开的呼声、尤其是按照摆在眼前的这段历史，人们甚至可能以为人民会涌进教堂、高声唱起感恩颂。——那么，在马基雅维利的幽灵面前，这些君主就会博得奥古斯都与提比略那种精巧政治的声誉：这两人同样保留了先前状态（当时是一个共和国）的形式，尽管这件事早已不再是、并且不可逆转地不再是了；——一种既维持又欺骗的做法，他们的罗马人便走进了其中，而正是它使一个合理的君主制国家的建立——罗马人当时还找不到这个概念——变得不可能。——这一政策之所以离我们的君主们更近，是因为他们若能从过去二十五年的经验出发，把与新宪法的创制、以及与一种从思想出发的现实相联结的危险与恐怖，同前等级议会宪法的制度所降到的那种无害的平静与虚无加以比较，——若他们在这已有的虚无之上进一步又结合了反思：那些制度在已经发生的全然不同的处境中——就像奥古斯都与提比略所留下的那些罗马制度一样——把它们在一个德意志帝国采邑中还似乎保有的那一点见识与彻底性都丧失干净了。

en: King Friedrich has shown himself above the temptation of this deception.

He summoned together the princely and countly heads of families of his realm, a selection from the rest of its nobility, and likewise a number of people's deputies chosen by the citizens for the 15th of March 1815, and the history of these deliberations opens with the ever great scene that the king, in the full assembly of these his imperial estates, first delivered from the throne a speech to them, in which, after he had first set forth what had already been done, namely that the previously so different lands and subjects had been united into an inseparable whole, that the difference of religious confession and of estate had vanished in civil relations, that the public burdens had been put on an equal footing for all and thus all had become citizens of one state, - then had given to his people the testimony of fidelity and obedience, to the army the testimony of courage and of the honour which they had brought to the name of Württemberg, to the state servants the testimony of support in his endeavours, and to the subjects of all classes the testimony of a willing submission to the heavy burdens of the time and to the endeavours of every kind by which security and preservation had been won,
zh: 弗里德里希国王显示出了自己超乎这一欺骗之诱惑的襟怀。

他召集了自己王国的王公与伯爵诸家系的家长、其余贵族中的一部分选任者，以及同样由市民选出的若干人民代表，于 1815 年 3 月 15 日会集；而这些审议的历史以那始终宏大的场景开篇：在其帝国等级议会的全体集会上，国王首先从宝座上向他们发表演说，在演说中，他先是陈述已经完成的事情——即此前彼此如此不同的诸领地与臣民已被联合成一个不可分割的整体，宗教信仰与身份等级在公民关系上的差别已经消失，公共负担对所有人一律平等，因而所有的人都成为一个国家的公民——随后，他向自己的人民给予忠诚与顺服的见证，向军队给予勇敢以及为符腾堡之名所赢得之荣誉的见证，向国家公务人员给予在其努力中予以支持的见证，向一切阶层的臣民给予对时代沉重负担、以及对为赢得安全与维持而作的一切努力的自愿顺从的见证，

en: now declared that he would lay the keystone of the edifice of the state, in that he gave his people a constitution.
zh: 继而宣告，他要为国家的建筑安上最后一块基石——即赐予他的人民一部宪法。

en: After he had [called on] the attending representatives, by whom the nation is summoned, to unite with the head of the state for the exercise of the most important rights of governmental power,
zh: 在要求在场的代表们（民族正是通过他们被召集起来的）与国家元首就政府权力中最重要的权利的行使相结合之后，

en: at the end he made the further appeal: Let us, united, for the promotion of the affairs of the nation, for which the constitution summons this assembly, consolidate the sacred bond between me and my subjects with reciprocal trust,
zh: 在结尾处还发出了这样的呼吁：让我们联合起来，为推进民族的事务——宪法正是为此召集这一会议的——以相互回应的信任把我与我臣民之间那条神圣的纽带加固，

en: he caused the constitutional document to be proclaimed by the Minister of the Interior.
After its reading aloud he bound himself by it and handed it over with his own hands to the president of the assembly.
zh: 他让内政部长颁布了那份宪法文书。
在宣读之后，他自己以它为约束，并亲手把它交给了会议主席。

en: There can surely be no greater spectacle in the world than that a monarch adds to the state power, which is at first entirely in his hands, a further power, and indeed the foundational one, that he takes his people up into it as an essentially participating component.

When otherwise one sees the great work of a state constitution, yes most other actions of government, only in a series of piecemeal actions and chance events without overview and publicity, and the public appearance of princely dignity and majesty had gradually been limited to birthday celebrations or wedding festivals, one may be tempted to linger for a moment on that scene where the appearance of majesty is so answerable to the inner content of its action as a beneficent, elevated and confirming view.
But it would lie just as near to think that one has to excuse oneself for such a moment of lingering.

For the occasions in which we have become accustomed to see the princely representation, the emptiness and inactivity of the former assembly of the estates, of the German imperial diet, in short the nullity and unreality of public life, have made such a weariness of such acts, such a moral and hypochondriac private conceit against the public and against the appearance of majesty into the prevailing mood, so that the mention of it and the view, if any, that such an appearance is capable of awakening generous feelings, would rather have exposed itself to the danger of being taken for anything else than for earnestness, hardly for good-naturedness, but much more to be judged as courtly folly and slavish blindness and affectation.

Our political deadness is incapable of being glad of such scenes, and thoroughness turns away from them as mere outward things to the substance of the matter and to its own thoughts about it; and here too the substance of the matter, the content of the constitutional document which the king has given, is to be briefly indicated.
zh: 世上大概不会再有比这更伟大的世俗场面了：一个君主在起初完全握于自己手中的国家权力之外，又添上了一种进一步的力量——而且是奠基性的力量：他把自己的人民接纳为其中本质上有所参与的一个组成部分。
倘若人们素来看国家宪法这一伟业、乃至政府的大多数其他作为，只是在一连串零碎的举动与偶然的事件中、毫无统观与公开性可言，而君主的威严与至尊的公开显现也逐渐缩减为生日庆典或婚礼——那么人们也许会忍不住在那一幕场景上停留片刻：在那里，威严的显现与其行动的内蕴如此相称，正如在一种仁厚、高迈而令人安心的观照上那样。
但同样容易想到，人们得为这样一个停留的瞬间致歉。

因为我们已习惯于见到君主的公开显现的那些场合——从前的等级会议、德国帝国议会的空虚与无所作为，以及公共生活整体的虚无与不真实——已经对这类行为生出一种腻烦，对公共的东西、对威严的显现生出一种道德的与疑病式的私人自矜，并使之成为弥漫的基调；以致提到它、乃至认为这样的显现有能力唤起慷慨之情的这一看法，与其说会被当作别的一切，倒不如说会冒着被当作轻浮而非认真、被当作宫廷式的愚蠢与奴性的盲目和做作来评判的危险。
我们政治上的死气对为这样的场景而欢欣是麻木的；而深究的头脑则把这类东西作为纯粹的外在之物撇开，转向事情的实质以及自己关于它的想法；在这里同样首先应当简要指出事情的实质——国王所赐予的那份宪法文书的内容。

en: It consists of 66 paragraphs and falls apart into two parts, the first of which has, in 46 §§ the title The Estates' Constitution, the second in 20 §§ the title General Provisions in Relation to the Constitution of the Kingdom and the Rights and Obligations of the King's
Subjects, and thus the one shows itself at once as the more detailed, the other as the less developed.
zh: 它由 66 款组成，分为两部分：第一部分以 46 §§ 为题「等级议会宪法」，第二部分以 20 §§ 为题「关于王国宪法以及国王的
臣民的权利与义务」；因此，前者立即显出为较为详尽的一份，后者则显出为发展得较少的一份。

en: Through the first the king granted an estates' representation with the following principal provisions: it shall consist a) of those who hold a virile vote and b) of elected members, both in one chamber.

The eligibility for election of the latter is bound to no estate; those in royal positions, officials, non-commissioned officers and soldiers, clerics, physicians and surgeons are excluded; the only further condition is an age of 30 years, and further belonging to one of the three Christian confessions of faith; the possession of a certain property has not been included among the conditions. - For the quality of an elector, the clear yield of 200 gulden from landed property and an age of 25 years are required.

The estates assemble only on the king's summons and necessarily every three years, after which time the elected representatives retire by half, but are again eligible and are replaced by new elections.
The assembly lasts not more than six weeks and is dismissed, prorogued or wholly dissolved by the king.
The elected deputies, including the chancellor of the university, the evangelical general superintendent and the Catholic dean, receive their travelling expenses paid and day allowances (at 5 fl.

The ministers may be present at the assembly at any time. - In the years in which the assembly of the estates is not summoned, a committee of twelve members chosen by it for three years assembles for the transaction of urgent business; an increase of the taxes or an alteration of the legislation, however, is not within its competence.
zh: 通过第一部分，国王授予了一种等级代表制，其主要规定如下：它应当 a) 由亲自享有表决权的等级成员与 b) 由选出的成员构成，两者同在一院之内。
后者的被选举资格不系于任何等级；任职于王家职位的人员、非军官与士兵、教士、医生与外科医生均被排除在外；唯一的另一项条件是年满 30 岁，并且属于三个基督教信仰告白之一；拥有一定财产并未被列入条件之内。——要成为选举人，则要求有来自不动产的每年 200 古尔登的纯收益，并且年满 25 岁。
等级议会只在国王的召集下开会，并且必然每三年一次；届时选出的代表半数退席，但仍可再被选出，并由新的选举加以补替。
会议的会期不超过六周，并且可由国王解散、延期或完全撤销。
选出的议员，包括大学校长、福音派总监督与天主教教长，其旅费由公家支付，并发给每日津贴（每人 5 古尔登
30 十字币）。
各部长可以随时列席会议。——在等级会议不予召集的年份，由其选出、任期三年的一个十二人委员会开会，处理紧急事务；但提高赋税或改变立法并不在其权限之内。

en: For the introduction of new taxes, of direct as well as indirect imposts, and for their collection, the consent of the estates is necessary; the existing imposts remain for the government of the then king as bases.
The calculation of the revenues and the use of the imposts is laid before the estates every year.
The determination of a civil list for the king is left to further negotiations.
zh: 开征新税——无论直接税还是间接税——以及征收这些税，都需要等级议会的同意；既有的各项赋税则仍作为当时国王政府的基础。
收入的核算与这些赋税的用途，每年都呈交等级议会。
为国王确定一份王室费用清单一事，留待进一步的谈判。

en: The estates have an equal share in legislation; without their consent no new general law touching personal freedom and property or the constitution can be promulgated.

The initiative in this lies with the king; the estates, however, may bring proposals for laws to the king as wishes, in the case of a refusal repeat them three times in future assemblies and, with regard to the motives, make new representations upon the last answer, which must be motivated.
zh: 等级议会在立法方面拥有同样的份额；没有它们的同意，任何涉及人身自由与财产、或涉及宪法的新的普遍法律都不得颁布。
在这一过程中，主动权属于国王；但等级议会可以把法律提案作为愿望向国王提出，若遭到拒绝，则可在往后的会议中重复三次，并就其理由对最后那必须说明理由的答复再提出新的陈情。

en: It is further granted to the estates to lay general wishes, representations and complaints before the king, - and the king promises to give a decision on every presentation of the estates, and also to accept complaints brought to them by individual subjects, if it is certified that the state authorities have refused to accept them.
zh: 此外，还允许等级议会向国王呈递各种总愿、陈情与申诉；——国王则许诺，对等级议会的一切呈递都作出决断；对于个别臣民向它们提出的申诉，若有证明称国家机关曾拒绝受理，也予以受理。

en: Finally the estates can demand the ordering of an investigation against royal state officials, and on the permission which is never to be refused by the king, in the case of high treason and embezzlement judgement is to be pronounced by an estates' court, in other cases by the ordinary course of law.
zh: 最后，等级议会可以要求对王家国家官员进行调查；在国王从不应拒绝的许可之下，犯有叛国与侵吞之罪时，应由一个等级法院判决，其他情形则循通常的司法途径判决。

en: The infinite importance and liberality of the rights which are here granted to the estates, as well as the simplicity and openness of these provisions, considered impartially simply according to their content without any other regard, certainly do the highest honour to the prince who gave them and to the age in which the law of the state has purified itself from privileges and ripened into principles; and such a work gains still more by comparison with the lack of form, narrowness and unclearness by which in constitutions at home and abroad, notably in the old Württemberg one, the rights of the people are often veiled and stunted in privileges and particularities, restricted and ambiguous, yes often made entirely into an empty show.
Are not the provisions adduced such constitutional foundations as can be acknowledged and accepted only with the highest assent?

What could be lacking cannot be something which would be contrary to them, but only additions and more developed provisions, and indeed only in accordance with those general truths of a state-law condition.
What still derives from the positive law of the state is above all only the privilege of the aristocratic institution.

Moreover, since the rational law of the state has come back from the democratic abstractions which simply reject such an institution, the privilege of this given actuality has in general been put very far away from the former feudal law by further statutes. - Here it deserves in the first place to be pointed out specially that to this element in the royal constitutional document, which is united with the elected deputies into one chamber, only 50 votes were granted, and to the latter 73 votes, and thus a considerable preponderance was conceded.
This relation of political power differs very much from the one which occurs in the system of two chambers and which already has important authority through its more general introduction and its age.

The contrast of that relation of votes against the one adopted in the provisional assembly of the estates of the Kingdom of Hanover, where the knightly estate was allotted one vote more than the burgher estate, may incidentally be mentioned, because the Württemberg estates have several times been provoked in the following deliberations by the liberal expressions of the Hanoverian embassy at the congress in Vienna concerning German constitutional matters.
zh: 在这里给予等级议会的那些权利，其无限的重要性与宽宏，以及这些规定的简明与公开——不偏不倚地单就其内容、不带任何别的考虑来看——无疑使那位赋予它们的君主、以及那个国家法已从特权中净化出来并成熟为原则的时代，赢得最高的荣誉；而这样一部著作在与那种无形、狭隘与含混的对照中还赢得更多：在国内外的宪法——尤其是在老符腾堡的宪法中——民众的权利常常被遮蔽并在特权与特殊化中萎缩，被限制而变得歧义，甚至常常完全被弄成了空洞的假象。
所列出的这些规定，难道不正是那种非得以最高的赞同加以承认与接受不可的宪法基础吗？
可能有所欠缺的东西，不会是与它们相抵触的东西，而只能是附加条款与更为展开的规定，而且只能依照一个法权状态的诸般普遍真理。
凡仍从实定国家法中而来的，无非主要是贵族制度的特权。
此外，合理的国家法既已从那些干脆排斥这种制度的民主抽象中退回来，那么这一既成现实的特权，总的来说就通过进一步的法令被置于远离旧日封建法的地位。——在这里首先只有一点值得特别指出：在王家宪法文书中，这一与选出的议员合于一院的成分只得到 50 票，后者则得到 73 票——于是后者取得了一项可观的多数。
这一政治权力的比例，与两院制下出现的那种比例相去甚远；后者仅凭其更普遍的设立与年代之久，已经具有重要的权威。
这一票数比例与汉诺威王国临时等级会议中所采纳的那一种（即骑士等级比市民等级多得一票）之间的对照，可以顺带一提，因为符腾堡的等级议会在随后的审议中曾多次受到汉诺威驻维也纳使团就德意志宪法事务所作的自由派表态的挑衅。

en: Still more unexpected might seem the further extension and almost complete lack of restraint which has been given to the democratic principle through the manner of electing the representatives, so that this element enters the state order in almost entirely loose form.

The few temperaments which show themselves in this, after the holders of a virile vote have already not been set over against [the elected] in a chamber of their own, are approximately the provisions that the electoral assemblies are presided over by the royal chief officials and in the good towns by the district governors, that the persons called in to conduct the election, such as the official writer and his substitute, are not eligible in the district itself in which they have this function; in other districts, however, they are.
The capacity to be elected as representative is, as indicated above, restricted to very few conditions.
In the first place all state officials and clerics, as well as physicians and surgeons, are excluded.

The consideration which presumably excluded the latter two classes may also have been taken with regard to the former, namely that their official functions do not permit them a longer distance and other occupations.

Quite apart from the fact that this would also be the case with the holders of a virile vote who hold royal offices, in so far as it is presumably not presupposed that they should always have themselves represented by others, and then that with those employed at the place of the assembly of the estates, which will in general be the capital, that ground is diminished, this consideration is certainly not important enough to justify a disposition so highly important for the main thing.

Even in the draft of the outlines of the new estates' constitution, the drafting of which the king himself had occupied himself with (see Supplement of Documents S. 5) and which he had handed to a commission of state councillors and high officials for deliberation in a speech delivered to the assembled council of state on 11. Jan. 1815, the provision occurs (see S. 8) that the royal officials too, in so far as their service relations permit it, shall be eligible for election.
zh: 更加出人意料的也许是：通过代表们的选举方式，民主原则所获得的那种进一步扩张与几乎全然的不受约束；于是这一成分便以一种几乎完全松散的形式进入国家秩序。
在这里所表现出来的少数几点考量——在亲自享有表决权的等级成员已被置于不与选出者分庭抗礼另设一院的地位之后——大致就是这些规定：选举会议由王家专区长官主持，在好城市里则由县长主持；参与选举事务的人，如文书官及其代理人，在其担任此职能的本区内没有被选举权；但在其他区内他们是可以被选举的。
被选为代表的能力，正如上文所述，只受极少数条件的限制。
首先，一切国家公务人员与教士，以及医生与外科医生，均被排除在外。
使后两类被排除的这项考虑，大概也同样适用于前两类：因为他们的职务不容许他们远行与从事别的事务。
且撇开这一点不谈：在任职于王家官署的那些亲自享有表决权的等级成员那里，这种情形同样会成立——因为人们大概并不预设他们每次都须由他人代行；再说，在等级会议的所在地（通常会是首都）任职的人们那里，这项理由就减弱了——这一考虑固然还不足以为一项对主要之事而言如此重要的规定作辩护。
甚至在那份新等级议会宪法要点的草案中——其拟订是国王本人亲自用心的（见《文件补编》S. 5），并已由他在 11. 1 月 1815 年向集会的国务会议所作演说中交给一个由国务顾问与高级官员组成的委员会审议——还出现了这样一项规定（见 S. 8）：王家公务人员，只要其任职关系许可，也具有被选举权。

en: The rapporteur would like to expatiate more widely on this subject, which is of great importance. - Even this circumstance must not be overlooked here, that in great states, such as France for example and still more England, the whole social condition in the interior and the far-reaching connexion outwards places individuals in quite different relations of wealth, culture and habit, of living and behaving in more general interests, than in a land of greater restriction as regards extent, social condition and wealth.

In such smaller countries the greater part of those who acquire a scientific, and in general a more general, education will see themselves induced to seek their economic and social existence in a state service; there will therefore, when state officials have been subtracted, be out of all proportion fewer to be found who bring into an assembly of the estates a considerable insight and experience in general business, - and still fewer who could be called statesmen.

The order of nobility has already been partly removed among the holders of a virile vote, another part of it will find itself in royal services; in general the nobility is not counted on for the places of the deputies to be elected; on the contrary.

The estate of advocates, which among the remaining estates can above all come into consideration, is bound in its concepts and transactions in the first place to the principles of private law and further of positive law, which are opposed to the principles of the law of the state, namely of rational law, of which there can be speaking only with a rational constitution, - so that the sense of a statesman only too famous hit it rightly here, when he declared the advocates to be the most incapable of advising and acting in public business.

How the spirit of the advocates has worked in the history of the Württemberg assembly of the estates will be seen in the sequel. - The legal exclusion of this estate could indeed be contested from the side of abstract right, but no more than the exclusion of physicians and surgeons; a state organisation, however, rests on a quite different concrete wisdom than on a formalism abstracted from private law.
A quite peculiar product of the old Württemberg condition, which is of the first importance for the estates' constitution there, the order of the writers, we shall come to know in the sequel.

The contribution which the order of merchants, manufacturers and other possessors of property can make to an assembly of the estates, important as it is, cannot for this purpose be in so numerous a proportion as, say, in England, and cannot by itself replace what is lost through the exclusion of state officials.
zh: 报告人愿意就这一极为重要的对象作更详尽的阐述。——在这里首先不可忽略的是这一情形：在法国这样的、尤其是英国这样的大国中，内部整个社会状态与向外广延的关联，使个人处在财富、教养与习俗的完全不同关系之中，使他们在更为普遍的利益中生活与举止；而在一个幅员、社会状态与财富都受更大限制的国家里，则并非如此。
在这样较小的国家里，凡取得学术的、总而言之更为普遍之教养的人，其大部分都会发现自己不得不去寻求一种公务职位作为其经济与社会的生存；因此，当国家公务人员被排除在外时，能够带着对公共事务的相当见识与经验进入等级会议的人，就会少得不成比例——而能被称作政治家的人，就更少了。
贵族这一等级已在亲自享有表决权的等级成员中被部分地取走；其中另一部分则将处于王家服务之中；总之，对于待选议员的席位，人们并没有把贵族算在里头；恰恰相反。
在余下的诸等级中唯有律师这一等级能主要地得到考虑；但它首先在其概念与业务上受私法原则、并且还受实定法原则的束缚，而这些原则是与国家法的原则——即那种只有在一份合乎理性的宪法之下才谈得到的理性国家法——相对立的；——因此，一位实在太过著名的政治家在这一点上算是切中要害了：他曾断言，律师是最不善于在公共事务中提供意见并采取行动的人。
律师的精神在符腾堡等级会议的历史中起了什么作用，以后自会见到。——就抽象法权而言，对这一等级成法文上的排除固然可以提出反对，但并不比排除医生与外科医生更有理由；然而，国家组织的依据乃是一种完全不同于从私法中抽象出来的形式主义的具体智慧。
老符腾堡状况中一个十分独特、并且对那里的等级议会宪法具有首要重要性的产物——文书吏这一等级，我们往后会认识到。
商人、工匠与其他财产占有者这一等级能够为等级会议作出的贡献，虽则重要，却在这一用途上不可能像英国那样有如此众多的人数，而且也不能独自补偿因排除国家公务人员而有所损失的东西。

en: However important this exclusion already is, through the reduction of the material from which capable deputies can be taken, so much the more important is it with respect to the element of disposition, which must predominate in an assembly of the estates, if it is not to turn into the most dangerous evil possible in a state.
This fundamental characteristic may in general be called the sense of the state.
It is not done away with by abstract insight, nor by mere rectitude and a good disposition towards the welfare of the whole and the best of the individuals.

Possessors of property, just as much as the individuals who are engaged in trade and industry and are otherwise in possession of property or of a skill, have the interest of preserving the civic order, but the direct aim of theirs in this is the private interest of their possession.

If the deputies of the estates bring with them the sense of private interest and of private law as their first aim, everything else being dependent on it and to be a consequence of it, then they set out to wring from the state as much as possible and to find what is superfluous - though in itself not inappropriate - yet not unconditionally necessary for their purpose, and in general they come with the will to give and to do as little as possible for the general. - It is not a question of what dispositions deputies taken from any station or condition may have; in the institutions of the state, as in every rational arrangement, one cannot reckon on the contingent, but the only question can be as to what the nature of the thing, here of the station, brings with it.
zh: 这一排除本身固然已经因为可供挑选称职议员的材料减少而显得重要，但对于心态这一要素来说就更为重要了——在等级会议中，心态必须占主导地位，否则这一会议就必定败坏成为国家中可能出现的最危险的祸患。
这一根本属性大体上可以称作国家的意识。
抽象的洞见并不能抵消它，单凭正直以及对于整体福祉与个人最大利益之善意的心态，同样并不能抵消它。
财产占有者，以及同样那些从事工商业、或者以别的方式拥有某种财产或某种技能的个人，都怀有维护市民秩序的利益；然而他们在此的直接目的，却是其占有的私利。

倘若等级议会的议员把私利与私法的心意当作自己首要的目的，而其余一切都应当依赖于它并成为它的结果，那么他们就会力图从国家身上尽可能多地榨取，并且把那些虽则本身并非不合目的、就其目的而言却并非绝对必要的东西认定为多余而加以剔除；总之，他们抱着为公共事务尽可能少给、少做的意志前来。——这里的问题并不是：议员从何种地位或何种境况中选出，他们可能抱有哪些心态；在国家的制度安排中，如同在任何合理的安排中一样，不能指望偶然；唯一可以追问的，只是事物的本性——在这里即该地位的本性——会带来什么。

en: The sense of the state, however, is acquired above all in the habitual occupation with the general affairs, in which not only the infinite value which the universal has in itself is felt and recognised, but also the experience of the resistance, the enmity and the dishonesty of private interest, and the struggle with it, in particular with its obstinacy insofar as it has entrenched itself in the legal form, is gone through.
Since the deputies are elected, it is an essential consideration that the electors should proceed above all from such conditions in which this sense must be present and in which it is formed.

The former Minister of the Interior in France, Vaublanc, took into his draft of a law on the manner of election for the chamber of deputies the provision outright that the royal officials of every kind, together with the clergy, should constitute the majority of the electors in the departments.

It is unanimously agreed that the English constitution is preserved by that alone which is called its abuses, namely by the wholly unequal and therefore unjust, yes in part entirely senseless privileges with respect to electoral rights, through which alone it becomes possible for the government in general to count on the majority of the votes. - It is in this connection a view of the uninstructed to regard the opposition party as a party against the government or against the ministry as such; even if the opposition does not merely attack individual ministerial measures - which is also done by the independent members, who in general otherwise vote with the ministry - but if it fights it in every and every particular, its struggle is directed only against this individual ministry, not against the government and against the ministry in general.

What is often reproached to them as something bad, that is, that they want only themselves to get into the ministry, is precisely their greatest justification, quite the opposite of the tendency which one so often sees praised in German estates or individuals as the courage of freedom and the defence of the citizens and of their rights - the tendency to wrest from the state as much property as possible for oneself.
zh: 然而国家的意识主要是在对公共事务的日常处理中获得的；在这种处理中，人们不仅会感受并认识到普遍者自身所具有的无限价值，而且还会经历私人利益的抵触、敌意与不诚实，并与它进行斗争——尤其是与它在法权形式中已经扎根之后那种顽固进行斗争。
既然议员是由选举产生的，那么一项根本的考量就在于：选举人应当主要出自那种必然具备这种意识、并正是在其中形成这种意识的境况。
法国前内政部长沃布朗在其关于众议员选举方式的法案草案中径直列入了这样一项规定：各类王家官员连同各省的神职人员，应当构成选举人的多数。

人们一致认为，英国的宪章恰恰是靠人们称之为其弊病的那种东西才得以保存的，也就是靠选举权方面那些全然不平等因而也不公正、甚至部分地完全荒谬的特权；正是靠这些特权，政府总体上才可能指望多数票。——在这里，把反对派看作一个反对政府或反对内阁本身的党派，是外行人的看法；即便反对派并不只是攻击某一项内阁措施——那些总体上原本与内阁一同投票的独立人士也这样做——即便它在一切方面都攻击内阁，它的斗争也只是针对这个具体的内阁，而不是针对政府，也不是针对内阁整体。
人们常常指责他们一件坏事，即他们只想自己进入内阁；而这恰恰是他们最大的正当理由，完全与那种倾向相反——人们常在德国的等级议会或个人身上把这种倾向赞誉为自由的勇气以及对公民及其权利的捍卫，——即那种要把尽可能多 [的] 财产从国家身上攫取到自己手里的倾向。

en: It must be left to German history to point out in what degree the appearance of the former so-called third estate at the landtags had its origin in the relation of ministerial office, in which the heads of the towns stood as princely officials, and in what degree by the entry into the same afterwards the civic councillors also obtained a share in the estate representation, and likewise how the original officials were at first only deliberating and only in the course of time became decisive in their votes. - In the treaty of Tübingen of 1514, which is regarded as the fundamental law in the constitution of the former Duchy of Württemberg, the princely officials are expressly named together with one from the court and one from the council of a town, who are to constitute the deputies of the territory at the landtags. - But with the imperial commissioners the estates already six years later, in the year 1520, brought it about that the officials were again struck out; the estates give thereby a bad example of the immutability of contracts just solemnly concluded. - It lies very near at hand to object to the eligibility of officials as deputies that they, being in the service of the prince, will naturally also speak and act in his interest, whereby the thought slips in somewhat that what is in the interest of the prince is against the interest of the people and of the state.

In any case the service at the person of the prince, court charges, is something different from the service rendered to the government and the state, and the opinion that what is done in the interest of the government and the state is against the interest of the people distinguishes the mob from the citizens. - The latest events in the world, the struggle for the independence of Germany, have infused into the German youth in the universities a higher interest than the mere direction towards the immediate future acquisition of bread and maintenance; it has also in part bled for the purpose that the German lands should receive free constitutions, and brought with it from the battlefield the hope of a further activity one day and of an efficacy in the political life of the state.

By acquiring its qualification for this through scientific education and devoting itself above all to the service of the state, is the German youth, as well as the whole scientifically educated estate which mostly assigns itself the same destination, to lose precisely through this the capacity to become members of the estates, representatives of the people?
zh: 至于从前的所谓第三等级在等级会议上出现这件事在多大程度上源于官员身份的关系——各城市的首脑作为诸侯的官员而处于这种关系之中——以及市民议员此后因进入这一关系而同样取得等级代表身份的程度，还有那些最初的官员起初只是参与商议、直到后来其表决才变得具有决定性，这些都应当留给德国历史去指出。——在 1514 年的《图宾根条约》中——它被视为旧符腾堡公国宪法中的根本法——明确列出了诸侯的属官，以及来自法院和来自一座城市议会的各一人，他们应当构成该邦在等级会议上的代表。——然而仅仅六年后，即 1520 年，在帝国钦差那里，等级议会就已经促成把这些官员重新排除出去；等级议会由此为刚刚庄严缔结的契约的不可变更性提供了一个糟糕的范例。——对官员作为议员的被选举资格提出异议，是再容易不过的了：既然他们身在君侯的效劳之中，自然也会在君侯的利益上说话和行事；这时差不多会附带地想到：凡是对君侯有利的东西，就是对人民和国家的利益不利的东西。

无论如何，在君侯本人身边的任职、宫廷职务，与为当局与国家效劳，是两种不同的东西；而认为凡是为当局与国家之利益所做的事就是对人民之利益不利的这种看法，正是把民众与公民区分开来的东西。——世界上最近的事件，德意志争取独立的斗争，已在大学里把一种比单纯着眼于直接谋取未来的面包与生计更高的关切灌注给了德意志青年；它也部分地为了德意志各邦获得自由宪法这一目的而流过血，并且从战场上带回了这样一种希望：日后能有进一步的作为，能在国家的政治生活中发挥作用。
德意志青年通过科学的教养而取得这方面的资格，并且主要地献身于国家公务；那么，它以及那个大体上给自己定下同样使命的整个受科学教养的阶层，岂不是正因此就失去了成为等级议会成员、成为人民代表的能力吗？

en: In this connection the important circumstance has still to be taken into account that the change in the relation of the former princely service is a significant moment in the transition of Germany from earlier disorder and barbarism to the rational condition of a state's life. - Something may be said about this circumstance from the appendix to the 25th part of the proceedings; there it is remarked on S. 25 that from the thirteenth and the following centuries the chamber offices were at first mostly entrusted to persons from the knightly estate with a holding of considerable revenues from landed property and the prestations of the subjects, who however found a pretext to give up the exercise of the office, which had become burdensome, and to have it administered by a custodian from the burgher estate with an assignment to a smaller share of the profits.

Later these offices, as well as the offices of guardianship, of the judges and others, were simply transferred to persons from the burgher estate, who however did not, as later on, regard this as a favour but as a heavy burden and had to accept it; this burden was not imposed on anyone for too long either; it was considered a special favour to be spared such offices - of which several examples are given there as well.
zh: 在这里还必须考虑到一个重要情形：旧时诸侯属官身份关系的改变，是德国从早先的无秩序与野蛮过渡到国家生活的合理状态的一个重大环节。——关于这一情形，可以从会议记录第 25 辑的附录中举出一些说法；那里在 S. 25 处提到，自十三世纪及其后诸世纪起，财政官职起初大多只交给那些出身骑士等级、拥有可观的来自土地与臣民负担的实物收益的人；这些人物后来却找到了一个托辞，放弃那已经变得繁重的职务之行使，并让一位出自市民等级的人以一份较少的收益份额代为管理。
后来这些职务——以及监护官职、法官职位和别的职位——干脆转交给出自市民等级的人；不过这些人当时并不像后来那样把它看作一种恩惠，而是看作一项沉重的负担，并且不得不接受它；这份负担也没有在任何人身上被强加太久；能够免于担任这类职务，反而被视为一种特别的恩惠——那里同样举出了若干例子。

en: In the case of these ministerial men, then, at least - even if there is something of a vassalage and even of a serfdom in it - the other circumstances fall away according to which one could believe them to be only for the interest of the prince, against the people, in the sense in which princely servants were later roughly taken for princely servants and for a class excluded from the people.

This latter position they had in so far as the revenues which they had to collect and to account for, as well as the judicial and police power which they exercised in the name of the prince, counted rather as rights of a private possession and of the private power of a third party against the citizens than as revenues of the state and duties of the state.

But as the manorial holdings and the family entails of the princely houses approximated more and more in later times to the character of state property, and the rights of guardianship and other rights over subjects and serfs began to pass over into the more rational character of state duty and state power, so too the princely servants came to rights in their offices and to the dignity of state servants, beyond the dependence of their salaries on the arbitrary will.

This transition from the administration of a private possession to the administration of public rights is one of the most important which were initiated by the course of time, and it has also left the relation of the officials no longer in the determination which obtained under the former Württemberg constitution; - it is one of the changes which were then consolidated and completed with the general transition of a non-sovereign principality into a state. - Since the positive state law, which the assembly of the estates made above all the basis of its claims, has the history as its basis, the general observation may be added here that it is precisely history which teaches us to recognise the circumstances under which a constitutional provision was rational, and it gives here for example the result that if the exclusion of the royal officials from the estates was rational formerly, it is not so any more under other circumstances. - That the assembly of the estates remembered neither the old relation of ministerial office and the express disposition in the treaty of Tübingen nor the difference between former princely servants and state officials is very intelligible.
More striking, however, is the fact that it seems to have been the ministry which caused the exclusion of state officials.
zh: 那么就这些官员而言——即便这里面有着某种封君关系、甚至某种农奴关系——那些使人们得以相信他们只出于君侯的利益而与人民相对立的情境，毕竟是不复存在了；后来的诸侯仆役大致被看作君侯的亲随和被排除在人民之外的一个阶层，正是后一种看法。
他们之所以处在后一种地位，是因为他们所收取和核算的那些收益，以及他们以君侯名义行使的司法权与警察权，与其说是国家的收入与国家的义务，不如说是针对公民的某种私人占有之权利和第三者的私人权力。
然而，正如诸侯各家的领地产业与家族信托在后来时代越来越接近国家财产的性质，而监护权与其他对臣民和隶属者的权利开始转变为国家义务与国家权力那种更为合理的性质一样，诸侯的仆役也超出了其薪俸对任意的依赖，而在自己的职位上取得了权利，并取得了国家公务人员的尊严。

从私人占有的管理转变为公共权利的管理，这是时间所开启的最重要的转变之一；它也使得官员的关系不再保持旧符腾堡宪法之下所具有的那种规定。——这是那些随着一个非主权侯国向国家的普遍过渡而随之得到巩固并完成的变迁之一。——既然等级会议主要作为其要求之基础的正面的国家法，是以历史为基础的，那么这里不妨附上一句普遍的观察：恰恰是历史教给我们认出在何种情势之下一项宪法规定是合理的；而这里它给出的结果是：如果把王家官员排除在等级议会之外在从前是合理的，那么在别的情势之下它就不再合理。——等级会议既不曾记得旧时官员身份的关系，也不曾记得《图宾根条约》中明文的规定，更不记得从前的诸侯亲随与国家公务人员之间的区别，这是完全可以理解的。
然而更引人注目的是：似乎是内阁促成了把国家公务人员排除在外的做法。

en: Another closely related sphere of public business was given by the constitution of the former duchy, namely the court and council of the towns, from whom the deputies to the landtag were to be taken.

Certainly a place in the magistracy is a suitable preparatory school for estate functions; the men of the magistracy live, like the officials, in the daily activity of helping to maintain the civic order, and in the experience of how laws and institutions work, and equally of what counter-effects the evil passions have to be fought against and endured.

The men of the magistracy are furthermore themselves from the burgher estate, they share its more definite interests, as they can share its closer confidence. - It was indeed from one end of Germany to the other that the complaint of incapacity, indolence and indifference - if not also of further corruption and badness of the communal administrations - had become so loud that their institution seemed above all to have needed a rebirth before the men could be trained and could come forth from it who possessed the capacity and the confidence for a larger sphere of action.
The right of the magistracy to fill up the places which become vacant in it by itself was probably the chief circumstance which brought them so low.

What one might otherwise call despotism, namely that many governments took away from the town magistracies and other communal boards the administration of the communal property and of the remaining institutions and foundations belonging to the churches, the schools and the poor, may in that incapacity have found not only its justification but may rather have shown itself to be an unavoidable duty.

The same ground of incapacity is also that which, of the share which the magistrates as courts should have had in the administration of justice, often left nothing more than the bare formality, and brought the business and the decision into the hands of the princely judicial authorities, the district officials, or forced them to take refuge in legal opinions from consiliaries and advocates; the governments too saw themselves induced by this no longer to leave in the hands of the magistrates any share in the administration of justice.
zh: 旧公国的宪法还给出了另一个紧密相关的公共事务领域，即各城市的法院与议会，等级会议的议员应当从中产生。
市政当局的职位固然是等级议会职能的一道合适的预备学校：市政当局的人像官员一样生活在那种帮助维持市民秩序的日常活动之中，生活在法律与制度如何起作用的经验之中，同样也生活在必须去抵挡并忍受那些恶劣情欲之反作用的经验之中。
市政当局的人此外本身就出自市民等级，他们分享这个等级更为明确的利益，正如他们能够分享这个等级更为贴近的信任一样。——然而从德国的一端到另一端，关于无能、懒惰与冷漠——若还不算关于市政管理的进一步败坏与恶劣——的抱怨都变得如此喧响，以至于它们的设置看来首先需要一次重生，然后人们才能在其中被培养出来，并从中走出那些拥有更大作为范围所需的能力与信任的人。
市政当局自行补上其内部空缺职位的权利，大概就是使它们落到如此低的首要原因。
人们通常或许会称之为专制的东西，即许多政府把市政当局以及其他市政管理机构对于市政财产、以及对于属于教会、学校与穷人的其余基金与机构的管理权收走，在那种无能之中也许不仅找到了其正当理由，反而可能显得是一项不可避免的责任。
同样的无能这一根源，也是这样一件事：市政当局作为法院本应在司法活动中占有的那一份，往往只剩下空壳般的形式，把业务与判决交到诸侯司法机关、专区长官手中，或者迫使他们躲进顾问与律师的法权意见里寻求庇护；政府也同样因此被促使，不再把司法活动中的任何一份留在市政当局手中。

en: Now although the municipal magistrates, according to their present organisation and character, cannot indeed arouse great hopes of supplying capable deputies to the landtag, this provision would still have deserved not to be quite forgotten; but enlarging modifications would of course have to do away with what is excessive and one-sided in that restriction.

But the other extreme, which likewise goes too far, we see in the royal constitution, in that firstly the eligibility for election as a deputy is almost as good as unlimited, and then secondly that the conditions for being an elector are likewise insignificant; - besides an age of 25 years, only a sum of 200 fl. in landed property is required for this.
zh: 尽管市政当局按照它们现有的组织与性质确实不能让人对它们能提供称职的等级会议议员寄予很大希望，这项规定本来还是值得不被完全遗忘的；不过，扩大性的修改当然必须纠正那一限制中过火与片面之处。
而另一个同样走得过头的极端，我们则在王家宪法中看到：其一，被选为议员的资格几乎可以说不受限制；其二，成为选举人的条件同样微不足道；——除了年满 25 岁之外，为取得这种资格只要求有来自不动产的 200 古尔登财产。

en: This latter kind of conditions of the capacity to elect has hitherto been foreign to the German institutions, and only in more recent times has this idea come into circulation; we would like to make some observations about it.

What is first of all striking about this is that, according to such dry and abstract determinations as the two cited, the electors otherwise do not appear in any association and relation to the civic order and to the organisation of the whole state.

The citizens appear as isolated atoms and the electoral assemblies as unordered, inorganic aggregates, the people as such dissolved into a heap - a form in which the commonwealth, wherever it acts, should never show itself; it is the most unworthy of it and the most contrary to its notion of a spiritual order.
For age, and likewise property, are qualities which concern only the individual in himself, not properties which constitute his standing in the civic order.

Such standing he has only through an office, a station, a civicly recognised trade skill and authorisation according to it, mastery, title and so forth. - The popular view is so accustomed to such standing that one says of a man only then that he is something, when he has obtained admission through an office, a mastery or otherwise in a definite civic circle; of one, on the contrary, who is only 25 years old and the possessor of a landed property [which] yields him 200 fl. and more yearly, one says that he is nothing.

If a constitution does make him into something, into an elector, then it grants him a high political right, without any connection with the remaining civic existences, and it brings about for one of the most important affairs a condition which is connected more with the democratic, yes even anarchic principle of isolation than with the principle of an organic order.
zh: 后一种这种关于选举能力的条件，直到最近在德国的各项制度中还是陌生的，而这种观念也只是在更近的年代里才流传开来；关于这一点我们想说几句。
首先引人注目的是：按照所引这两条那样干枯而抽象的规定，选举人除此之外在任何联合体中都不出现，也与市民秩序以及国家整体的组织没有任何联系。
公民显现为孤立的原子，选举会议显现为无秩序的、非有机的聚合体，人民整体则溶解为一堆——共同体在任何行动中都不应当以这种形态显现；这是最配不上它的、也最与它作为精神性秩序的概念相抵触的形态。
因为年龄以及财产都只是仅仅关涉个人自身的品质，而不是构成他在市民秩序中有效性的那些属性。
这样的有效性，他只有凭借官职、地位、得到市民社会承认的营业技能及依此而来的资格、师傅资格、头衔等等才能获得。——民众的想法与这种有效性如此熟悉，以至于人们只有在一个人凭借官职、师傅资格或以别的方式在某个特定的市民圈子里获得接纳之后，才说这个人是个「什么」；反之，对于一个只有 25 岁、并且是一处每年向他产出 200 古尔登以上的地产的所有者[的人]，人们则说他什么也不是。
如果一部宪法毕竟把他变成了什么——变成了一个选举人——那么它就赋予他一种高的政治权利，却不给予他与其余一切市民生存的任何联系；并且它就最重要的事务之一造成了一种状态，这种状态与个人孤立化的民主、甚至无政府原则的联系，要比与一种有机秩序的原则更为紧密。

en: The great beginnings of internal legal relations in Germany, by which the formal constitution of the state was prepared, are to be sought in history where, after the old royal governmental power had sunk in the middle ages and the whole had dissolved itself into atoms, the knights, the free men, the monasteries, the lords as well as the merchants and manufacturers now formed themselves against this state of disruption into communities and corporations, which then wore against one another for so long until they found a tolerable existence side by side.

Because the supreme state power was there so very loose, in whose impotence precisely lay the need of those corporations, these partial communities formed their ways of connection all the more firmly, precisely, yes even scrupulously, up to an entirely narrowing formalism and guild spirit, which through its aristocracy became an obstacle and danger to the formation of the state power.

Since in the most recent times the development of the upper state powers has been perfected, those subordinate guild circles and commonalities have been dissolved or have at least been deprived of their political position and their relation to the internal state law.

But it would now indeed be time again, as one has hitherto organised oneself above all in the circles of the higher state authorities, to bring the lower spheres back again into a political order and honour, and to insert them into the state as an organic formation, cleansed of privileges and injustices.
A living connection exists only in an articulated whole whose parts themselves form particular subordinate circles.

But in order to obtain such a thing, the French abstractions of sheer number and quantum of property must finally be abandoned, at least no longer made the principal determination and above all put forward as the only conditions of one of the most important political functions.
Such atomistic principles are, in the political sphere as in science, fatal to all rational concept, articulation and vitality.
zh: 德国内部法权关系的那些重大开端——国家之正式形成正是由此得到准备的——应当在历史中这样一段时期去寻找：在中世纪古老的王家统治权沉没、整体分解为原子之后，骑士、自由民、修道院、领主以及从事商业和手工业的人们，面对这一解体的状态结成了各种社团与行会，而这些社团与行会随后彼此磨蚀了如此之久，直到它们找到了一个尚可的并存状态。
因为那里的最高国家权力是如此松散——那些行会之所需恰恰就在于这种无力——所以这些局部共同体就把它们的联结方式形成得格外牢固、格外精确，甚至格外烦琐，直至形成一种完全收缩的形式主义与行会精神；而这种精神因其贵族性而成为国家权力形成途中的阻碍与危险。
自从在最近的时代里上层国家权力的形成得到完善以来，那些从属的行会圈子与共同体便已被解散，或者至少被剥夺了它们的政治地位以及它们与国家内部法的关系。
但如今大概又到了这样的时候：人们迄今为止主要是按照上级国家机关的圈子来组织自己的，现在也应当把下层领域重新带回一种政治秩序与政治尊严之中，并在剔除特权与不正之后，把它们作为有机的构成插入国家之中。
活生生的联系只存在于一个分节化的整体之中，而这个整体的各个部分本身又构成特殊的、从属的圈子。
然而为了获得这样一个整体，终究必须放弃法国人那种关于单纯人数与财产量数的抽象，至少不能再把它们当作主要的规定，尤其不能把它们当作最重要的政治职能之一的唯一条件。
这样一些原子主义的原则，正如在科学中一样，在政治领域里对一切合理的概念、分节与生命力而言都是致命物。

en: It may be recalled here that the exercise of such a wholly isolated office as that of being an elector easily loses its interest for the individual in a short time, and is in general dependent on accidental disposition and momentary whim.

This office is exhausted with a single act, an act which within several years occurs only once; with the large number of those having a vote, the influence which the individual has through his voice may well be considered very insignificant, all the more so since the deputy whom he helps to elect is himself again only a member of a numerous assembly, in which always only a small number can bring themselves into evidence of a considerable importance, while otherwise through only one voice among many they deliver an equally inconspicuous contribution.

Much as it is therefore psychologically expected that the interest of the citizens should spur them on to seek out their eligibility to vote most eagerly, to hold it important and an honour, and to press towards the exercise of this right and to exercise it really with great circumspection and without any other interest whatever, experience has on the contrary shown that the too great distance between the importance of the effect which is to come out and the influence of the individual, which presents itself as extremely insignificant, soon has the consequence that those entitled to vote become indifferent to this right of theirs; and when the first laws occupy themselves with the exclusion of many citizens from voting, legal dispositions will soon be needed to induce those entitled to come to the poll. - The so often superficially used example of England with its strong agitation at the elections to parliament does not fit here either; for in this part of the English constitution it is precisely the privileges and inequalities of qualification that are the most influential circumstance - in which rather the opposite lies in that atomistic method.
zh: 这里不妨再提一提：像成为选举人这样一项完全孤立的职务的履行，很容易在短时间内就使个人对它失去兴趣；总而言之，它是取决于偶然的心态和一时的随意的。
这项职务靠一次行为即告了结——这是一种在好几年之内只发生一次的行为；在投票者人数众多的情况下，一个人通过自己的选票所具有的影响，很可以被看作微不足道；这就更是如此，因为由他帮助选出的那位议员本身也不过是一个众多集会的成员之一，而在这样的集会中，总是只有少数人能够显出自己具有相当的重要性，此外他们则通过众多选票中的一票，提供一份同样不显眼的贡献。

因此，尽管在心理上人们期待公民的兴趣会驱使他们去急切地寻求投票资格，把它看作重要和一种荣誉，挤着去行使这项权利，并且真正以极大的谨慎、不带任何别的利益去行使它，但经验同时也表明：应当产生出来的作用的重要性，与个人那被自认为极其微小的作用之间的过大距离，很快就会带来这样的后果——即享有投票权的人对这项属于他们的权利变得漠不关心；而当最初的法令忙于把许多公民排除在投票之外时，很快就会需要一些法定的安排，来促使有资格的人前往投票。——那个被如此肤浅地一再援引的英国例子，即议会选举中的强烈活动，在这里也同样不合适；因为在英国宪法的这一部分中，恰恰是资格上的特权与不平等才是最有影响的情势——而那种原子主义的方法所包含的恰恰是它的反面。

en: It is of course self-evident that these remarks against the abstract principles of number, of the quantum of property, and of age cannot be meant to deprive these circumstances of their significance and their influence.

On the contrary, if the qualification for voting at the elections and the eligibility itself are connected with the other institutions of the state, then these circumstances exercise their influence already of themselves; and if this is ordained by law here and, for example, for the capacity to be a member of a municipal magistracy, a court, a board and a member of a corporation, a guild and the like, a certain age, a minimum property and so forth are required, then this stands in far better proportion than when such dry, yet only external conditions are so sharply juxtaposed to the high interest of the estate membership. - The guarantee which is sought through such conditions for the fitness of the electors and the elected is anyhow partly of a negative kind, partly a mere presumption; whereas on the other hand there is a quite different, positive guarantee, through the confidence of the governing power in state services or through the confidence of the communities and the fellow citizens in being elected to communal services, offices, and taken into communities, furthermore through real activity and participation in the organic state and popular life to have acquired the skill and the sense of it, the sense of governing and obeying, and to have had the opportunity that the electors could become acquainted with and test the dispositions and the fitness.
zh: 不过不言自喻的是：这些针对数量、财产量数与年龄之抽象原则的评论，其用意不可能是要剥夺这些情形的意义与影响。

恰恰相反：如果选举时的投票资格以及被选举资格本身同国家的其他各项制度相联系，那么这些情形本来就自行发挥其影响；而如果这一点在这里由法律规定，并且例如对于担任市政当局成员、法院成员、董事会成员以及社团、行会等等的资格规定了某种年龄、基本财产等等，那么这一点远比那种干枯的、却仅仅是外在的条件同等级成员身份所具有的崇高利益被生硬地相对置时更为相称。——人们试图通过这类条件为选举者与被选者的称职所寻求的那种保证，归根结底一部分是否定性的，一部分不过是一种推定；因为此外还有一种完全不同的、积极的保证：通过对执政当局在国家公务上的信任，或通过对各共同体与同胞在受选任于公共事务与官职、被接纳进各个社团这一点上的信任，此外还通过对国家与人民的有机生活的真实参与，从而获得处理它的本领与对它的感觉、对统治与服从的感觉，并且使得选举者得以认识并检验这些人的心态与能力。

en: Determinations of that kind which presuppose the people rather as a heap than as a state, and now divide this heap according to number into particular heaps and according to age and a single determination of property into two classes altogether, can properly not be called institutions of the state.

They do not suffice to take away from the share of the people in the general affairs its democratic unfitness and to withdraw from chance the aim of obtaining capable deputies for an assembly of the estates.

An institution of the state cannot simply remain at the demand that something shall happen, at the hope that it will happen, at the restriction of a few circumstances which might make it harder - it deserves that name only if it is the arrangement that what is to happen shall happen.
zh: 那类规定把人民预设为不是国家而是一堆，并且随即按照人数把这一堆分成为各别的堆，按照年龄和一项单一的财产规定把这一堆总共分成两类——这样的规定其实不能被称为国家的制度。
它们不足以消除人民参与公共事务在民主方式下的不合比例，也不足以把「为一次等级会议取得称职议员」这一目的从偶然的手中夺走。
一项国家制度不能仅仅停留在「应当发生某种事」的要求上，停留在「希望它将会发生」的指望上，停留在对若干可能使之更加困难的条件的限制上——它只有当它就是那种安排——使应当发生的事情确实发生——的时候，才配得上这个名称。

en: Since the reporter has become so prolix on this point, the remarks on the others must be put more briefly. - The estates have the equity granted to them that no new taxes shall be introduced and the existing ones shall not be increased without their consent.

Württemberg would indeed perhaps be the first German land in which general estates came so early into the possession of this right in so open and definite a manner; the estates which we see elsewhere emerge or come to life again contain in part elements very restrictive from the feudal constitution, in part their formation and the determination of their activity still appear in too provisional and obscure a light for them to be compared with the free, frank and clear form into which the monarch of Württemberg wanted to set his own. - The bloody struggle of the Tyroleans against forms of state administration which they believed contrary to their old hereditary rights has aroused general interest; when their former constitution was finally reintroduced, the monarch reserved to himself the determination of the sum of the state burdens and left to the estates only the distribution.

It can now be disputed whether the old Württemberg estates already possessed the right granted to them by the king's constitution or not, and whether they did not formerly possess a much more far-reaching one - a dispute which, without any practical interest, would for that very reason be all the more suited to give vent to a true querelle d'Allemand.

One may well say that the Württemberg estates were formally put back approximately on the standpoint on which the former Württemberg territory found itself, by the provision that the existing taxes are left alone and that only an increase is not to take place without their consent.

For the direct and indirect burdens which flowed into the princely chamber then as now, and which are based on ground-rents, dues, tithes, services of labour and so forth, are lord's dues and in the sense of private law property of the regent or of the state; they take the existing as their basis and are therefore independent of any consent of the estates.

The other part of the proper direct and indirect taxes, the burdens which were levied in the sense of state law, was determined both as to the amount and as to its use for state purposes, namely for the discharging of the debts of the state, for the payment of the district and home militia, by contract under the intervention of the supreme judge and the confirmation of the imperial authority, so that the estates were also in this bound to the existing as to a law.

Now if out of all the clauses and special conditions under which the former estates, except in the case of an increase, exercised the tax consent at all, one were also to draw a general point of view and the assertion that they possessed this right of consent in a comprehensive sense, such a right yet receives an entirely new position and an incomparably greater scope and importance through the new position that the Württemberg land has become from an imperial fief an independent state.
In that condition, war and peace were not made by the individual imperial estate but by the emperor and the empire; the efforts which a war required were in part once for all fixed by a roll.

Not to speak of the fact that the formal self-will of the German estates, which would achieve no more than what could not be repelled right or wrong, had the consequence that the passive efforts became all the greater - an expenditure which fell back on the estates just as unavoidably.
zh: 报告人既已就这一点变得如此详尽，其余各点的评论就必须写得简短些。——等级议会所获致的是这样一种公正：未经它们同意，不得开征新税，也不得提高既有的赋税。

符腾堡大概真的是第一个这样的德意志邦国：它的一般等级议会如此早、并且以如此公开而确定的方式取得了这项权利；我们在别处看到其兴起或复兴的那些等级议会，一部分包含来自封建宪法的极为限制性的成分，一部分则显得它们的形成与其活动范围的规定仍处在过于临时而昏暗的光线之下，以致它们无法与符腾堡君主想要赋予自己的那种自由、直率而清晰的形态相提并论。——蒂罗尔人反对那些他们认为与自己古老的世袭权利相抵触的国家管理形式的血腥斗争，引起了普遍的关注；在他们原有的宪法终于得以恢复的时候，君主把国家负担总额的规定权留给了自己，而只把分摊留给等级议会。
如今人们可以争论：老符腾堡等级议会是否已经拥有国王宪法所授予他们的那项权利，以及他们此前是否不曾拥有过一项远为广泛得多的权利——这场争论没有实际意义，而正因如此，它反而更适于大发一场地道的法国式争讼。
人们大概可以说：符腾堡等级议会由于那项规定——既有各税维持不变，而仅是提高则非经它们同意不得发生——在形式上大致被重新置于从前的符腾堡领地所处的那种立场之上。
因为那些从前和现在一样流入诸侯国库的直接税与间接税——它们以土地地租、永久地租、什一税、劳役等等为基础——属于领地贡赋，并且在私法意义上的确是君主或国家的财产；它们以既有者为基础，因而完全不受等级议会的同意所约束。
而那些真正的直接税与间接税——即以国家法意义征收的各项赋税——则无论在数额上还是在用于国家目的用途上，都通过契约、在最高审判者的干预与帝国机关的确认之下被确定下来，即用于清偿国家债务、用于支付各区与本地的民兵；因此等级议会在这方面同样也被束缚于既有者，如同被束缚于一项法律。
如今，即便人们想从那些条款与特殊约定中——从前的等级议会正是在这些条款与约定之下，除了提高的情形之外，根本无从行使那项税收同意权——再引出一种总的观点以及这样一个主张：即他们曾以全面的意义拥有这项同意权，然而这项权利本身还是由于符腾堡邦国已从一个帝国采邑成为一个独立国家这一新的地位，而获得了一种全新的地位，以及一种无可比拟的更大的范围与重要性。
在那种状况下，战争与和平并不是由个别的帝国等级作出，而是由皇帝与帝国作出；一场战争所需要的努力，有一部分通过一份兵役册一次性地被确定下来。
更不必说，德国各等级那种形式上的自作主张——它所能成就的并不比那些无论合于法还是不合于法都无法抵挡的事情更多——所造成的后果是：被动的努力变得愈发庞大；——而这一份开销同样不可避免地落回到等级议会身上。

en: Against the refusals of the estates, the prince had in the imperial courts a support and an aid in general.

But now that Württemberg has become an independent state, the right of consent to taxation by the estates acquires an equally independent character and with it an entirely new meaning, upon which it is by no means possible to fall back on the previous condition of things.

Here too, then, the state needs entirely new guarantees against private selfishness and against the presumption of the estates, since the former guarantees which the government had from the emperor and the empire no longer exist; it is an entirely new element, the political one, that has arisen, into which the estates have been moved, of which they previously had need. - German special history supplies examples enough that the drive of the former estates in their political nullity went in the direction of passive neutrality, preferred to hold off interference in world affairs entirely from themselves and to let what might happen happen over them with disgrace, rather than to seize upon a self-decision to act and to honour.
With such a drive to honour- and actionlessness towards the outside, there is connected the direction of turning activity not against the outer enemies but rather against the government.

Too often the estates, in critical circumstances, saw nothing else than a favourable opportunity to put the government into a quandary, to prescribe conditions for the endeavours which it demanded for its own and its people’s honour and welfare, and to acquire concessions in rights against it.

Too often they brought it about that in this way they brought misfortune and disgrace upon a land for the present moment, but for the future a restriction and weakening of the strength of government and with it a permanent basis for internal and external disruption.

Out of the political nullity into which the German people had been brought down by its constitution, out of the incapacity of the many small wholes, of the greater part of the imperial estates, to have an own decision and will, there had to emerge a spirit of swampiness into private interest and indifference, yes into enmity against the thought of having a national honour and of making sacrifices for it. - If, for example, in the English nation the feeling of national honour has penetrated the various classes of the people more generally, then the right of parliament to consent to the taxes every year has an entirely different meaning than the same right would have in a people which was brought up in private selfishness and, because it lay outside the political standpoint, was held in the spirit of narrow-mindedness and private selfishness.

Against such a spirit already the governments would need new guarantees for the preservation of the state, since they have lost the one from emperor and empire, which was hardly sufficient in the first place.

The right of participation in the determination of the state burdens, whatever its shape may formerly have been, is now, since the estates have no superior over them other than their state government, which at the same time they stand opposed to, in itself an infinitely higher and more independent competence than before, just as with it they acquire a relation and an influence on war and peace, on foreign politics in general as well as on the inner life of the state.
zh: 面对等级议会的拒绝，君主总归在帝国法院那里有支柱与助力。
然而既然符腾堡已成为一个独立的国家，通过等级议会行使的税收同意权也获得了同样的独立性，从而获得一种全新的意义；对先前的那种状态根本无从援引。

因此国家在这里也需要全新的保证来抵御私心与等级议会的僭越，因为政府先前从皇帝与帝国那里所拥有的那些保证已不复存在；所出现的是一个全新的、政治性的因素，等级议会被移置到了其中，而从前它们是不需要这一因素的。——德国的专门史提供了足够的例证：从前的等级议会因其政治上的虚位，其倾向流于被动的中立，最愿意完全不介入世界事务，宁可让任何可能发生的事情带着耻辱从自己身上过去，也不愿抓住自主的决断去行动、去争取荣誉。
与这种在对外上既无功业也无作为的倾向相连的，正是把活动不是转向外部敌人、而是转向政府的那种取向。
在危急的情势中，等级议会往往只看到一种有利的机会：使政府陷于困境，为政府为它自己及其人民的荣誉与福祉所付出的努力设定条件，并以此从政府那里换取权利上的让步。
他们往往促成这样的结果：以此给一个邦国在当下带来不幸与耻辱，却为将来带来对政府力量的限制与削弱，从而为内在与外在的瓦解留下一份持久的根基。

从德国人民因其宪法而被降低到的那种政治上的虚位中，从许多小的整体、帝国等级中较大的一部分无力拥有自己的决断与意志这一情形中，必然涌现出一种沉沦的精神：沉沦于私利与冷漠，甚至与「拥有一份民族荣誉并为之作出牺牲」这一想法为敌。——例如，如果民族荣誉感在英国民族中更为普遍地渗透了各个民众阶层，那么议会每年批准赋税之权就具有一种全然不同的意义，而这一同样的权利在一个于私心之中被养成、并且因为它处在政治立场之外而被保持在狭隘与私有的自利精神中的民族那里，将是别样的。
单是针对这样的精神，各国政府为了维持国家就需要新的保证，因为它们已经失去了来自皇帝与帝国的那份本来就不够充分的保证。
参与决定国家赋税之权，无论从前是何等模样，如今由于等级议会之上除了他们同时又与之对峙的国家政府之外再无其他尊长，它本身较之从前具有无限地更高、更加独立的权限；他们也因此而在战争与和平上、在整个对外政治上以及在国家内部生活上获得了一种关系与影响。

en: Through the circumstance that the existing burdens have been taken by the royal constitution as the basis for the lifetime of the reigning monarch, the right of taxation was indeed restricted in form; for in substance it is limited in any case by the necessity of need.

This necessity could now indeed be present with respect to the magnitude of the burdens; - in all states the need of the last years - and in the richest, such as England, most of all - has driven the taxes to a height never previously imagined, and France, Austria and others have helped themselves out of these financial predicaments only by arbitrary and forcible operations.

Setting aside now the need, of which nowhere has it been seen that it was not present, setting aside the impossibility of basing a financial constitution all at once on other principles, the Württemberg estates could put up with this article out of gratitude towards the prince, who was the first and, until now, after two and a half years, almost the only one to have given his land such an open and liberal constitution, - a prince against whom, as Count von Waldek said in the first speech, which on the part of the assembly of the estates opened the sittings, right at the beginning (Proceedings
II.

, S. 3) says, that all the estates of the land, all the provinces of the empire vied with one another in feelings of gratitude for his decision to establish a constitution, - a prince to whom Count von Waldek continues to give the praise (likewise in the same place):
zh: 由于既有的各项赋税被王家宪法作为在位君主终身期间的基础，征税之权固然在形式上受到了一种限制；因为就实质而言，它本来就因需要的必然性而受着限制。
就赋税的规模而言，这种需要固然完全可能存在；——在所有国家里，近几年的需要——而且在像英国这样最富的国家里尤其如此——已把税负推到了此前从未想象过的高度；法国、奥地利以及其他国家在这样的财政困境中，也只是靠专断而强制的手段才脱了身。
如今且撇开需要不谈——人们在任何地方都未曾见到它不存在——也撇开「无法一下子把一部财政宪法建立在别的原则之上」不谈，符腾堡的等级议会本可以出于对君主的感激而接受这一条款：这位君主是第一个、并且直到如今、在两年半之后几乎还是唯一一个给了自己的邦国一部如此公开而宽宏的宪法的人；——而对于这样一位君主，正如瓦尔德克伯爵在由等级会议方面揭开会议的那第一篇演说开头所讲的（会议记录汇编
第 2 卷
，S. 3）说道：全国的各个等级、帝国的所有省份都以感激之情竞相赞颂他那建立一部宪章的决定；——对于这位君主，瓦尔德克伯爵继续给予这样的赞语（同样在原处）：

en: "that the same Württemberg has been governed in all the storms of the last decades with rare strength" ("rare qualities", it says in the sequel of the speech (Proceedings
II.

, S. 4), "have always distinguished the rulers of Württemberg"; for this indeterminate word the further historical exposition there gives, for them, except for Duke Christoph, the nearer meaning of princely arbitrariness or weakness of character) -
zh: 「同一个符腾堡在最近几十年的所有风暴中以罕见的强健受到治理」（「罕见的品质」，演说的下文如此说（会议记录汇编
第 2 卷
，S. 4），「历来都使符腾堡的统治者们与众不同」；关于这个不确定的说法，同处在那里就他们（公爵克里斯托夫除外）进一步的历史阐述给出了更切近的含义：君侯的任性或性格的软弱）——

en: the praise, "that the same Württemberg has given a considerable extension" (namely through the so-called mediatization of the German estates which were previously immediately subject to the empire - an extension which Count von Waldek (Vol.

, S. 93) characterises as an unlawful condition, an impairment of the rights of the territorial lords and of their subjects entrusted to them by God, as an extension from which those through whose incorporation it took place could not withdraw only because they had to give way to force) -
zh: 这项赞语，「同一个符腾堡使之有了相当可观的扩张」（即通过所谓对先前直接隶属于帝国的德国各等级的强制归并——这种扩张，瓦尔德克伯爵（会议记录汇编第
6 卷，S. 93）却把它描绘为一种不法状态，是对等级领主及其由上帝托付给他们的臣民之权利的侵害，是一种扩张；而那些因被归并其中而使其扩张得以成立的等级领主之所以不能回避它，只因他们不得不向强力让步）——

en: the praise, "that the same one now loses not a moment to undo the consequences of the circumstances of the year 1806 which are foreign to his will, namely the abolition of the constitution founded for all eternity by his illustrious ancestors".

(The whole course of the deliberations shows that the resistance of the estates concerned the single point that through the royal constitution given, the former one is not restored and that consequence is not annulled.)
zh: 这项赞语，「他现在片刻也不放过，要再度扬弃 1806 年情势中那些不合其意志的后果，即其尊贵祖先为永远而建立的那部宪法的扬弃」。
（全部审议的进程表明，等级议会的抗拒所涉及的唯一点是：通过所给出的王家宪法，先前的那部宪法并未得到恢复，那一项后果也并未被扬弃。）

en: As is well known, the demand of the estates that even in the lifetime of the king their competition should extend to the taxes already existing has had no success, owing to the early death of the king, just as they have also cut off such negotiations because of their non-acceptance of the royal charter, which allowed them new negotiations about the taxes in the event of a change of government.
zh: 众所周知，等级议会要求即便在国王在世期间其竞争也要及于既有的各项税赋，这一要求因为国王的早逝而没有成功；同样，由于他们不接受王家宪章——那部宪章在政府更迭时为他们开辟了关于税收的新谈判——他们也把这样的谈判截断了。

en: To complete the historical account of the main moments of the constitutional document, the second part of it would still have to be adduced, the general provisions in relation to the constitution of the kingdom and the rights and obligations of the king’s subjects.
But these do not suffer either an extract or an appraisal, they are simple organic provisions which speak for themselves and constitute the rational foundation of a state-law condition.
For example § 52.
All subjects are equal before the law; they have access to all state offices; neither birth nor one of the three Christian confessions of faith excludes from this. - § 53.
To the public burdens and taxes all are to contribute proportionately equally according to the laws. - § 55.
Every subject has, if he is exempt from military service or has discharged it, the right of emigration. - § 56.
It is free to every subject to choose his station and trade according to his own free inclination and to train himself for it, and so forth.

These principles allow only the observation that it can never occur to imperial estates to reject them, and only an ugly perversity, obstinacy, or whatever one might wish to call it, could bring such an assembly to the point of not mentioning them and of not doing the honour to the regent who expressly makes them the fundamental determinations of the rights and obligations of his subjects.

However older constitutions may behave towards such principles, these are bound up in them with particular and external circumstances, caught in them, yes often obscured by them; it is not for the sake of the principle, that is, of reasonableness and of an absolute right, that rights appear to be present in them, but they appear as individual acquisitions which are due to particular circumstances and are also restricted to these and those cases, as if they could just as well be lost through unfortunate circumstances.

It is an infinitely important advance of education that it has advanced to the recognition of the simple foundations of the institutions of the state and has known how to grasp these foundations in simple sentences as an elementary catechism.

If the assembly of the estates had arranged that the 20 §§ which contain these general provisions were hung on tablets in the churches, taught to the adult youth, and made a standing article of school and church instruction, one would be less astonished than that the assembly of the land ignored them and did not feel the value of public recognition through the government and of the general knowledge of such principles.
zh: 为了补完对宪法文书主要环节的历史陈述，还应当引述它的第二部分，即关于王国宪法以及国王臣民的权利与义务的一般规定。
但这些规定既经不起摘录，也经不起评断；它们是简单的有机规定，自身已足以言明一切，并构成一个法权状态的合理基础。
一切臣民在法律面前一律平等；他们都有进入一切国家官职的资格；出身以及三种基督教信仰告白中的任何一种都不构成排除。—— § 53.
按照法律，一切人都应当按比例同样地分担公共负担与赋税。—— § 55.
每个臣民，只要免除兵役义务或已服满兵役，便有移居国外的权利。—— § 56.
每个臣民都可以自由地按自己的自由意愿选择自己的地位与行业，并为此而使自己受到训练，等等。
这些原则只容许这样一句评注：帝国等级绝不会想到要摒弃它们；而只有一种乖戾的悖谬、固执——或者人们愿意怎么称呼它就怎么称呼它——才可能使这样一个会议走到那一步：不提及它们，也不给那位统治者以应有的敬意——他明确地把它们作为其臣民权利与义务的根本规定。
无论更古老的宪法对这类原则作何态度，这些原则在它们那里总与特殊的、外在的情势相纠缠，被囚禁于其中，甚至常常被它们遮蔽；在其中之所以显得存在有权利，并不是为了原则的缘故——即不是为了理性与一种绝对权利的缘故——而是这些权利显得像是若干单独的既得权益，它们归功于特殊的情势，因而也仅限于这一种那一种情形，仿佛它们也可能因不幸的情势而同样失去。
教养在此取得了一项无限重要的进步：它推进到了对国家制度之简单基础的认识，并且懂得把这些基础把握成简单的语句，成为一部入门的基本教理问答。
如果等级会议曾经促成这样一件事：把包含这些一般规定的那 20 §§ 制成牌子悬挂在教堂里，教给成年青年，并使之成为学校与教会教育中的一项固定内容——那么人们对另一件事的惊讶就会少得多：即地方议会竟然对它们置之不理，竟没有感受到通过政府而得到公开承认、以及对这类原则的普遍知晓所具有的价值。

en: But for the sake of this generality they only make a ground-plan for a legislation which is still to be drawn up, like the Mosaic commandments or the famous Droits de l’homme et du citoyen of modern times.

For an existing legislation and a government and administration already in existence, they are the lasting regulators upon which a revision as well as an extension of what already exists must be founded, if the one or the other is necessary.

The royal constitutional document stops at these general foundations and does not contain the further development of them, nor the reception of nearer provisions which could already have existed as institutions of the state.

Organic constitutional provisions and proper laws border on one another in general very closely, and the further labour of the development and subsumption of the already existing institutions could above all have furnished an object of the activity of the assembly of the estates.
zh: 但为了这种普遍性，它们只构成一部尚待拟定的立法的大纲，就像摩西的诫命，或近代那份著名的《人权与公民权宣言》（Droits de l’homme et du citoyen）一样。
对于一部既有的立法以及已经存在的政府与行政机构，它们是持久的调节物；如果修订与扩展已存在之物二者之一是必要的，那么对这一方或那一方的修订或扩展就必须建立在它们之上。
王家宪法文书停留于这些一般的基础之上，既不包含对它们的进一步展开，也不包含对那些更具体的规定的接纳——而那些规定本来就已经可以作为国家制度而存在。
有机的宪法规定与真正的法律总体上彼此紧邻；而对既有的各项制度加以展开与归摄的进一步工作，主要本可以成为等级会议活动的一项对象。

en: These are now the main moments of the manner in which the king meant to have supplemented the previous state constitution of his realm with the important limb of a representation of the people and with the acknowledgement and proclamation of the general principles of justice in the life of the state: the incorporation of that limb and with it the establishment of the basis for the further development and application of the principles of right through the actual summoning of the estates, carried out according to the stipulation of the constitutional document, through his own public binding himself to the document, its solemn handing over to his estates and its publication, as the instruction which conferred their legitimacy upon them, he believed to have effected and completed.

One now expected perhaps that the further course of history would show how this new creation, the estates, moved within the circle allotted to them and how this important element of life, added to the organism of the state, had operated within it.

But it is not the history of such an assimilating and life-giving activity that unfolds before our eyes, but rather that the members called to it refuse to let themselves be taken into the state as this limb; they nevertheless declare themselves to be estates, but of another world, of a past age, and demand that the present be transformed into the past, reality into unreality.
zh: 这就是国王自以为能够以人民代表制这一重要环节、并以对国家生活中正义之一般原则的承认与宣告，来补充其王国既有的国家宪法的方式与主要环节；而对那一环节的归并，从而也即通过按照宪法文书的规定所实际进行的等级议会召集、通过他本人公开地以该文书为约束、通过该文书向他的等级议会的隆重交付与公布——作为赋予他们正当性的训令——以便为法权原则的进一步展开与适用建立起基础，他都自以为已经完成。
人们那时大约期待：历史的进一步进程将会展示，这一新的造物——等级议会——如何在为它们所划定的范围内活动，以及这一被添入国家有机体之中的重要生命要素如何在其中发挥作用。
但在我们眼前展开的，并不是这样一种同化而又赋予生命的效力之历史；而是：那些被召来担任此职的成员，拒绝让自己作为这一环节被接纳进国家；他们却仍然自称为等级议会——但却是另一个世界、一个已经过去时代的等级议会——并要求让现在变成过去，让现实变成非现实。
