en: In the same sitting, on 15 March, in which the king believed to have constituted his realm inwardly at last, the beginning takes place that partly the formerly privileged classes, partly those summoned in order to be the estates, jointly declared that they find themselves outside the new legal constitution of the state and that they will not enter into the constitution given by the king at all.
zh: 就在同一场会议——3 月 15 日——之中，国王自以为终于在内部完成了对其王国的组建；而就在这时，开端出现了：一部分是从前享有特权的阶层，一部分是被召集来充当等级议会的人，他们共同声明：自己处在国家新的法权状态之外，并且根本不愿进入国王所给出的那部宪法。

en: In the first place the agnates of the royal house (Vol. I, S. 26 ff.) declare that they expressly reserve to themselves and to all future agnates, heirs and heirs’ heirs of the royal house the rights of the former condition. - Then a number of territorial lords declare that they expect from the congress of the monarchs at Vienna the determination of their rights and relations and that they therefore cannot beforehand submit themselves to a particular estates’ constitution; they accordingly declared themselves released from participation in the deliberations. - In general, the declaration was inserted into the first address of the estates (though it is not easy to see from what authorisation) that the remaining princes and counts and the whole nobility too can only enter into it with a reservation of their rights and of the pronouncement of the congress. - These reserved rights are given a remarkably wide meaning in particular in a complaint addressed to the estates by Count von Waldek in the name of the high-lye and Limpurg house (Vol.
VI, S. 91 ff.) a remarkably wide meaning.

It is said there S. 93 that this high-lye house never accepted the abdication of the Roman emperor (an abdication which otherwise was accepted by all the potentates of Europe) and (S. 97) that after the dissolution of the Rhine Confederation it had entered into the legal possession of all its former legal jurisdictions, and that only the actual possession of them is still unlawfully lacking to this day; - that is to say in other words, it is hereby formally released from the legal incorporation into the Württemberg state and from the relation of subjection to it, and it is even added that the count is ready, when a constitutional condition has once come about in Württemberg, to state those terms under which the county of Limpurg would be prepared to enter by a contract into a relation of subjection towards Württemberg.
zh: 首先，王室的同宗男系继承人（会议记录汇编第 1 卷，S. 26 及以下）声明：他们以及王室未来的全部同宗男系继承人、继承人与继承人的继承人，都明确保留旧日状态下的权利。——其次，若干等级领主声明：他们期待维也纳各国君主大会对其权利与关系作出规定，因而不能预先服从一部特殊的等级议会宪法；于是他们宣布退出对各项审议的参与。——总之，等级议会的第一份陈情书中被插入了这样一项声明（尽管看不出这是依据何种授权）：其余的诸公爵与伯爵以及全体贵族，也只有保留其权利并保留大会裁决的条件下，才肯参与其中。——尤其是瓦尔德克伯爵以林普堡侯爵家族的名义向等级议会递交的一份申诉书，对这些被保留的权利赋予了一种引人注目的宽泛意义（会议记录汇编第
6 卷，S. 91 及以下）赋予了一种引人注目的宽泛意义。

那里在 S. 93 处说：这个侯爵家族从未接受罗马皇帝的退位（这一退位为欧洲一切君主所接受），并且（S. 97）在莱茵邦联解散之后已进入其以往一切法权管辖权的合法占有之中，而直到此刻只是缺少对这些管辖权的实际占有；——换句话说，这就是说，它在此正式宣告脱离被合法归并进符腾堡国家以及臣属于它的关系；甚至还补充道：伯爵已准备好，一旦符腾堡出现一个宪章状态，他就要说明那样一些条件——林普堡伯国愿在这些条件之下通过一份契约而与符腾堡结成一种臣属关系。

en: That the royal ministry was able to regard such things as even ridiculous - assumptions of territorial lords reaching to the point of not recognising the abdication of the Roman emperor - does not belong here; but in an assembly of the estates it can seem incomprehensible to grant participation and voting in their deliberations and decisions to such members as formally declare that they legally do not yet belong to the Kingdom of Württemberg at all, that they are indeed willing to take part in passing decisions binding for the Württemberg people, but that these decisions are not yet binding for such helpers, but only once a constitutional condition has come about with their help they will declare what conditions they please to attach themselves to. - Even if the phenomenon of the presumption of making laws for others while declaring oneself not subject to the same should otherwise lie nearer to hand, it will on the contrary be harder to find examples among estates of such a degree of laxity as to put up with such things and to grant a share in the deliberations and decisions on such a condition, equally arbitrary, made against the king.
zh: 王家内阁竟能把这类事情——直至拒不承认罗马皇帝退位的那种僭越——看作可笑之事，这不属于本题；但在一个等级会议中，把商议与决议中的参与权和表决权授予这样的成员，看来是难以理解的：他们正式声明自己在法权上根本还不属于符腾堡王国；他们固然愿意参与作出对符腾堡人民有约束力的决议，但这些决议对这样的「帮手」尚无约束力，而只有当一个宪制状态借助他们的帮助达成之后，他们才会声明自己愿意以哪些条件参与其中。——如果说「为他人立法却宣布自己不受其约束」这一僭越现象通常就更加近在手边，那么反过来，在等级议会中要找到这样的松散程度的例子就更难：它们竟然忍受这类事情，并且竟然在这样一项同样是针对国王而擅自提出的条件之下，允许对方参与商议与决议。

en: One more estate, namely the prelates, made after a few days the insignificant step of presenting in an address - yet only as a wish - that they should be represented as a separate estate in the assembly of the estates,127) and that the former rights should be granted to them. - Of the two prelates who were already members of the assembly of the estates, the one who was called as chancellor of the university of Tübingen declared that he did not know whether he represented the university or the church or the estate of scholars; the other, who was called as evangelical general superintendent, made the naive utterance that a good friend had advised him not to sign the petition of the other prelates, in order to appear impartial and to be able to support their cause all the more (Vol.
II, S. 64 ff.).
zh: 还有一个等级——即教士们——在几天之后迈出了微不足道的一步：在一份陈情书中提出——不过只是作为一个愿望——他们希望作为一个特殊等级在等级会议中得到代表127)，并且希望旧日的权利能够重新让予他们。——在这两位已经是等级会议成员的教士中，一位受聘为图宾根大学校长者声明：他不知道自己代表的是大学、教会还是学者等级；另一位受聘为福音派总监督者则作出天真的表述：一位好友劝他不要在另一位教士的请愿书上签字，以便显得公正，从而能更好地支持他们的事情（会议记录汇编第
2 卷，S. 64 及以下）。

en: The entire assembly of the estates itself likewise takes up a standpoint opposed to the actual circumstances of the world.

It rejects the constitution given by the king and with it the instruction by virtue of which it is convened, assumes a calling of its own and resolves upon the non-acceptance of that constitution in a sense which contradicted the general constitution of Europe and Germany just newly founded by all the European powers. - The assembly of the estates did not reject the royal constitution on the ground that it was contrary to the right which subjects can claim for themselves in the state constitution out of the eternal right of reason.

What one would have had to expect to precede its rejection, an examination of that document, it did not enter into at all and would indeed have had to acknowledge the general principles of it, but it rejected it for the reason that it was not the old Württemberg constitution, - and not merely in so far as it was different from this, for even this examination it did not send in advance, but dryly and expressly, because it was not in name that old constitution, because the act by which it was to enter was not the mere restoration and revival of the old. - But the dead cannot come alive again; the assembly of the estates proved in its demand that it had not only no concept of the nature of the task which was to be solved, but not even an inkling of it.

It showed that it regarded the necessary in the task as the whim and private arbitrariness of the king or of his ministry and believed that this was to be done with a contingency, not with the nature of the thing.
It did indeed allow that some circumstances were new and that in view of them modifications would have to be made.

For these new circumstances only a few outward things counted for it, which do not touch the essence in the difference of the old and the new relation at all, - namely the accession of an estate of nobility which, as was remarked above, wanted to be considered that it legally - thus in relation to the constitution, where alone the legal condition was in question - does not properly constitute a part of the subjects at all, nay which rejected the determination of a position in the state and in private law within the empire from the state with competition of the assembly of the estates.

The other circumstance was the admission of the subjects belonging to another Christian confession to the same rights of state citizenship as the Lutherans, a circumstance which in any case does not touch the nature of the constitution, any more than the former was yet to be an object of it.
As a further occasion for modifications the enlargement of the land by more than half in comparison with its previous extent was regarded.

In truth this circumstance could furnish a very important ground against the dry introduction of the former constitution of Old Württemberg, whereas the assembly of the estates sought with grounds of advocacy from former cases, the old positive state law, the formal concept of incorporation, to prove that the newly added part has a right to the benefit of the constitution of the other part.

But in the last resort, for the main thing, the whole consideration of this regard and quite particularly the proofs of advocacy were something very idle, almost a querelle d’Allemand; for even if Württemberg had received no extension whatever and had remained entirely in its previous territory, in which the old constitution had its being, the change of position for it, the need and the necessity of a new constitution, would have remained the same.
zh: 整个等级会议本身同样把自己置于一种与真实的世界情势相对立的立场上。
它拒斥国王所给出的宪法，从而也拒斥据以召集起来的训令；它自赋一种自己的使命，并以一种与刚刚由欧洲各列强重新确立的欧洲与德意志之一般宪法相抵触的意味，决意不接受那部宪法。——等级会议拒斥王家宪法，并非因为它与臣民们能够依据理性的永恒法权在国家宪法中为自己主张的那种权利相抵触。

人们本来必须预料到在它拒斥之前会有对那份文书的一项审查——那项审查它根本不去进行，而且它本应承认其中的一般原则——但它之所以拒斥那份文书，恰恰是因为它不是老符腾堡的宪法；——甚至不仅仅是因为它与后者有所不同：它连这样一项审查也没有预先提出，而是干巴巴地、直截了当地说，因为它并不是就名分而言那部旧宪法，因为那个据以进入的举动并不是单纯的旧物之恢复与复活。——然而死者不能复活；等级会议在它的要求中表明：它对那项有待解决的任务的本性，不仅毫无概念，而且连一点头绪也没有。
它表明：它把这项任务中必要的东西看作是国王或他的内阁的一时兴致与私意，并且相信这是出于偶然，而不是出于事情的本性才这样去做的。
它固然承认：某些情势是新的，并且就这些情势而言本应作出某些修改。
对于这些新情势，在它看来只关乎几样外在的东西，它们根本触及不了新旧关系之差别中的本质；——即新增了一个贵族等级；如上文所指出的，这个等级自以为自己从法权上说——因而就宪法而言（那里所谈的只是法权状态）——其实根本还不算臣民的一部分，甚至它还排斥了在帝国中取得一种国家法权地位与私法权地位的规定，而这种规定要由国家与等级会议相互竞争来给出。
另一个情势是：属于另一种基督教信仰告白的臣民被纳入与路德宗信徒相同的国家公民权之中；这一情势本身就并不触及宪法的本性，正如前一个情势原本也还不会是宪法的对象一样。
作为促成修改的又一个理由，人们认为该邦国的疆域较其原有范围扩大了一半以上。
事实上，这一情势本可以为反对干巴巴地恢复老符腾堡旧宪法提供一个非常重要的理由；与此相对，等级会议却试图以从前诸案中的律师式论证、以旧日的实定国家法、以归并的形式概念来证明：新加入的那一部分对另一部分所享有的宪法的恩惠享有权利。
但从根本上说，就主要之事而言，对这一顾虑的整个考虑、以及尤其是那些律师式的证明，都是极其无聊的东西，几乎就是一场法国式争讼；因为即使符腾堡根本没有得到任何扩张、仍旧完全留在它从前那块旧宪法所施行的疆域之内，一部新宪法的迫切需要与必然性对它来说也仍然是同一个。

en: For a closer elucidation of this necessity, the disadvantageous consequences could now be developed in a great many directions, which the reintroduction of the old Württemberg constitution would have had under circumstances entirely different from and more than merely those just mentioned.

The education of the time already demanded at least a compilation and sifting of those constructions and charters which have run out into an unformed edifice just like the German imperial constitution.
One needs only to look at the meritorious collection made by our Mr.

Church Councillor Paulus out of the principal documents of the Württemberg territorial fundamental constitution, in order to see that such a condition of the constitutional foundations is an inexhaustible armoury for advocates and legal advisers for their deductions, but at the same time a formulation by which the knowledge of the constitution and with it more or less the thing itself is taken away from the people, a formulation with which the age can no longer be content.

That something has come about in view of this formality and that a business which only appears to concern the form must also have had an influence on the matter will be spoken of further below. - But as regards the disadvantageous consequences, the so-called beneficial consequences can be set against them, and above all the right which is not to be made dependent on consequences; in view of the latter in particular this has also been done by the estates to satisfaction and to satiety.
zh: 为了更切近地阐明这一必要性，人们本可以从许多方面展开这样一些不利的后果：在与方才所提及的那些情势完全有别、且远不止于此的情势之下，恢复老符腾堡的宪法会带来这些后果。
时代的教养至少已经要求：把那些像德意志帝国宪法一样流为一座不成形建筑物的各种设计与宪章加以汇总与甄别。
人们只需要看看那部有功的收藏，它是由我们的阁下枢密
……教会顾问保卢斯先生从符腾堡邦国根本宪法的主要文书中编纂出来的，以便看到：宪法基础处在这样一种状态之中，对律师与顾问来说是一架用于推演的取之不尽的武器库；但它同时又是一种表述——凭借这种表述，宪法知识、从而或多或少连同事情本身被从人民那里夺走了；而时代已不能再满足于这样的表述。
在这种形式化的情况下究竟产生了一些什么，以及一件看似只关乎形式的事务也必定对物质发生过影响，下文还会再谈。——至于那些不利的后果，则可以摆出所谓的「有利的后果」来与之相对抗，尤其是摆出那种不应取决于后果的权利；就后者而言，等级议会也早已做得够多、做得令人厌倦了。

en: From such a discussion there arises the ordinary endless talking back and forth, because such reasons and counter-reasons have in themselves no final decision, when the praetor is missing who would have to give that decision.
What is at stake is solely the nature of the thing, and this in the present case is very simple.

The change which has been preparing itself for centuries and has only now been completed late enough is the already-mentioned transition of the more considerable German lands from the relation of imperial fiefs into the relation of sovereign lands, that is, of states.

In those, on the one hand the prince, on the other hand land and people - though the latter as subjects (often even to the degree of serfdom) - could stand opposed to one another with an independence which on both sides could come close to rights of sovereignty.

For between the two stood the emperor and the empire as an external bond, which held both in this independence and also held them together in a makeshift way, - just as one private person is an independent person in relation to another private person.

In the relations which they form with one another, they start from subjective need and arbitrariness; but only because they are at the same time in a state, have an authority and courts above them, do relations become contracts, does it have any complete real sense to conclude contracts, and are individuals maintained in their independence and in their relations.

But the more powerless that intermediate and supreme authority proved itself, the worse both sides had to fare in their collisions with one another, because, being at once independent and yet bound to each other as government and subjects, they could not come apart.
zh: 这样一番来回辩驳所产生的，就是那种通常的无休无止的你来我往：因为当那个本应作出终局裁断的裁判官不在场时，这等理由与反驳理由本身并不包含任何最终的裁断。
唯一要紧的只是事情的本性，而在当前这个个案中，这一本性非常简单。
这场自数世纪以来一直在准备、直到如此之晚才得以完成的变革，就是前面已经说过的：那些较为重大的德意志邦国从帝国采邑的关系转入主权邦国的关系，亦即转入国家的关系。
在那种关系中，一方面是君主，另一方面是土地与人民——尽管后者作为臣民（往往甚至达到农奴的程度）——双方可以以一种独立的姿态相对而立，而这种独立从两方面看都几乎可以接近主权之权。
因为横亘在两者之间的，是皇帝与帝国作为一条外在的纽带，它维系着双方的这种独立性，也勉强地维系着二者的联结，——正如私人在对私人而言是一个独立的人格那样。
在彼此结成的诸种关系中，他们是从主观的需要与任意出发的；但只是因为他们同时处于一个国家之中、其上有政权与法院，那些关系才成为契约，订立契约才具有完全而真实的意义，个人也才在其独立性与诸种关系中得以维持。
然而，那一中介与最高的权力越是显得无力，双方在彼此的冲突中就越是糟糕；因为他们虽然独立，却又作为政府与臣民彼此束缚在一起，无法分开。

en: Such a condition, in which prince and people were bound together by such an external power, brought it about that the actual rights of the state lay on the side of the subjects.

Rights of this kind include most of those which flowed from the feudal relation; yet it would be superfluous to touch upon such here, because in Old Württemberg there was only a insignificant nobility, whose rights were in any case of no great consequence for the state relation.
But the right of the former Württemberg estates to have the treasury in their hands deserves essential mention.

With it was connected for them the right not only to enjoy diets themselves, but also to appoint officials, legal advisers and above all a committee, and to assign salaries from the treasury to its members as well as to those officials.

Yes, this committee itself had the administration of the treasury, out of which it drew its salary determined as a whole by the estates; but further its administrative right extended so far that it even decreed for itself supplementary salaries and remunerations, and further decreed and paid to its members as well as to other individuals rewards and pensions for real or imagined services; yes precisely this use of the country’s money for the personal, for itself, which will most of all despise to keep secret, was withdrawn from all control.
zh: 这样一个状态——君主与人民被一条如此外在的权力联结在一起——带来的后果就是：真正的国家之权落在臣民这一边。
这一类权利中包括那些从采邑关系中流出的大多数；不过在这里逐一涉及它们则是多余的，因为在老符腾堡只存在一个无足轻重的贵族，其权利对国家关系总体上并无重大后果。
但有一项权利值得着重提及：从前符腾堡等级议会掌握国库之权。
与此相联的，是它们的权利：不仅自己享有津贴，而且可以任命官员与顾问，尤其可以任命一个委员会，并从国库中为该委员会的成员以及那些官员拨付薪俸。
不仅如此，这个委员会本身就掌管着那座国库，它从中领取由等级议会整体规定的薪俸；而且它的管理权还伸展到如此地步：以至于它甚至给自己批下加薪与酬金，还为它的成员以及其他个人就实际的或想象出来的效劳批下并发放奖金与养老金；正是这种把邦国钱财用于个人、用于自身的做法——一种最不屑于加以隐瞒的荣誉——完全逃脱了任何监督。

en: To the inner disruption and moral swampiness which lies in such a private plunder and in such a condition as such, the formal disruption of the state is closely related: that the estates, through the treasury which they have in their hands, set themselves up for their purposes as a kind of sovereign power and enter into connection with foreign powers.

From one’s own treasury it is no great step to the maintenance of one’s own troops, and it would be only ridiculous to prohibit the latter by law for the estates, while by the former one puts the power and the means for it into their hands.

If the aforementioned intermediate and supreme power of the emperor and the empire was still in existence, such a consequence could be prevented in individual cases, - namely where that power was effective, as well as in the case where it pleased it; but it remained a matter of chance whether this consequence was prevented or not.

Yet in the German empire too there was no lack of cases in which estates were entitled to maintain their own troops, as for example the town of Emden in East Frisia, no less than the fact that in this very land, which lay more remote from the influence of the empire, the estates themselves recruited troops against their prince, concluded treaties with foreign powers and called their armies into the country and paid them.

In this respect there is hardly a more instructive history than the excellent history of East Frisia written by Wiarda;128) we see in it a connected picture of the most shameful, most revolting and most destructive disruption which arose from the relation between prince and estates, in whose hands lay rights which belong to sovereignty.

In larger outlines such things are to be found, for example, in the history of France and England before these countries had completed their formation into states, not to mention Poland, only that these histories are also more free of the disgusting side, namely the complete legal and paper formalism of the German land.
zh: 在这样一种私人劫掠、这样一个状态之中所包含的内在瓦解与伦理上的沉沦，与国家在形式上的瓦解极为相近：等级议会凭借它们掌握在手的国库，为自己的目的把自己弄成一种主权的力量，并与外国势力建立联系。
从自己掌握国库到自己养一支军队，并不算大的一步；而只以法律禁止等级议会养兵，却通过前一样东西把实现这一点的力量与手段交到它们手里，那才只是可笑。
如果前面提到的皇帝与帝国的中介与最高权力尚还存在，那么这样一个后果在个别情形中是可以被阻止的——即在那一权力有效运作之处，以及在它恰好愿意那样做的时候；但这一后果究竟被阻止还是没有被阻止，始终听凭偶然。
然而在德意志帝国之中也不缺少这样的事例：等级有权维持自己的军队，例如东弗里斯兰的埃姆登城；同样也不缺少这样的事实：在这个离帝国影响更为遥远的邦国里，等级议会自己招募军队来对抗自己的君主，与外国势力缔结条约，把它们的军队召进国内并为之支饷。
就这一点而言，几乎没有比维阿达所写的这部出色的《东弗里斯兰史》更有教益的历史了128)；我们在其中看到一幅连绵的图景，描绘出由君主与等级议会之间的关系所生出的那种最可耻、最令人厌恶也最具破坏性的瓦解——那些权利正掌握在等级议会手中，而这些权利本应属于主权。
在较大的轮廓上，这类事情在法国与英国的历史中同样可以找到——在这些国家完成其成为国家的塑造之前——更不必说波兰了；只不过这些历史在更大程度上摆脱了那可憎的一面，即德意志邦国那种十足的法权与文书的形式主义。

en: The archives of the East Frisian estates, in whose service he himself stood and by whose commission he wrote his work, were opened to the said historian.
The Württemberg estates did not bring about such a history; the famous Moser,129) who was capable of it and who was also their legal adviser, they drove out from their midst.

Yet among other particulars which are available to the public, a brochure stands out which, in one aspect of the subject touched upon, at least gives a glimpse into the independent estates’ administration of the treasury during a certain period, and which has appeared under the title: The Administration of the Württemberg Provincial Treasury by the Former, Now Discharged Committees of the Württemberg Estates; Drawn from Territorial Accounts, Acts and Documents (without place of publication) 1799.

The assembly of the land, which was summoned together again once after about 25 years in the year 1796, examined the accounts of the committees which it found; the said brochure provides at least a part of the results of this examination.

The preface says about it summarily: "The results of these accounts contain not only some tons of gold which have been used contrary to law, but they run into millions and amount, from the last landtag of 1771 to the beginning of the present one, in March 1797, where an end was made of the abuse, to the enormous sum of 4 238 000 fl., that is: four million two hundred and thirty-eight thousand gulden of state property, for the faithful administration and use of which the committees were on oath and responsible."
zh: 那位史家获准查阅东弗里斯兰等级议会的档案——他本人就在它们的服务之中，并且正是受它们的委托写成此书。
符腾堡等级议会并没有促成这样一部历史；那位有能力写成此书、并且也是它们的顾问的著名莫泽129)，被它们从自己人中间赶了出去。
不过，在其他一些公开可得的细节之中，有一本小册子格外引人注目：它至少让人瞥见了所论问题的一个方面——某一时期等级议会独立的国库管理，并且它是以这样的标题出版的：《符腾堡邦国金库由符腾堡等级议会先前那些如今已被撤销的委员会管理；从邦国的账簿、卷宗与文书中摘出》（无出版地）1799 年。
那场在 1796 年、约二十五年来第一次重新召集起来的等级会议，审查了它所发现的那些委员会的账目；上述小册子至少提供了这次审查结果的一部分。
序言对此概括地说：「这些账目的结果所包含的，不只是若干吨被违法使用的黄金，而是以百万计的数目：从上一次等级会议（1771 年）直到当前这一场开始之时，即 1797 年 3 月祸害被终止之时，其总数为 4 238 000 古尔登——请听我说：四百二十三万八千古尔登的国家财产；而这些委员会曾就其忠实的管理与使用宣誓并负有责任。」

en: This result may be sufficient to mention; to draw out of it a detailed picture of how deep the independence has made this estates’ administration sink does not belong here.

One would in particular have to single out the manifold remunerations which the committee members awarded to themselves for every significant and insignificant business apart from their regular salary (e.g. to a chancery clerk for finding out what the duke’s pleasure was), and so many things which seem to be able to be called a regular swindle, in which the same family names occur especially often.

Then too the neat specimens of diplomatic attempts and missions and above all their rewards would be noteworthy; in the account from 1778 to 1781 there occurs a sum of 5000 fl. which was paid over in the year 1770 to a foreign privy councillor for a journey to Petersburg, in order to transact there the published (?)

business of the land there; a journey to Munich on commercial matters at 8700 fl. each, and so forth. - It is of no avail to say that the wasting and plundering of the state treasury were abuses and contraventions of law; if in 26 years the sum of the country’s money used contrary to law can amount to four millions, then the laws under which such a contravention of law is possible are certainly no good; a good constitution is presumably only such a one through which contraventions of law are punished and, still more, prevented. - If such things happened when the wood was green, one would like to ask what will they be when it is dry?

If plunder and waste happened at a time when the emperor and the imperial courts still stood above the estates, when the estates themselves had ended a long, extremely costly process against their prince on account of extortions and contraventions of law and had taken over a great mass of debts - the payment of which may perhaps not even yet be completed some fifty years later to this hour; - at a time which one hears praised as a time of German honesty, of estates’ dignity, of a felicity created by the constitution, in contrast to the corruption, luxury and injustice of more recent times!
zh: 这个结果提一提或许就足够了；从它那里铺陈出一幅详尽的图画，描绘这种独立性把这套等级议会的管理拖到多深的深渊，不属于本题。
尤其应当从其中挑出来的是那些名目繁多的酬金：委员会成员为每一件大大小小的事务——除了他们的正常薪俸之外——都自行给自己加发（例如给一名文书官一笔钱，只因为他打听了公爵的心意）；还有那么些事情，说它们是正式的敲诈大概也说得过去，而在这些事上，同一些家族姓氏出现得格外频繁。
其次，那些干净漂亮的外交试探与派遣、以及尤其是对它们的酬劳，也值得注意；在 1778 年至 1781 年的账目中，出现了一笔 5000 古尔登的款项，它在 1770 年被支付给一位外国的枢密院顾问，用于前往彼得堡，以处理在那里所办的（??）

邦国的事务；另有一次出于商务之事的慕尼黑之行，每次 8700 古尔登，等等。——说国家国库的挥霍与劫掠是滥用权力、是违法行径，这毫无用处；如果在二十六年里，被违法使用的邦国钱财可以达到四百万之数，那么那些使这类违法行径成为可能的法律肯定是不中用的；一部好的宪法大概只有这样一部：借助于它，违法行为受到惩罚，而且更多地被预先防止。——如果这样的事发生在树木还青的时候，那么人们真要问一句：到了枯的时候那又该怎么样呢？

如果劫掠与挥霍发生在这样一个时代——那时皇帝与帝国法院还凌驾于等级议会之上，那时等级议会自己还结束了一场针对自己君主的、旷日持久而代价高昂的诉讼，其起因是君主的勒索与违法，并且还承接了一大批债务——而这批债务的清偿也许直到此刻、即五十来年之后都还没有完成；——如果劫掠与挥霍发生在这样一个人们听人赞颂为德国式正直、等级议会的尊严、宪法所创造的幸福，与近代的败坏、奢侈与不义相对照的时代——那才真是令人不寒而栗。

en: But the evil that the independence of the estates made it possible for them to plunder the state treasury, be it now a necessary consequence or it may be countered by laws and changed institutions, still remains by far the greater evil in relation to the state: that the independence of the estates in the disposal and administration of a state treasury makes it possible for them to make the course of the state difficult, indeed to hamper it, partly on the side of internal affairs, partly especially on the side of the political relation to other states - a relation which lies already more remote from the estates, and is often hateful to them, and has hitherto been foreign to the Germans in general.

The idea of wanting to put into the hands of the estates, or of whatever corporation in the state it may be, a military power and army independent of the government would generally be regarded as a measure that shatters the state; but it would make no great difference if the disposal of the whole or a part of the state treasury and the authority to grant salaries and pensions out of it belonged to such a corporation.
It can seem that estates of a former German land, which had such a disposal, if this is no longer granted to them, lose a great deal in competence and power.

But it has already been remarked that through the transformation of a land from an imperial fief into a sovereign state the estates have gained infinitely in competence and power, and precisely because of this new increment the earlier competence cannot remain compatible with it.

With such provisions the state would cease to be a state and would be shattered by the two sovereign powers which would be in it; - or rather the unity would be restored, either by the so-called estates, as we have seen this in more recent history, overthrowing the existing government and seizing it for themselves, or, as we have likewise seen, by the governments driving away such estates and thereby saving state and people.

The greatest guarantee and security of the estates is precisely this, that they do not possess a power contrary to the nature of the thing, - whereas the most foolish thing is to seek in such a power a protection for oneself and for the people; for such a power makes it a matter of right, or sooner or later of necessity, to abolish such estates.
zh: 然而，等级议会的独立性使它们得以劫掠国家国库这一祸害，无论它现在是一种必然的后果，还是可以通过法律和改变了的制度加以遏制，就国家而言，始终还有一种远为巨大的弊病：等级议会在国家国库的支配与管理上的独立性，使它们有可能给国家的进程制造困难，甚至加以阻挠——一方面在内政方面，另一方面尤其在与其他国家的关系方面；而这种关系对等级议会来说本就更为遥远，并且常常为它们所厌恶，对德意志人整体来说迄今则一直是陌生的。
想把一支独立于政府的军事力量与军队交到等级议会、或国家中任何一个社团的手里，这一念头一般会被看作一项把国家砸得粉碎的措施；但如果整个或一部分国家国库的支配权，以及从其中发放薪俸与养老金的权力归于这样一个社团，那差别也不见得有多大。
人们可能会觉得：从前的某个德意志邦国的等级议会曾经拥有这样一种支配权，如今这项权力不再授予它们，它们在权限与力量上就损失良多。
但前面已经指出：一个邦国从帝国采邑变为主权国家，等级议会在权限与力量上便获得了无限的增长；而正是由于这份新的增长，先前的那份权限才不可能与它并存。
有了这样的规定，国家就不再是国家，而会被它内部并存的两重主权力量砸得粉碎；——或者更确切地说，统一会以某种方式恢复：要么是那些所谓的等级议会——如我们在近代史上所看到的——推翻既有的政府并把它攫为己有；要么是政府——如我们同样看到的——把这些等级议会驱逐出去，从而挽救国家与人民。
等级议会最大的保证与安全恰恰在于：它们并不掌握一种与事情本性相抵触的权力；——而最愚蠢的，莫过于在这种力量中为自己和为人民寻找保护；因为这样的力量使得废除这样的等级议会成为一项权利，或迟早成为一项必要。

en: It must further be added that with the qualitative difference of a fief and a state the closer formality is also entirely changed, which in the former had the relation between prince and subject.

In that prince and land, as owners and holders of special privileges, stood opposed to one another like private-law persons and so under a third, the power of the emperor and the empire, they were in the situation of being before a praetor, able to conclude contracts with one another and to behave towards one another according to the manner of private law.

Even in more recent times, when truer concepts have taken the place of the notion - formerly taken thoughtlessly and unreasoningly - that governments and princes rest on divine authority, the expression "state contract" has still seemed to contain the false thought, as if in the state the concept of a contract truly fitted the relation between prince and subject, between government and people, and as if the legal determinations of private law which follow from the nature of a contract could, indeed should, find their application here.

A little reflection makes it evident that the connection of prince and subject, of government and people has at its basis an original, substantial unity of their relations, whereas in a contract, on the contrary, what is assumed is the opposite, namely the equal independence and equal indifference of the two parties towards one another; an agreement which they conclude with one another about something is an accidental relation which arises from the subjective need and the arbitrariness of both.

The connection in the state differs essentially from such a contract; it is an objective, necessary relation independent of arbitrariness and caprice; it is in itself a duty, upon which the rights depend; in a contract, on the contrary, arbitrariness grants mutual rights, out of which duties only then flow. - With the transition of a land from its imperial fiefdom into a state, the previous independence of the two sides, mediated by a third intermediate and supreme power, and with it the whole contractual relation, has fallen away.
zh: 还须补充的是：随着采邑与国家之间的质的差异，近乎程式的东西也完全改变了——在采邑中，这一程式就是君主与臣民之间的关系。
当君主与邦土作为特殊权利的所有者与享有者，像私法上的人那样彼此相对，并因而处在一个第三者——皇帝与帝国的权力——之下时，他们就如同处在一位裁判官面前，能够彼此订立契约，并按照私法的方式彼此相待。
即便在较近的年代——那时更为真实的概念已经取代了先前那种既无思想又无理性地接受下来的表象，即政府与君主建立在神圣权威之上的表象——「国家契约」这一说法似乎仍然包含着一个错误的想法：仿佛在国家中，契约这一概念真正契合于君主与臣民、政府与人民之间的关系；仿佛私法的那些法定规定——它们从契约的本性中产生——在这里能够、乃至应当得到适用。
稍加思考便可看出：君主与臣民、政府与人民之间的联结，以其关系中一种原初的、实质的统一为基础；反之，在契约中所预设的恰恰是相反的东西——即双方彼此之间同等的独立与同等的漠不相关；双方就某事彼此达成的协议，是一种偶然的关系，它出自双方主观的需要与任意。
国家中的这种联结，与那样的契约有本质的不同：它是一种客观的、必然的、不依赖于任意与意愿的关系；它本身是一项义务，而各项权利依赖于它；反之，在契约中是任意相互让予权利，而义务只是从这些权利中才流出来。——随着一个邦国从其帝国采邑身份转入国家，双方先前那种由第三者——中介与最高权力——所中介的独立性，以及随之而来的整个契约关系，都消失了。

en: The fundamental error of the position which the Württemberg estates gave themselves lies herein, that they start from a positive right, looked upon themselves entirely as if they still stood on that standpoint, and demanded the right only on the ground that they had formerly possessed it.

They acted as a merchant would act who, with regard to a ship which contained his fortune and which, however, has been destroyed by a storm, would still continue the same way of life and demand the same credit from others on it, - or like a landowner whom a beneficent flood had covered the sandy soil he possessed with fertile loam, and who wanted to till and cultivate his field in the same way as before.
zh: 符腾堡等级议会为自己所取的立场所犯的根本错误就在这里：它们是从一种实定法权出发的，把自己完全看成仿佛仍站在那个立场上，并且仅仅以「从前曾经拥有」为理由去要求那项权利。
它们行事的方式，就像一位商人：他的船载着他的全部财产，却已被风暴毁掉，他却还要照旧过原来的生活，并且还要别人就这条船给予同样的信用；——又像一位地产主：一场慈悲的洪水把他所拥有的沙土覆盖上肥沃的腐殖土，他还要像从前一样去耕种与经营自己的田地。

en: One sees in the manner in which the estates summoned in Württemberg conducted themselves precisely the counterpart of what began 25 years ago in a neighbouring realm and what at that time resounded in all minds, namely that in a state constitution nothing should be acknowledged as valid except what is to be acknowledged according to the right of reason.

One could have the concern that the leaven of the revolutionary principles of that time, the abstract thoughts of freedom, had not yet fermented and been digested in Germany, and that assemblies of the estates would avail themselves of the opportunity to make similar attempts and to bring about confusions and dangers.

Württemberg has indeed given the consoling example up to this degree that such an evil spirit no longer haunts, but at the same time also that the enormous experience which has been made in France and outside France, in Germany just as well as there, was lost to these estates, - namely the experience that the extreme of obstinate persistence on the positive state law of a vanished condition and the opposite extreme of an abstract theory and shallow chatter were equally the entrenchments of selfishness and the sources of misfortune in that land and outside it. - The Württemberg estates wanted to begin again on the standpoint on which the former estates found themselves; they did not enter into the content of the royal constitutional document and did not ask and try to prove what and that something is reasonable right, but simply persisted in the formalism, demanding an old positive right on the ground that it had been positive and contractual.

One had to regard the beginning of the French Revolution as the struggle which the rational state law entered into with the mass of positive law and of privileges by which it had been suppressed; in the deliberations of the Württemberg estates we see the same struggle of these principles, only that the places are exchanged.

If at that time the majority of the French imperial estates and the party of the people asserted and reclaimed the rights of reason and the government was on the side of the privileges, then in Württemberg rather the king placed his constitution in the territory of rational state law; the estates threw themselves up on the contrary as defenders of the positive and of the privileges; yes, they gave the reverse spectacle of doing this in the name of the people, against whose interest those privileges are directed even more than against that of the prince.
zh: 从在符腾堡被召集起来的等级议会所采取的行事方式中，人们看到的恰恰是二十五年前在一个邻近之邦开始、并且当时在所有精神中回响的那件事的反面：即在一份国家宪法中，除依照理性的法权应当被承认者之外，不应承认任何东西为有效。
人们可能担心：那个时代革命原则的酵母——关于自由的抽象思想——在德国还没有发酵透、还没有被消化，而等级会议会抓住机会去作类似的尝试，从而带来混乱与危险。

符腾堡确实提供了这样一个多少令人宽慰的例证：那种恶劣的精神不再作祟；但同时也表明：法国以及法国之外——在德国也和在法国一样——所获得的那番巨大经验，对这些等级议会来说是失落了的；——这经验便是：对一个已经消失的状态的实定国家法的僵硬坚持这一极端，与一种抽象理论和浅薄闲谈的相反极端，同样都是那个邦国及其之外的自私的堡垒与不幸的根源。——符腾堡等级议会想要重新从前代等级议会所站的那个立场上开始；它们不去进入王家宪法文书的内容，也不去追问、不去证明何物是合理的法权以及有合理法权存在，而只是一味坚持形式主义，以「那曾经是实定的、并且是契约性的」为理由去要求一项旧的实定法。
人们必须把法国大革命的开始看作理性国家法与实定法的大批条文以及那些压抑它的特权之间的一场斗争；而在符腾堡等级议会的审议中，我们看到的是这些原则之间的同一场斗争，只不过双方的位置被调换了。
如果当时法国的帝国等级中的多数与人民党主张并索回理性的权利，而政府站在特权的一边，那么在符腾堡，倒是国王把自己的宪法置于理性国家法的领域之中；等级议会则反过来，奋起充当实定法与特权的卫道士；是的，它们还上演了一出颠倒的戏：以人民的名义去做这件事——而那些特权所损害的，与其说是君主的利益，不如说更是人民的利益。

en: One could say of the Württemberg estates what has been said of the French émigrés: they have forgotten nothing and learned nothing; they seem to have slept through these last 25 years, the richest which world history has perhaps had, and the most instructive for us, because our world and our representations belong to them.

There could hardly have been a more terrible mortar for crushing to pieces the false legal concepts and prejudices about state constitutions than the court of these 25 years; but these estates have come out of it unimpaired, just as they were before. - Old right and old constitution are just as fine, grand words as it is sacrilegious sounding to rob a people of its rights.

But whether that which is called old right and old constitution is right or bad cannot depend on its age; the abolition of human sacrifice, of slavery, of feudal despotism and of countless infamies was also always an Aufhebung of something which was an old right.

It has often been repeated that rights cannot be lost, that a hundred years of injustice cannot make a right, - one should have added: if only the hundred years of injustice had been called right for those hundred years; further, that a hundred-year-old and genuine positive law goes to ruin rightedly if the basis falls away which is the condition of its existence.

If one has the pleasure of threshing empty straw, one may assert that after the death of the one, the other spouse still retains his right to him, and that the merchant whose ship has been swallowed by the sea still retains his right to it.
It has always been the disease of the Germans to cling to such a formalism and to go round with it.
So then, even with this Württemberg assembly of the estates, almost the whole content of its activity is confined to the unfruitful assertion of a formal right with the selfishness of the advocate.

In vain did a few voices try to lead them to the matter itself, among them the president of the assembly, the Prince of Hohenlohe-Öhringen, to turn them aside now and then from the course of legal proceedings, - the mortar in which the age had been crushed for 25 years had, after all, no power over them.
zh: 人们可以就符腾堡等级议会说出那句关于法国流亡者的话：他们什么也没有忘记，什么也没有学会；他们似乎把最近这二十五年——世界历史大概所能有的最丰富的二十五年，也是对我们最有教益的二十五年，因为我们的世界与我们的表象属于它们——睡过去了。
要碾碎关于国家宪法的那些错误法权概念与偏见，几乎不可能有比这二十年的法庭更可怕的一具石臼了；然而这些等级议会毫发无损地从其中走了出来，一如它们此前的样子。——「旧法权」与「旧宪法」这两个词，就其动听与堂皇而言，与「夺走一个民族的权利」这种说法听起来亵渎神圣，一模一样。
然而，被称为「旧法权」与「旧宪法」的东西究竟是好是坏，并不能取决于它的古老；废除人祭、奴隶制、封建专制以及数不清的污秽，也始终是对某种「旧法权」的扬弃。
人们常常反复说：权利不会丧失，一百年的不正义不能造成一项权利；——人们本应补上一句：哪怕这百年的不正义在这百年之间被称为「权利」；此外还应当说：一项百年以上的、真正实定的法权，只要那构成其存在条件的基础消失了，它就会理所当然地走向消亡。
如果有人有兴致去打空草，那么他也就可以断言：夫妻中的一方去世之后，另一方对他仍保有自己的权利；商人的船被大海吞没之后，他对这条船仍保有自己的权利。
一向以来，抱住这类形式主义不放并借此四处游荡，正是德意志人的病症。
于是，即便在这场符腾堡等级会议上，其活动的全部内容几乎也被限制在：凭着律师式的私心去主张一种形式上的权利，而这主张毫无成果。
少数几道声音曾徒劳地试图把他们引到事情本身上来，其中包括会议主席霍恩洛厄-厄林根亲王，他不时试图使他们偏离那条诉讼程序的道路；——那架把时代碾碎了二十五年的石臼，对他们终究是无能为力的。

en: From this conduct of the estates, of holding fast to the formalism of positive law and to the standpoint of private law where it was a matter of rational law and of state law, it follows for the history of their one and a half years of deliberations that they are extremely poor in thought and contain little, or almost nothing, instructive for so great an object as that presented to them, the free constitution of a German state in the present time.
Instead of fruitful work, therefore, almost only an external history presents itself, of which the main course is now to be indicated.
zh: 从等级议会这种行事方式——在涉及理性法与国家法之处，却抱住实定法的形式主义与私法的立场不放——可以就其一年半的审议之历史得出这样的结论：它们在思想上是极为贫乏的；对于摆在它们面前的那样一个伟大的对象——当今一个德意志国家的自由宪法——它们所包含的教益很少，或者几乎等于零。
因此，代替富有成果的工作，摆在我们面前的几乎只是一部外在的历史；现在不妨勾勒出它的主线。

en: It has already been mentioned that, after the king had on 15 March 1815 solemnly opened the assembly of the estates and, after the handing over of the constitutional charter, had left them to themselves, Count von Waldek appeared with a speech which began with the praise of the king just mentioned, of the "lofty monarch who has shown rare strength, has considerably extended Württemberg and now establishes the constitution founded for eternity by his illustrious ancestors, all princes of rare qualities".

This praise is now, like the whole speech, so strained and ambiguous, the stamp of refinement is pressed so firmly on every word, that the assembly of the estates could rejoice in it of the cleverness of their orator, of having shown to the outside the duty of devotion, but of having reserved everything within; - the king and the ministry, on the contrary, could take these distorted and hidden expressions as mockery, all the more so since he is expressly credited with the decision to establish the bond long acknowledged as beneficial between the regent and all the estates of the state and a constitution satisfying all parts, and to undo again the abolition, effected nine years ago, of the constitution founded for all eternity by the illustrious ancestors.

One could take this assurance for a bold assumption, if action had been taken at once and only in its sense; but as said, it could appear rather only mocking and malignant, since the grievance of the assembly of the estates had from this first sitting onwards for its sole content that, on the contrary, the king had not wanted to restore that old constitution at all, and that with the constitution which came from him not a single one of the estates of his state, no part of it (apart from the king himself and his ministers), was satisfied.
zh: 前面已经说过：国王在 1815 年 3 月 15 日隆重开启等级会议、并在交付了宪章文书之后让他们自行其是，随后瓦尔德克伯爵——他不是老符腾堡人，也并非以自己享有表决权的等级成员的身份，而只是一名这样的成员的代理人——登台发表了一篇演说；这篇演说以方才提到的对国王的赞颂开篇，即那位「高迈的君主：他显示了罕见的强健，使符腾堡大有扩展，如今又建立起那部由其尊贵祖先——清一色是具有罕见品质的亲王们——为永远而创立的宪法」。

然而这篇赞颂——如同整篇演说一样——被写得如此曲折而含糊，每一个词都被打上了精致做作的印记，以致等级会议得以在其中为自己演说辞令的精巧而自得：在对外上显示了应有的虔敬，在内里却把一切都保留了下来；——而国王与内阁却可以把这些被扭曲、被隐藏的说法当作嘲讽来听；这就更其如此，因为人们明明把这样一项决断归到国王名下：建立起那条几个世纪以来被公认为有益的、把统治者与国家一切等级联结起来的纽带，并制定一部令各方满意的宪章，同时再度扬弃那项九年前发生的、对尊贵祖先为永远而建立的宪法的扬弃。
如果当即就照这个意思行事、并且只照这个意思行事，那么人们本可以把这一保证看作一个胆大的假定；但如前所述，它显得更多地只是讥讽而刻薄，因为从第一次会议起，等级会议的全部不满就只包含着这一点：恰恰相反，国王根本不想恢复那部旧宪法；而且对于他那部出自他手的宪法，他国家中的等级议会没有一个——它的任何一部分（除了国王本人和他的大臣们）——是满意的。

en: The further course of this speech is a historical compilation of the fortunes of Württemberg under its constitution; as the general result it appears that the condition of the land at all times, while it had that constitution, was miserable, depressed, unhappy.

From this a conclusion is drawn which contrasts with such a premise, "that the old Württemberg constitution has blessed the land for centuries, that it has the most decided advantages over all the constitutions of other lands, that it has undoubtedly always been the best constitution of a German land, and has been the object not only of the admiration of Germany but even repeatedly of the attention of England".

Hereby and because everything in it is determined contractually and nothing is doubtful, because it is guaranteed that it has been sworn by all regents, that the people has not renounced it, etc., it alone is to be acknowledged as fundamental law and fundamental contract.
Some modifications which have become necessary through the changed circumstances, the ones mentioned above, are to be founded only on it.

The address proposed by the orator accordingly and accepted by the assembly does not express these thoughts in direct style, but rather brings them in a crooked way in the form of indirect hypotheses as follows: if the people have chosen representatives only on the presupposition that the old inherited constitution, which has blessed Württemberg for centuries, confirmed, etc.

constitution is to be taken as the basis of all modifications, and if furthermore the majority of the territorial lords must reserve their rights and the pronouncement of the congress, then the estates acknowledge with the most humble gratitude that the king in the opening of this day has given them occasion to deliberate on the application of the newer relations to the older relations of the land.
Just as therefore the assembly must reserve to itself to lay the result of its deliberations before the king, so they do not doubt, etc.
zh: 这篇演说的进一步进程，是一份关于符腾堡在其宪法之下之命运的历史汇编；作为一般的结果可以看到：这个邦国在拥有那部宪法的一切时期中，其状况都是凄惨的、压抑的、不幸的。
由此便得出一个与这一前提适成对照的结论：「老符腾堡的宪法数百年来造福于这个邦国；它比一切其他邦国的宪法都有明确得多的优势；无疑它历来都是一个德意志邦国中最好的宪法；它不仅曾是德国赞赏的对象，而且还不止一次成为英国关注的对象。」
因此，并且因为其中一切都以契约方式规定、没有任何可疑之处，因为已有保证：它已为历任统治者所宣誓，并且人民并未对它作出放弃——等等——所以唯有它应当被承认为根本法与根本契约。
某些因情势变化而成为必要的修改——即上文所提到的那些修改——只应当以它为基础。
演说者据此提出并由会议接受的陈情书，并不以直接的方式表达这些想法，而是以一种曲折的方式、借着间接假设的形式这样表述：如果人民只是在这样一个预设之下才选出了自己的代表——即预设那部古老的、世袭的、几百年来造福于符腾堡的、经过确认的——
宪法应当成为一切修改的基础；而如果多数等级领主还必须保留自己的权利与大会的裁决——那么等级议会以最恭顺的感恩承认：国王在今日的开会中给了他们一个机会，去商议如何把较新的关系适用于这个邦国较旧的关系。
正如等级会议必须为自己保留把商议结果呈报国王的权利一样，他们也不怀疑——等等——

en: Quite otherwise than this hypothetical concealing style sounds, quite otherwise than that only a deliberation is reserved, that the result of the deliberation should be reported to the king only in future and, if such a result is obtained, only then, the assembly already in its next sitting states the meaning of its address expressly to the effect that by it it has declared that it can negotiate concerning the newer modifications, brought about by particular circumstances, only on the basis of the old Württemberg constitution.
zh: 这一假设性的、遮遮掩掩的腔调完全是另一回事；把它说成只是保留一次商议、说是商议的结果要到将来、并且只有当这样的结果取得之后才呈报国王——这也完全是另一回事。因为会议紧接着就在它的下一次会议中就明确地表达了其陈情书的意旨：它借此声明，关于因特殊情势而起的那些较新的修改，只有以老符腾堡的宪法为基础才可加以磋商。

en: After the speech of Count von Waldek and the reading of his prepared address, and after only one further deputy had made some urging remarks on the signing of the address, there followed the silent unanimous acceptance of it by the assembly.
zh: 在瓦尔德克伯爵的演说和他所预备的陈情书的宣读之后——其间只有一位议员就签署该陈情书说了几句敦促的话——便是会议对它无声的一致接受。

en: The balanced style and content of the speech and the address, which on the one hand is interwoven with a boldness which one could even call mockery, and on the other hand is strained, hidden and stiff, has already been made noteworthy.

The diplomatic negotiations of more recent times show, amid all the caution, composure and balance of expression, an open, direct and dignified bearing, and with the greatest cleverness at the least a self-satisfied shrewdness.

How much more should one have expected from a German assembly of the estates in openness, vitality and dignified frankness in their first declaration, instead of the annoying strainedness and concealment and then the silence with which the rest of the assembly hid behind that strainedness!
zh: 这篇演说与这份陈情书的措辞与内容——一方面织入了那种甚至可以称之为嘲弄的大胆，另一方面又拘谨、隐藏而僵硬——其那种经过斟酌的通报风格，已经被人注意到了。
近代的外交谈判在措辞的一切谨慎、沉着与斟酌之中，显露出一种公开、直接而有尊严的姿态；而在最大的明智之中，最少的却是那种讨人喜欢的乖巧。
人们原本该从一个德意志等级会议的第一份声明中期待更多的坦率、生气与有尊严的公开——而不是那种令人反感的矫饰与隐藏，以及随后其余成员躲在这种矫饰背后的沉默！

en: But what they afterwards very much boasted of here was the unanimity with which the decision to accept the address was taken.
What this and the outward manner of carrying the address through in the sitting came to, the following sitting and the further course of the deliberations will show.
In this sitting (of 17 March) six gentlemen of the nobility protest against the statement contained in the address that the nobility present reserves its rights.

Their declaration made on this point states that the speeches of the two members, on which the address was based, were delivered in part so quickly, in part in so weak a voice, that they could not be heard; further it is remarked that the rising from the seats was to serve in place of a formal vote, but the occasion and the purpose of this rising were not generally known. - The formality of voting must above all have been determined in an assembly and known to the members; even if for the first moment a manner had to be invented, it had to be accompanied by an expression and a declaration that its meaning could not be open to doubt.
The picture of the silence is made complete by the mention of the rapid reading of the statements and the low voice there.

Is this a picture worthy of the first appearance of an assembly of the estates, of an appearance with which it took for all time the decisive, indeed its only decision? - Those six members gave the unqualified declaration that they gratefully accept the constitution given by the king.

This explicitness contrasts very sharply with the turns of phrase of the address, whose meaning one had otherwise to be prepared and informed about in order to know that it was to be the non-acceptance of the charter.

It would have been more open and more worthy of an assembly of German men and representatives of the people if it had declared its non-acceptance of the royal constitution just as unqualifiedly as those six nobles declared their acceptance.

The delicacy observed towards the king is mentioned now and then in what follows; but the true delicacy undoubtedly lies in a cultivated frankness, and the most indelicate behaviour and tone towards the king and towards itself is presumably the strainedness and attitude mentioned above.
zh: 但他们事后在这里自鸣得意得多的，却是那项接受陈情书的决议是以怎样的意见一致通过的。
这件事以及在会议中强行通过该陈情书的那种外在做法究竟意味着什么，接下来的会议与审议的进一步进程将会显示出来。
在这次会议（3 月 17 日）中，六位贵族先生对陈情书中所载「在座的全体贵族保留其权利」这一说法提出抗议。
他们就此所作的声明指出：作为该陈情书依据的那两位成员的发言，一部分讲得极快，一部分声音极为微弱，以致听不分明；此外还提到，会员从座位上起身应当是代替一次正式的表决，而这次起身的缘由与目的却并非众所周知。——表决的形式在一个会议中首先必须是确定下来并且为各位成员所知晓的；即便在最初的时刻必须发明出一种做法，它也应当伴随着一声表述与一项声明，以表明其意义不容置疑。
而那幅沉默的图景，由于提到了这些陈述被飞快地宣读、以及声音低微，便变得完整了。
这样一幅图景，配得上一个等级会议的首次登场吗——一个就是靠它永远作出了那项决定性的、其实也是它唯一的一项决议的登场？——那六位成员明确声明：他们感激地接受国王所给出的宪章。
这种明确，与陈情书中的那些说法形成了尖锐的反差——对于这些说法，人们原本必须事先有所准备并得到告知，才知道它的意思原来是不接受那部宪章。
如果它能像那六位贵族宣告接受那样不折不扣地宣告自己不接受王家宪法，那么这个做法本会更坦率，也更配得上一个由德意志人士与人民代表组成的会议。
以下不时提到对国王所抱的那种谨慎；但真正的谨慎无疑在于一种有教养的坦率，而对国王并且对自身最不谨慎的行为与腔调，想必就是上面所提到的那种矫饰与姿态。

en: More important, however, is that a main decision should not merely have been preceded by two reports which hardly touched the matter, and that the unanimity of the decision, instead of being able to count as a merit, must rather have been the greatest reproach and censure for the assembly.
One sees the assembly of the estates for the great majority already agreed in advance upon their decision and the matter settled in silence.

Another part shows later indeed in part an opposition, but above all it shows complete indifference to the nerve of the decision, namely to the old constitution; this part claims for itself neither the formal right nor the content of it, but wants only a good and therefore rather a better constitution than the old Württemberg one. - One sees therefore an assembly which in its relation is still new, which is brought to reserve and silence by the ignorance of its constituents, the uncertainty of what is to be, the unwontedness and unpractisedness, and which the stiffness and the concealing decisiveness of some members impress upon.

If the assembly had grasped its position and its notion more clearly and more boldly, then it would rather have had to make the greatest openness and fullness of statement its law and, instead of being silent, to have regarded it as the greatest thing, since it had been granted to it to have the word.

Even if the unanimity had been present according to the actual intention or had emerged from intimidation and lack of self-confidence, still in all cases it would have had to make it a duty for itself, if one likes to call it so, to elect a devil's advocate - and this name seems not at all inappropriate in view of the proved animosity against the royal constitution - it would have had to, ex officio, develop itself all the reasons which could argue for the acceptance of the royal constitution and let them be set in the clearest light, and then likewise let an unreserved statement of its real opinion and a detailed account of its motives precede its decisions.

But such a deliberation has neither preceded nor followed the decision; but an assembly of the estates is there for that, not only that it should not act without deliberation, but that it should hold its deliberations on the interests of the state before the people and the world.
zh: 不过更为重要的是：这样一项主要决议本不应仅仅以两篇几乎不触及实质的报告为前奏；而且，决议的一致性与其说能被算作一种优点，不如说必定成为对会议最大的指责与非难。
人们看到，等级会议中的绝大多数事先就已同意他们的决议，事情在默默中就已了结。
另一部分人后来确实在某些方面显示出反对，但尤其显示出对决议之神经——即对那部旧宪法——的完全漠然；这部分人自己既不主张那种形式上的权利，也不主张它的内容，而只是想要一部好的、因而是比老符腾堡宪法更好的宪法。——因此人们看到的是一个在其处境上尚且全新的会议：它由于对自己的构成成分缺乏了解、对将要出现什么没有把握、由于不合习惯与缺乏训练，而被引向拘谨与沉默；而少数成员那种拘谨与隐藏的坚决又强加于它。
如果会议能够更清楚、更勇敢地把握自己的立场与概念，那么它反而必须把最大的坦率与详尽作为自己的法则；而且与其保持沉默，它就必须把这视为最大的事，因为发言权已经被赋予给了它。

即便这种一致性按其真实意图而言确曾存在，或者是从恫吓与缺乏自信中产生的，在一切情形下，它都必须把这样一件事变成自己的义务——如果人们愿意这样称呼的话——即选出一位「魔鬼代言人」；而考虑到已经证明了的对国王那部宪章的敌意，这个名称似乎并不怎么不合适。——它必须以其职权自行展开一切可以主张接受国王那部宪法的理由，并让人把它们置于最明亮的光照之下；然后，同样地，必须让对其真实意见的毫不含糊的表述与对其动机的详尽剖析先行于它的决议。
但这样一场商议既没有先于决议，也没有后于决议；而等级会议之所以存在，正是为了这一点：不仅是为了使它不未经商议就行事，而且是为了使它能在人民与世界面前进行关于国家利益的商议。

en: When some months later Mr Gleich, representative of Aalen, delivered a report which was quite contrary to the hitherto undeliberated presuppositions of the assembly, the committee which had to render a report on it pointed out to him that such an appearance must occasion astonishment and general disapprobation in an assembly in which concord and patriotic rectitude had hitherto kept every foreign and dishonest influence at a distance.

How? A deputy who takes the courage finally to make his dissenting opinion audible against this silent and dead unanimity must by that expose himself to the imputation of a foreign and dishonest influence?

In any case the direct imputation of dishonesty or the complete abstention from mere insinuation would have been more worthy. - To the report of Mr Gleich the committee at the beginning of its report ascribes - or rather says that it seems to have - the purpose of forming an opposition party in the assembly hitherto so most honourably characterised by concord.

Whoever has only thought a little about the nature of an assembly of the estates and is familiar with its appearances cannot fail to notice that without an opposition such an assembly is without external and internal vitality, that precisely such a contrast belongs to its essence, to its justification, and that it is only really constituted when an opposition comes to light in it; without one it has the form only of a party or even of a clump.
zh: 几个月之后，阿伦的代表格莱希先生发表了一篇报告，其内容与会议迄今未经商议的前提完全相反；负责就此提出报告的委员会向他指出：在一个此前一直以和睦与爱国的正直把一切外来的、不正当的影响都排斥在外的会议中，这样一种现象必定引起惊讶与普遍的反对。
怎么？一位终于鼓起勇气、让自己不同的意见公开反对这种沉默而僵死的全体一致的人，就因此必须让自己招致「受外来的、不正当的影响」这种嫌疑？
无论如何，直接指斥其不诚实，或者完全不作单纯的中伤之辞，都更为体面。——委员会在报告的开头就把一个目的加在格莱希先生的报告上——或者更确切地说，说他似乎有这样一个目的——即在那个迄今为止以和睦而备受称誉的会议中组建一个反对党派。
凡是稍稍思考过等级会议的性质、并熟悉其各种表现的人，都不可能注意不到：没有反对派，这样的会议是没有外在与内在生命力的；恰恰是这样一种对立才属于它的本质、属于它的正当性；而只有当一个反对派在其中显露出来时，它才真正地成为它所是的样子；没有这样的东西，它就只具有一个党派、甚至一团东西的外形。

en: The reporter has dwelt at length on the manner in which the assembly of the estates has appeared, because it is not only remarkable in itself but also characteristic of the whole sequel.

With respect to the formality of the course which the assembly conducted its business, two circumstances still deserve to be made noteworthy. - The course of its deliberations within itself was in general this, that for a subject occurring a committee was appointed by it, a report was rendered by this, then it was debated and upon this the decision was to be taken. - In the choice of the committee it was most frequently, especially at the beginning, where it mattered most to get into possession and to make an impression, invariably the vice-president, who proposed the members by name.

This board chosen by the assembly proposed into the first committees, after only two members had yet shown themselves publicly in the assembly, at once those members who marked themselves out for ever as the heads of the old Württemberg party.

It resulted from this that the word came completely into their hands, all the more so if one sees the otherwise delicate consideration of the members of the assembly of the estates towards one another.

This went so far that in one case, where the assembly had resolved to appoint a committee of twelve members, and eleven had received the majority, while for the twelfth place four members had equal votes, they did not now co-opt one of these four, by which three of them would have been excluded, but rather against their own resolution appointed all fifteen in their committee of twelve members. - Already at the second committee, which was to be appointed, there then occurs a remarkable stiffness in order to bring it about that the four heads appointed into the first did not fail either to become members of the second.

It is very essential for the freedom of an assembly, given the great influence of a committee in general, that the same individuals do not occupy all the committees, when every business occurring has to be prepared by such a one, so that this preparation for everything does not remain in the same hands.

This influence is moreover almost unconditional in an assembly in which almost the only, at least the principal report on a matter comes from the committee and is so to speak really not discussed at all.
zh: 报告人对等级会议登场的方式之所以详加论述，是因为这不仅本身引人注目，而且对于整个后续过程都具有代表性。
就会议处理其事务所采用的那种程序的形式性而言，还有两种情形值得加以指出。——他们内部谈判的进程大体上是这样：出现一个事项，就由会议任命一个委员会，由该委员会提出报告，然后进行辩论，随后作出决议。——在委员会的选任上，最常见的——特别是在开头，那时最有赖于占据有利地位并造成声势——是由副主席提议具体人选。
这个由会议选出的主持机构，在会议中才只有两位成员公开露面之后，就立即在最初的几个委员会中提名了那些永远以老符腾堡党派首领自居的人。
由此可见，发言权完全落入他们手中；尤其是当人们看到等级会议成员彼此之间素有的那种相互体谅时，就更是如此。
这种体谅走得如此之远，以至于在一个情形中：会议曾决议任命一个十二人委员会，十一人的多数已经产生，而第十二个位置有四位成员票数相同——他们并没有从这四人中增补一人（那样就会把其中三人排除在外），而是违背自己的决议，把十五个人全都任命进了这个十二人委员会。——紧接着在应当任命第二个委员会时，就出现了一种引人注目的拘谨，其结果是被任命进第一个委员会的那四位首领也不曾不成为第二个委员会的成员。
考虑到一个委员会一般所具有的巨大影响，对一个会议的自由来说非常关键的是：在每一件出现的事务都必须由这样一个委员会先行准备的情况下，不要总是由同样的人去占据所有委员会，以免这一切的准备始终留在同样的人手中。
在一个几乎只有委员会的报告——至少某件事的主要报告——出自委员会、并且可以说根本不加讨论的会议中，这种影响更是几乎是无条件的。

en: The other noteworthy thing, namely, is the manner of the reports.

In the deliberations one finds not freely delivered speeches, but above all only read reports, fewer and only short oral utterances, in general no living speech and counter-speech; only towards the end of the assembly once, when instead of the matter the personality of a dissenting member, Mr Dr Cotta, was made the object, did the utterances fall, and among them some quite indecent personalities, not as usual indeed as written votes, but this time without preparation blow for blow; the natural eloquence showed itself which has still preserved itself on our markets for such cases; but the eloquence which held sway on a Roman forum, one did not see come to the fore. - That the reports of the committees were composed in writing and read out is of course otherwise self-evident.

What however the debating which followed hereupon consisted in was mostly this, that, sometimes several days and weeks later, one or some members read out a brought-along written vote, and again perhaps days and weeks later another member produced a like vote.

In one and the same sitting therefore a reading of several essays could follow one another, each of which referred to a quite different subject, and very often had no other consequence at all than that it was simply read out.

Precisely that enlivening which emerges from the fact that an assembly of men is set opposite to one another in order to assert, to prove, to refute, to move, face to face, mouth to mouth, with the living presence of mind, falls away completely through that written method. - One cannot call the reading of one essay after another of many kinds a discussion.

Rightly it is law in the English parliament that the reading of written reports is not permitted, partly because such an essay can very easily be the work of another, partly but above all because the whole nature of such an assembly is thereby changed.

Apart from a few speeches composed in a lively sense but likewise read out, the present fascicles of the proceedings are above all a collection of legal scruples, with citations not merely from the litany of landtag recessions, inheritance settlements, princely testaments and so forth, but also for example from the Corpus Iuris, Montesquieu, Zonaras130), [J. U. v.] Cramer in the treatise De tacente dissentiente (in Opuscula T. II, and in the Usus philosophiae Wolfianae in iure, spec.
XII [1740]) and deductions and stillborn advocate's writings pieced together with such pompous erudition.
zh: 另一件值得注意的事，就是报告的方式。

在谈判中人们找不到自由发挥的演说，最常见的多半只是照本宣科的报告，此外只有少数而且很简短的口头发言；总之没有活生生的发言与对答。只有在会议临近结束时，有一次——当人们不再讨论事情本身，而是把一位持异议的成员、科塔博士先生的人格作为对象时——发言才真正展开；其中甚至有一些相当不得体的人物，他们不再像通常那样以书面投票意见的形式出现，而这一次是不经准备、你来我往地交锋；于是一种在我们的市场上为这类情形保存至今的自然雄辩显露了出来；但那种曾在罗马广场上称雄的雄辩，人们却没有看到它现身。——委员会的报告是书面写成并加以宣读的，这一点本来也是不言自喻的。
而紧接着而来的所谓辩论，大多是这样：在有时相隔数天乃至数周之后，一两位成员把自己带来的书面投票意见照本宣读；然后又可能在数天、数周之后，另一位成员又提出一份同样的意见。
因此，在同一次会议中可能会接连宣读好几篇文章，每一篇都涉及一个全然不同的对象；而且极为常见的情况是，它除了被宣读之外根本没有别的结果。
恰恰那种由「一群人面对面而坐、要在活生生的精神在场之中口对心地主张、证明、反驳、感动」这一事实所产生的生气，却通过那种书面方法几乎完全消失了。——把各种论述接连宣读，不能称之为讨论。
英国议会以法令禁止宣读书面报告，这是有道理的：一方面这样一篇文章很容易是别人代写的，另一方面——尤其是主要的原因——因为这样一个会议的整个本性由此就被改变了。

除了少数几篇以活的精神写成、但同样只是宣读的演说之外，现有的这几辑会议记录主要是一份法律疑虑的汇编，其中引用的不仅有等级会议决议、继承和约、王公遗嘱等等的连篇祷文，而且例如还有《法典大全》（Corpus Iuris）、孟德斯鸠、佐纳拉斯130) 、[J. U. v.] 克拉默的《论沉默的异议者》（De tacente dissentiente，收入《论文集》（Opuscula T. II）第二卷，以及《沃尔夫哲学在法权中的运用》（Usus philosophiae Wolfianae in iure）第
十二 [1740]），以及诸如此类用堂皇学问拼凑起来的推演与胎死腹中的律师文书。

en: If an assembly of the estates represents the people, such a deliberation is the way in which a people expresses itself, the way in which action is taken upon such an assembly and upon a people itself?
Treatises composed in that manner in the study are also only addressed to studies or destined to become files for men of business.
But assemblies of the estates have their essential public among the people; how can this take an interest in such paper deliberations and pedantic deductions and go on with it?

Rather, in such a way its representatives isolate themselves from one another and still more from the people themselves and carry on the affairs of the people much more with an exclusion of the people, even if the sittings were public.

The physiognomy of the deliberations of the Württemberg assembly is in this way not very different from that of the activity of a society of young men who associate, who form essays for the advancement of their education as an exercise, and who on loan from one another hear them read out.
zh: 如果等级会议代表着人民，那么这样一场商议就是一个民族自我表达的方式，也就是对这样一个会议、对人民本身发生作用的方式吗？
以那种方式在书斋里写成的论述，也不过是写给书斋看的，或是注定成为实业人士的卷宗。
然而等级会议的根本观众却在于人民；人民怎么可能对这类纸面上的商议与迂腐的推演产生兴趣，并就此继续下去呢？
毋宁说，它的代表们这样地彼此隔离，而且更加与人民本身隔离；它们更是在排斥人民的情况下处理人民的事务，哪怕这些会议是公开的。
这样一来，符腾堡会议的审议之面貌，与一群年轻人的会社的活动并无多少不同：他们结合起来，为练习起见撰写短文以推进自己的教养，并且彼此借阅、听人朗读。

en: Setting aside the material side, this written manner, with the consequences which it must have had for the whole course of the conduct of business, was presumably also a ground for the statement, adduced in part VIII, S. 20, of a representative - admittedly declared indecent - "that if the petitions which had come in had not provided material for entertainment, one would not have known how to fend off the boredom". - In any case, if the debates of the estates were to consist chiefly in the communication of written deductions, their personal meeting would be quite superfluous and a great many costs saved; the whole thing could be dispatched by the circulation of the essays.

Whoever is accustomed to reading prefers in any case to read such essays himself to giving himself up to hearing them; but everyone would also have the choice of having them read out to him by his wife or a good friend, and the votes could then just as well be sent in in writing.
zh: 撇开物质的一面不谈，这种书面方式——连同它必然对整个办事进程所产生的影响——大概也是下面这条声明的一个缘由：一位代表在《会议记录汇编》第 8 分册 S. 20 处引述说（当然被斥为不得体的话）：「如果那些送到的请愿书没有提供可供消遣的材料，人们就不知道该怎样抵挡无聊了。」——何况，如果等级议会的辩论主要就是传达书面推演，那么它们的亲自聚集就相当多余，而且能省下许多费用；整个事情靠传阅这些短文就可以打发了。
习惯了阅读的人本来就更愿意自己读这些短文，而不是去听人朗读；不过每个人也都可以选择让妻子或一位好友替他朗读，而那些表决意见同样可以用书面形式寄送。

en: But to pursue the historical thread further, the great political event occurred right at the beginning of the sittings of the assembly of the estates, the arrival of Bonaparte in France from the island of Elba.
The king informed them already two days after the opening of the estates of the measures taken in Vienna.
An event of this kind was suited to bring to light the disposition and the whole character of a German assembly of the estates, through its behaviour and bearing in it.

If it had been possible that a German people could have received this event with joy and hope, then it could seem dangerous that estates, whose intentions were already indicated and were opposed to the will of their king, should be gathered together at this moment.

But since that was impossible, such an assembly had to seem the more desirable, in order to be able with united energy to make use of the means which an event so far-reaching, which seemed to threaten the peace of Europe afresh, required especially in the lands lying near France.
zh: 然而若要把历史的线索继续追下去，那么就在等级会议开会之初，便发生了那个重大的政治事件：波拿巴从厄尔巴岛回到法国。
在等级议会开幕之后仅仅两天，国王便把在维也纳所采取的措施告知了它们。
这样一类事件，很适于通过一个德意志等级会议在这件事中的举止与态度，把它的情怀与整个性格照亮出来。
如果一个德意志民族有可能以喜悦与希望来接受这个事件，那么等级议会——它们的意图前面已经说过，是与自己的国王的意志相对立的——在这个时候聚集在一起，就显得危险了。
然而既然那是不可能的，这样一个会议就必定显得更为可取，以便能够以集中的精力调动那些手段——一个如此深远的事件、一次看来重新威胁欧洲安宁的事件——在靠近法国的那些邦国中尤其需要这些手段。

en: It has been only too common a ruinous, unpatriotic, and in the higher sense often criminal artifice of the estates to want, instead of joining openly with their government in the common cause of averting the distress of the state, to make use of the pressure of the political circumstances into which their government had been placed, in order to extort advantages for themselves from the government and at the same time to bring about an embarrassment inwardly along with the outward one, by which the strength of the government towards the outside, instead of being increased, was weakened and in essence and in fact made common cause with the enemy. - On 28 March a member, in the whole feeling of the importance of the circumstances, moved (Vol.

II, S. 41), that the assembly should on its part declare to the king that the last drop of blood, the last gift of its property, was ready for him and for the good cause, - as the assembly intended to achieve this by a general arming, by a loan to be opened, but as it saw itself able to carry this out only by the old constitutional way. - A part of the nobility recognised in an address to the estates (Vol.

II, S. 14), that the highest danger requires the highest exertion, and asked, without adding any conditions, the assembly to initiate a step to the effect that the king should order a general arming of the country and military exercises.
Addresses from many district offices came in in a similar sense.
One from Esslingen of 29 March (Vol.

II, S. 48, the others have remained unprinted) expressed, with regard to the measure already taken by the king of raising a land battalion of 500 men in every district office, the concern that too many lenient considerations had been prescribed and that the defensive preparations could thereby suffer difficulties and delays; it wished for a general levy.
A report enclosed from the village headman Reinhard of Upper Esslingen has likewise been printed (Vol.
II, S. 50); it says: "The attempt to obtain volunteers as field corporals seems to be in vain with the discharged soldiers.
The people have, as many or most of them do, too blunt a feeling for love of fatherland and for defence.
Everything that is fit shall take up arms, from the 18th to the 40th
year.

"When the Swabians are levied in mass, they go and strike with force, but if they have free will, then nothing happens!!" - To this mayor, in that he speaks in this way of his people, among whom he stands in the thick of it, the assembly of the estates did not presumably wish to make the charge of slandering the people - a term which has become popular in our days - since it gave his report the distinction of being printed, and the title of a vigorous declaration.
zh: 等级议会常常采取这样一套有害的、不爱国的、在更高意义上甚至常常是犯罪的手腕：它们不与自己的当局公开地同做一件事来抵御国家的危难，反而想要利用当局所处的政治情势的逼迫，从当局那里强取对自己有利的好处，同时在外部的困局之外又在内部制造出一种困局；这样一来，当局对外的力量非但没有增加，反被削弱，而且就其本质与实情而言，与敌人站到了同一边。——3 月 28 日，一位成员怀着对情势重要性的全部感受提出动议（会议记录汇编第
2 卷，S. 41），声明等级会议方面也要向国王表明：它愿意献出最后的一滴血、财产的最后一份奉献，为他、为正义的事业效忠；——等级会议打算通过全民武装、通过一笔将要开办的借款来达成这一点，但它自认为只能以旧宪章的方式来实行这一切。——贵族中的一部分在一份致等级议会的陈情书中认识到（会议记录汇编第
2 卷，S. 14），最高的危险要求最高的努力；他们并且不附加任何条件地请求等级会议着手促成这样一件事：即国王下令实行全民武装与军事操练。
许多专区官署的陈情书也以类似的意思送来。
埃斯林根的一份，3 月 29 日（会议记录汇编第
2 卷，S. 48，其余的未予付印），对于国王已经作出的决定——在每一个专区官署组建一支五百人的地方营——表示忧虑：所规定的迁就之处太多，以致防御措施可能因此遭遇困难与耽搁；它希望实行全民征召。
上埃斯林根乡长莱因哈德随附的一份报告，同样作为一篇「有力的声明」被付印（会议记录汇编第
2 卷，S. 50）；它说：「试图招募志愿兵充任军士长，在退伍士兵那里似乎白费力气。
人民——正如其中许多人或大多数人的情形——对祖国之爱与防卫有着过于迟钝的感觉。
凡身体健康的，都要拿起武器，从 18 岁到 40
岁。
「如果施瓦本人被大批征召，他们就会前去并且奋勇作战；但如果他们有自由意志，那就什么也不会发生！！」——对于这位市长——他就这样谈论自己身处其中的民众——等级会议大概不愿意给他扣上「诽谤人民」的罪名（这是我们这个时代流行起来的一个说法），因为它给了他的报告以付印的殊荣，并冠以「有力的声明」这一标题。

en: But the assembly of the estates had already shackled itself in this as in its other affairs by assuming that the motions and proposals which it made could be interpreted as being for the exercise of the right of petition granted to it in the royal charter and, as a consequence of this, for a factual recognition of this charter.

As if the meeting together of the assembly of the estates on the ground of this constitution had not already been a quite formal fact, and as if the representatives of a people, who are assembled under such circumstances, under whatever title, form and authorisation it may be, did not have to banish all other considerations, in particular the fear of consequences, and alone to think and act vigorously for the salvation of their people!
zh: 然而等级会议无论就这件事还是就它其他的事务，早已通过这样一点给自己套上了枷锁：它认定自己所提出的动议与建议，可以被解释为是在行使王家宪章所授予它的请愿权，并且作为这一点的结果，是在事实上承认这部宪章。
仿佛等级会议依据那部宪法聚集在一起，本身还不曾是一个完全正式的事实；仿佛一个民族的代表们——他们在这样的情势之下、以什么样的名义、形式与授权而聚集——不是必须摒弃一切其他的考量，尤其是必须摒弃那种害怕惹出后果的顾虑，而只能为着自己民族的拯救有力地思考与行动！

en: The assembly at first had the addresses which had come in read out and entered them in the records.

With regard to the general arming of the country it was indeed rather out of season to observe as a merit of the town of Tübingen that it had already made the motion for it at a time when the situation in France was not yet known.

If mere patriotism in the face of a foreign danger can so easily hit upon the idea of a general arming of the people, then a more mature and better insight into the expediency of such a measure, military and above all political, was to be expected of an assembly of the estates, - at a time when the new meeting together of the estates itself caused the most manifold bustle and inner tension.
But into what light could the proposal of such an arming be placed, when it appeared even earlier, before the event in France gave such a measure an outward motive!

In any case experience had taught that such a constitutional arming in the many cases in the last 25 years in which Württemberg in particular had been overrun by war had shown not the least effectiveness, indeed had not shown itself at all, as according to their whole intention and condition it could hardly have been otherwise; in so far it can seem almost ridiculous to recall such an arming of the country under the danger of that time.

If the estates brought forward a proposal of which they had to reckon with the great probability that the king would not give it any sequel, then the belief in their earnestness and good will became all the more doubtful when they then refrained, on their part, from co-operating in the military measures which the king recognised as expedient and ordered.
zh: 会议起初让人宣读那些送到的陈情书，并把它们归入卷宗。
关于全民武装一事，颇不为合时宜地指出：图宾根城的功劳在于，在法国的情势尚未为人所知的时候，它就已经为此提出了动议。
如果单纯的爱国主义在对外危险面前如此轻易地就想出全民武装的主意，那么对这样一项措施在军事上、尤其在政治上是否明智，一个等级会议就应当有更成熟、更清醒的认识——何况是在这样一个时期：等级议会这种新的聚集本身就已经引起了各式各样的骚动与内在的紧张。
然而这样一项武装的建议又能被置于何种光亮之下呢？它出现得甚至更早——在法国的那个事件为这样一项措施提供外在动机之前！
何况经验早已教会人们：这样一项合乎宪法的武装，在过去二十五年中符腾堡特别遭受战争蹂躏的许多情形里，并未显示出丝毫效力，甚至根本没有显现出来——按照它全部的意图与状况，本来也不可能是别的样子；因此，在当时的危险之下仅仅回想起这样一项全民武装，看上去几乎可笑。
如果等级议会提出的建议，它们自己必定清楚十有八九不会得到国王的采纳，那么当它们随后又不肯就国王认为合宜并已下令的军事措施从自己这一方面加以协助时，人们对它们的认真与善意的信念就更加可疑了。

en: Among the means belonged especially the raising of the extraordinary war expenditure, of which the king caused the calculation to be laid before the estates under 17 April.

According to the same, the costs alone of the equipment and the maintenance of an army of 20,000 men, whose setting up the king had made binding towards his allies, exceeded the peace budget by 3 1/2 millions; to this came the burdens of the marches of the allied armies, about which likewise a convention had been concluded.

The king demanded of the estates a deliberation and, in the shortest possible time, a declaration as to how these extraordinary means were to be raised. - The answer to the question what the Württemberg estates, expressly called upon by their king as well as by their fellow citizens to co-operate and authorised to support the cause of Europe, had done to avert that danger of a unique kind and of a wholly extraordinary character is simply this: that they have done nothing at all.

The whole merit, of how Württemberg then appeared in the rank of all the European powers, they have rather left to the king, to the then crown prince, to the ministry and to the army. - The government, in fulfilment of its general, moral and positive obligations, has pursued its course for itself with honour and glory and, as it seems, has not been held back in the least by the refusal of the estates to co-operate.
The estates on the contrary have achieved nothing except to have shown their bad will, the non-appreciation of their beautiful position and the dispensability of their co-operation.
zh: 这些手段中特别包括筹措这笔异常的战争开销；国王于 4 月 17 日前后让等级议会看到相关账目。
按这份账目，单是装备与维持一支两万人军队的费用——国王已就这支军队的组建向他的盟国承担了义务——就超出和平预算三百五十万；此外还有盟军过境的开支，关于这一点同样缔结了一项协定。
国王要求等级议会议事，并在尽可能短的时间内声明这些非常手段应当如何筹措。——至于这样一个问题：符腾堡等级议会受其国王以及其同胞明确要求参与、并被授权支持欧洲的事业，为避免那场独特而极不寻常的危险做了些什么——答案是：它们根本没有做任何事。
符腾堡当时在欧洲各国行列中出场时的全部功劳，它们倒是留给了国王、当时的王储、内阁与军队。——政府为履行自己普遍的、道德的与实定的义务，独自走着一条通向荣誉与光辉的道路；而看来，等级议会拒绝协助并未使它受到丝毫牵制。
而等级议会则一无所获，只是显出了它们一贯的恶意、对自己美好处境的误认，以及它们之参与助的无关紧要。

en: Further some addresses directly concerning this subject were presented by them to the ministry, which no longer spoke of a willingness to make sacrifices, but were meant to provide relief to the land, exhausted as it admittedly was, by demanding that the royal chamber of domains, the church property and so forth should compete with them for the war burdens.

For that purpose the king had already caused effective negotiations to be carried on with his allies and the competent army commands; the answer which the estates received to their demand was simply this, that as much as was contributed from special state revenues would have to be replaced in the financial budget from other sources, and that what was at issue here was precisely extraordinary means. - In the sense of the earlier relation, in which prince and land each had, so to speak, its own private treasury, the endeavour of both parties had to tend towards shifting as much of the burdens as possible onto the other.

Since for the estates there was in general nothing recognised at all in the existing condition of a state, and in particular the determination of a civil list, to which the king had already declared himself willing in the charter, was not yet regulated, indeed had not yet come up for discussion, the notions taken from past conditions, which in the changed time had become all the more confused, of the opposition of the interest of the land and the interest of the state, of a land treasury and the state treasury, could have no significance, much less application and efficacy.
zh: 此外它们还向内阁递交了几份直接关乎此事的陈情书，这些陈情书已不再谈论自愿献身，而是要通过要求王家领地管理署、教会财产等等与它们一同分担战争负担，来使这个固然已被耗尽的邦国得到宽减。
为此目的，国王早已让其与盟国以及有关的军事指挥官进行过有效的交涉；等级议会对它的要求所得到的答复很简单：从特别的国家收入中所出者，须在财政预算中以其他来源补足，而眼下所谈的恰恰是非常手段。——按照从前那种关系的意味——在那关系中君主与邦土各自仿佛都有自己的一只私人钱袋——双方的意图都必然趋向于：尽可能多地把负担推给对方。
由于对等级议会来说，一个国家现有的状态中根本没有任何已被承认的东西；尤其是那笔王室费用清单——国王在宪章中已经表示愿意接受它——尚未得到规定，甚至还没有被提出来讨论；那么，那些取自过去情势、在变动的时代里变得更加混乱的表象——即把邦国利益与国家利益相对立、把邦国金库与国家金库相对立的表象——就不可能有任何意义，更谈不上适用与效力。

en: But the principal objection which the estates raised to the king’s call for co-operation in the extraordinary circumstances of the fatherland was this, that they made such co-operation dependent on the granting of their demands, the withdrawal of the royal charter and the reintroduction of the old Württemberg one.

That nobility which on 4 April declared for itself and, believing that it could also stand good for the whole nobility of the empire in this respect, also for the latter in an address to the estates, recognised as its duty to fight in the ranks of the general arming of the country and to sacrifice goods and blood for the fatherland with the remaining estates, explained this the following day to the effect that the declaration submitted was meant only for the assembly of the estates, by no means for the royal state ministry, since writings which flow from the heart are exposed to so many different explanations. - In truth this explanation was the most immediate example of such manifold capacity for explanation. - He therefore subjected his willingness to join with goods and blood in the defence of the fatherland to the measure to be taken by the assembly of the estates.
zh: 然而等级议会对国王「在祖国非常情势中参与协作」的号召所提出的主要反驳是：它们把这种协作变成以满足它们的诉求、撤回王家宪章以及恢复老符腾堡宪法为条件。

有位贵族在 4 月 4 日为自己声明——他相信自己在这点上也能为全帝国的全体贵族作保，因而也为后者在一份致等级议会的陈情书中声明：参加全民武装的行列、与其余等级一道为祖国献出性命财产，是他的义务——次日却这样解释：所提交的那份声明只适用于等级会议，绝不适用于王家国务内阁，因为发自内心的文字会招致五花八门的解释。——事实上，这番解释正是那种多义性的最直接的例证。——因此他把自己愿以性命财产投入祖国防卫的意愿，置于等级会议将要采取的措施之下。

en: But this initiation consisted in the fact that the assembly in an address to the king of the same date brought together both the constitutional question and the measures which the present situation required, although the king had just had it announced to them that for a definitive decision on the former subject he expected the return of the crown prince.

This ground, which for the moment evaded the issue, was an argumentum ad hominem against the estates, since these had proved in lengthy deductions of state law that the right of the male-line heirs to have their assent given in matters of the constitution was theirs; the estates could from the involvement of the crown prince draw the consequence of a factual recognition of this right. - The estates declared in their address somewhat more precisely that nothing was more urgent than to place the people in a position by the united direction of the monarch and the estates to defend the fatherland, and that the will of the honest people offered itself for everything its zeal considered necessary; but they could base their actions only on the foundations of the hereditary constitution, and the restoration of the credit of the state was possible only through a loan guaranteed by the constitution, - that is, if the collection of the taxes and the disposal of this part of the state treasury were handed over to the estates.
The same happened in an address of 18 April, in which they state, "that for all subjects, for the new as for the old, the name old constitution has a magic power".

But it had emerged from the petitions and addresses which had come in that the general indignation against the reappearance of Bonaparte, the feeling of the danger thereby threatening the fatherland, had proved for itself a magic power, had acted like an electric shock.

If it is stated in the address immediately before that the fruit and wine harvest had been frozen and that therefore a great part of the subjects is literally struggling with despair, then it is not obvious how the old constitution could have proved its magic power here, how the estates could have refrained from accomplishing united help by deed under such harsh external and internal circumstances. - Further, it has amply been shown that the old Württemberg constitution exercised not the least magic power on the newer subjects - more than half the land - that they rather regarded what they had received to enjoy from it as a kind of plague, as the worst scourge of the land, - as will be mentioned further on.

Otherwise, however, the whole course of the estates’ deliberations can indeed be looked at as a history of the magic power of that name to which the assembly had from the very beginning surrendered itself without entering into the matter; - or rather, it has already been touched upon above in connection with the estates’ treasury management what formerly lay behind that name, and the account of the oppressive scourge of the land still to be given will bring out something further.

In the present case it is the black magic of the word, which allowed the words, ready to sacrifice goods and blood for the good cause, to come to nothing else than to remain words. - Of this magic power the estates give a more exact account in that nothing secures the fatherland so surely against the poison of the dangerous principles which are now propagated again from France as 25 years ago; - it has already been remarked above that this power has preserved the estates not only against the poison of the elapsed 25 years, but also, so to speak, still much more against the rational concepts of them.
zh: 然而这一着手之处在于：会议在一封同日致国王的陈情书中，把宪法问题与当前情势所必需的措施这两件事合在了一起；尽管国王刚刚让人告知它们：关于前一个对象，他期待王储的归来才能作出确定的决断。

这个暂时回避问题的理由，对等级议会而言乃是一个诉诸个人的论证（argumentum ad hominem）——因为它们在冗长的国家法推演中证明了：王室同宗男系继承人有权在宪法事务上获得它们的同意；等级议会于是能够从王储的参与中推出这一权利已被事实上承认这一后果。——等级议会在其陈情书中更确切地声明：没有什么比通过君主与等级议会的共同领导，使人民有能力保卫祖国更为紧迫；那老实人民的意志愿为其一切热忱认为必要的事效劳；但它们的行动只能建立在世袭宪法的基础之上，而国家信用的恢复只有通过一笔由宪法担保的借款才可能实现，——也就是说，只有把税收的征收与国家金库这一部分的支配权交给等级议会才行。
4 月 18 日的一份陈情书中也发生了同样的事；其中它们声称：「对一切臣民、对新的与旧的臣民来说，「旧宪法」这个名字都具有一种神奇的魔力。」
然而从那些送到的请愿书与陈情书中可以看出：对波拿巴卷土重来的普遍愤怒、对由此而向祖国威胁之危险的感受，本身证明了具有一种神奇的魔力，像一次电击那样起了作用。

如果陈情书在此之前紧接着就指出：水果与葡萄收成被冻坏了，因此很大一部分臣民简直在与绝望挣扎，那么旧宪法在这里如何能证明自己的魔力，就难以理解了；等级议会又怎么能在这样严酷的内外情势之下，不以行动促成共同的援助呢。——此外也已经充分表明：老符腾堡的宪法对较新的臣民——这个邦国一半以上的人——根本没有发挥任何魔力；他们反而把它所给予自己去享受的东西看作一种瘟疫、看作这个邦国最可恶的灾祸——下文还会再说到这一点。
不过，综观等级议会审议的全部进程，倒不妨把它看作一部关于那个名字之魔力的历史——等级会议从一开始就对它屈从，却不去究其实质；——或者更确切地说：上文在谈到等级议会的金库管理时，已经触及当年藏在这个名目之下的究竟是什么；而对那场压抑这个邦国的灾祸的下述说明，还会揭示出更多的东西。
