在当前这个个案中，这是文字的黑魔法：那些甘愿为正义的事业献出性命财产的言辞，除了仍旧只是言辞之外，没有长成任何别的东西。——关于这种魔力，等级议会给出了更确切的说法：没有什么比这更能确实地保护祖国免受那些此刻又如二十五年前一样从法国传播开来的危险原则的毒害；——上文已经指出：这种力量不仅保护了等级议会免受过去二十五年的毒害，而且可以说，还更多地保护了它们免受这些原则的合理概念。

en: As for the more precise aspects of the position which the estates gave themselves, they, in rejecting the royal charter on whose ground they had assembled, were in uncertainty whether they existed at all or not.

Consistently, after the opening made by the king, they would have had to dissolve at once and disperse, or rather, since the manner of election was not in any case suited to the old constitution, they would have had to allow themselves not to be elected at all and the electors not to vote at all. - Since it now became a fundamental maxim of their activity to do nothing out of which a consequence could be drawn to their factual recognition of the royal charter, they proceeded even in the most external formalities as if on eggs.
Already in the first address of 15 March they wisely abstained from the signature "assembly of the estates" and signed themselves "Those summoned to the assembly of the estates".

When in the royal resolution of 17 of the same month this was pointed out to them, that the king expected submissions and motions not from such an assembly but only from the assembly of the land constituted by him in the prescribed form, since it was only to the assembly of the land that the rights determined in the constitutional charter belonged, and that he would in any case not allow himself to be held up by formalities and for the present would look past the want of form - as this resolution really did enter into the content of the estates’ submission -, then the majority found in the signature "assembly of the estates" a prejudice and an inconsistency, until the representative of Marbach, Herr Bolley, put an end to this scrupulosity by the clean expedient of signing in their next submission (of 22. March) indeed in that way, but at the same time laying down a caveat therein!

In this submission it says further that a scruple with regard to formalities would have been an offence against the only purpose, the welfare of the monarch and of the subjects, - namely with reference to their manner of election and their appearance after the summoning.

But why, then, do they remain so scrupulous in the rest because of formalities? Have they not thereby offended against that one purpose, as they say? - In disregard of that conclusion and the caveat interposed, the secretary nevertheless had to announce in the sitting of the 28th that it had only occurred to him after the engrossment of the submission - which engrossed submission was incidentally read aloud again in public in the assembly in the next sitting of 23. March and signed by the president, the vice-president, a holder of a virile vote and an elected deputy and the two secretaries - that the closing word "assembly of the estates" was still missing therein.
This want was therefore removed by a subsequent submission.

In the next royal resolution the assembly was instructed, by an ordered course of business, to remove the errors even of the outward form which had been noticed in their submissions so far, to the end of holding itself to the course of business prescribed in the constitutional charter and in particular of electing a vice-president, likewise secretaries and the estates’ officials.
zh: 至于等级议会为自己所取立场的更具体的一面：它们既已拒斥那部它们据以聚集的宪章，便处于这样一种不确定之中：它们究竟是否存在，还是根本不存在。
按此一贯的逻辑，在国王宣布开幕之后，它们本应立即自行解散、各自分开；或者更确切地说，既然连选举方式本来都不适合旧宪法，那么它们本应根本不被选出，而选举人也根本不必投票。——既然「不做任何可能引出对其事实上承认王家宪章这一后果的事」现在成了它们行动的根本准则，那么即便在最表面的形式上，它们也是如履薄冰。
在 3 月 15 日的第一份陈情书中，它们就明智地避免使用「等级会议」这一署名，而署名为「应召出席等级会议者」。

当同月 17 日的王室决议向它们指出这一点时——国王所期待以合乎规定的方式收到陈情与动议的，不是这样一个会议，而只是由他亲手组建的那个等级会议，因为只有在宪章文书中所规定的权利属于它；并且他无论如何不会因形式手续而耽误，而暂且越过形式上的欠缺——正如这项决议确实深入到该陈情书的内容一样——于是多数人便在「等级会议」这一署名中看出了一种成见与不自洽；最后，由马尔巴赫的代表博莱先生以一个干净的办法了结了这番顾虑：在它们的下一份陈情书（3 月 22. 日）中确实照此署名，同时却在其中附带了一项保留。
在这一份陈情书中还说：对形式手续的顾虑，本身就是对唯一目的——君主与臣民的福祉——的一种冒犯；——即就它们的选举方式以及受召集后的出场情形而言。

那么，它们为什么在其余方面仍然如此顾忌形式手续呢？这样一来，它们岂不是正如自己所说的，冒犯了那唯一的目的吗？——不管那番结论与所附的保留如何，书记员在 28 日的会议上仍不得不报告说：直到那份陈情书誊清定稿之后他才想到，其中毕竟还少了「等级会议」这个收尾的字样；——顺便说一句，那份誊清的陈情书在 3 月 23. 日的下一次会议上又曾在会议中公开宣读，并由主席、副主席、一位亲自享有表决权的等级成员、一位选出的议员以及两位书记员签了字。
这一缺失后来通过一份补充的陈情书而消除了。
在下一份王室决议中，会议被要求通过一套有秩序的办事程序，消除它迄今所送陈情书中连外在形式上的毛病；为此目的，它应当遵守宪章文书所规定的办事程序，尤其应当选出一位副主席、同样还有书记员，以及等级议会的各项职员。

en: It would be too diffuse and too tedious to pursue further the pedantic course of these precautions.

Although the illustrious Mr President repeatedly urged the assembly to the elections of those officials, for whom the king had of course also prescribed the taking of oaths of service, and sought (Vol. III, S. 151) to draw them away from their constant, "repetitions of sentences once uttered which lead no further", "from their forensic" course of advocacy, reminding them, since such an election can in any case take place without prejudice, "not to put the good itself at stake over clinging to forms and to the empty sound of the word", they were in their scrupulosity and cunning far too persistent to be moved to such actions insignificant for their pretensions, - if only their other actions had had more content and significance!
zh: 若要继续追踪这些小心谨慎的迂腐程序，那将过于冗长，也过于乏味。

尽管那位尊贵的主席先生一再敦促等级会议去选举那些官员——国王当然也为这些官员规定了要宣读效忠誓词——并试图使它们（《会议记录汇编》第 3 卷，S. 151）放弃那些「不断重复着一次说过、却引不出任何下文的话句」、放弃「它们那套诉讼式的」律师做派，并提醒它们：既然这种选举本来就不带任何成见，那么「不可因执着于形式与词语的空洞声响而连事情本身也押上」；但它们在自己的顾虑与狡黠中实在太过坚持，不肯为这些对它们的自命而言毫无意义的举动所动——要是它们其余的举动能再多些内容与意义就好了！

en: The more definite claim of the assembly of the estates was that in view of the right the old constitution had not perished and been abolished, that they and the people could only have taken the king’s decision, after the removal of the existing obstacles, to give a constitution, in the sense that the old one should again come into reality.

At the same time it demanded that the king should have its deliberation and approval sought for the ordinances which he issued during the sitting together of the assembly; thus it demanded to exercise the rights of real old estates.

So it appointed no vice-president on the ground that this post was no institution of the old Württemberg assembly of the estates, but it was content with the presidency of the Prince of Hohenlohe-Öhringen and with the participation in voting of the territorial lords, equally no institutions of the old constitution. - For its one and simply put requirement of the restoration of the old constitution it relied on the will of the people expressly uttered at the elections and in a great many addresses presented. - This is a great word; above all the representatives of the people have to beware of despoiling this word or using it lightly.
What the matter was with the will of the new Württemberg people has already been mentioned.
It has also been stated what a man of the people, the mayor Reinhard, said, that so many, yes most of the people have too blunt a feeling for love of fatherland and for defence.
But apart from this, knowing what one wants belongs to the hardest and therefore to the greatest things one can say of a human being.

It is not the first and best out of the people that are picked out to be representatives of the people, but the wisest who are to be taken, because it is not the people who is to know, but they who are to know what its true and actual will is, that is, what is good for it.

How greatly they mistake their dignity and their vocation when they hold on to the loud clamour in this matter, to a clamour so barren as "old constitution", yes even want to rely on the petitions and addresses of this sort.
zh: 等级议会更明确的断言是：就法权而言，旧宪法并没有消亡、也没有被扬弃；它们与人民之所以只能把国王「在消除迄今的障碍之后给出一部宪法」这一决定理解为——旧宪法应当重新成为现实——，正是出于这个意思。
同时它还要求：对于国王在等级会议聚集期间所颁布的各项法令，必须先取得它的商议与批准；这样一来，它就是在要求以真正的旧等级议会身份行使权利。
所以它也没有任命副主席，理由是这个职位并不是老符腾堡等级议会的机构；但它却满足于霍恩洛厄-厄林根亲王担任主席，也满足于等级领主们参与表决——这两者同样不是旧宪法的机构。——为它那唯一而直截了当的要求——恢复旧宪法——它所依据的，是在选举中以及在大量递呈的陈情书中人民明确表达出来的意志。——这是一个了不得的说法；人民代表尤其必须提防，不要亵渎这个说法，也不要轻率地使用它。
新符腾堡人民的意志究竟是怎么回事，前面已经提到过了。
也已经引述过人民中的一人、市长莱因哈德所说的话：人民中有那么多人、乃至大多数的人，对祖国之爱与防卫有着过于迟钝的感觉。
不过撇开这一点不谈：知道自己想要什么，这属于人们能对一个人说出的最困难、因而也最伟大的事情。
被挑选出来充当人民代表的，并不是人民中最好最优秀的那一些，而应当是最有智慧的那一些；因为并不是人民本身应当知道，而是这些代表应当知道人民的真实而实际的意志究竟是什么，也就是：什么对人民是好的。
它们对自己的尊严与使命误解得何等之深：它们竟在这件事上抓住那一片喧嚷不放——甚至抓住像「旧宪法」这样干瘪的喧嚷；它们甚至还想以那些相关的请愿书与陈情书为依归。

en: If, however, they based the nature of their whole authorisation on such a ground and refused to acknowledge the royal authorisation, then they gave themselves a position which steps out of the state organism and stands opposed to the government as an independent power, whose basis, if it does not already contain the poison of a revolutionary principle, at least comes very close to it.

In accordance with this position the assembly of the estates called its negotiations with the government understandings, - they were notes which it exchanged with the same; it called its submission of addresses to the ministry a diplomatic course (Vol. VIII, S. 81) - a course which only sovereign states enter into with one another.

The situation in which the government found itself through the distress of the moment and itself through the tension which was caused by the meeting together of such an assembly of the estates under such circumstances, - furthermore the circumstance that the king probably did not wish to break off again so soon the work he had independently begun, may have contributed their share; but always the moderation of the king is also to be acknowledged, that he overlooked the unformed and the presumptuous of such a relation, entered into a negotiation in this way with the assembly and, although it scorned to be the estates of his realm, nevertheless treated it continually as such.
zh: 然而，如果它们把自身全部授权的性质建立在这样的基础上，并且拒绝承认王室的授权，那么它们就给自己设定了一种脱离国家有机体、作为独立力量与政府相对立的地位；这种地位的根基——即便还不至于包含革命原则的毒质——也至少已经擦着它了。
按照这一地位，等级会议把它与政府的谈判称作「磋商」——那是一些它与政府彼此交换的照会；它把向内阁递交陈情书称作一条外交途径（《会议记录汇编》第 8 卷，S. 81）——一条只有主权国家之间才会走的途径。
政府因当下的困境、并且也因在这样的情势下一个这样的等级会议聚集所引起的紧张，而所处的境地——再加上国王大概也不愿就此中断他独立开创的事业——这些或许都起了作用；但无论如何也应当承认国王的适度：他忽略了这样一种关系的不成形与僭越，以这样的方式与会议打交道，而且尽管会议不屑于做他王国的等级议会，他却始终把它当作这样的等级议会来对待。

en: So much about the formality of the relation into which the estates placed themselves.

But in order to look at the essential of it more closely, it can be observed that after the king had made his charter known to them they could do three things: either refuse to let it hold as binding without examination, therefore enter into an investigation of it and only after the result of this declare themselves; secondly, accept it, but reserve to themselves the working out of what is still missing and undeveloped and to initiate corresponding legislative proposals; or thirdly, reject the royal constitution without examining it, put forward one of their own and demand from the king the acceptance of it. - The demand can seem not merely reasonable but absolutely just, that a people must itself examine the constitution which is given to it and that it can be given validity in no other way than by the people accepting it with its will and its insight; if this were not so, one may add, then despotism, tyranny, infamy could put the people into any fetters. - And yet, to consider the matter from no other side than experience, one may appeal to this, partly that peoples themselves, and indeed the most liberal of them, have acknowledged their unfitness to give themselves a constitution, and have commissioned a Solon, a Lycurgus for this, which men further used a stratagem in order to remove the so-called will of the people and the declaration of this will about their constitution, - partly that Moses like Louis XVIII gave the constitution of their own accord and made not the will of the people but the divine or royal authority the basis of its validity. - In respect of Württemberg, however, the mayor Reinhard of Upper Esslingen has said everything in his dictum: When the Swabians have free will, then nothing happens at all. - But as for the anxiety about despotic constitutions which could come about without consulting the will of the people, ... it may arise from a well-founded mistrust or from a shallow wisdom and cowardly ignorance of the true power of the spirit of the people and of the age; here it is not a hypothesis but a definite case that is in question. - As experience shows, it is just as easy to see from the nature of the thing that nobody can be less capable of making a constitution than what one may call the people, or an assembly of its estates; even if one does not want to consider that the existence of a people and of an assembly of the estates already presupposes a constitution, an organic condition, an ordered popular life.
zh: 关于等级议会为自己设定的这种关系的形式性，就说这么多。

但若要更切近地考察其本质，就可以指出：在国王把它们自己的宪章公布之后，它们有三种做法可择：或者拒绝让它未经审查就具有约束力，因而就它展开一项调查，等到调查的结果出来后才表明态度；其二，接受它，但为自己保留处理那些尚付阙如与尚未展开之处的权利，并据此提出相应的法律草案；或者第三，不加审查地径直拒斥王家的宪法，自己拿出另一部来，并要求国王接受它。——这个要求看上去不仅合理，而且是绝对公正的：一个民族必须自行审查给予它的那部宪法，除了民族以其意志与见识接受它之外，这部宪法不可能以别的方式获得效力；若非如此，人们可以补上一句：那么专制、暴虐与污秽就可以把一个民族套上任何一副镣铐。——然而，若只从经验这一面来考察这件事，人们可以援引这样一些事实：一方面，民族自己——而且是最自由的民族——承认了自己不善于给自己立宪，于是委托了一位梭伦、一位吕库古来做这件事；另一方面，还有一些人物耍了手段，以便消除所谓「人民的意志」以及人民关于其宪法的这一意志的声明——另一方面，摩西与路易十八都出于自身的意愿给出了宪法，他们把其效力的根据放在神圣的或王室的权威上，而不是人民的意志上。——就符腾堡而言，上文那位上埃斯林根市长莱因哈德在其断语中已把一切都说尽了：如果施瓦本人有自由意志，那就什么也不会发生。——至于对那种不经征询人民意志就可能产生的专制宪法的忧虑，……它或许出自一种有根据的不信任，或者出自对人民精神与时代精神的真实力量肤浅的智慧与怯懦的无知；这里所说的不是一个假设，而是一个确定的个案。——如经验所显示的，从事情的本性也同样容易看出：没有人会比人们所谓的「人民」、或比它的一个等级会议更不善于制定一部宪法；即便人们不愿考虑：人民的存在与一个等级会议的存在，本身就已经预设了一部宪法、一种有机的状态、一种有秩序的公共生活。

en: The third course which the Württemberg estates took, of simply rejecting the royal constitution - without examining it and without separating off what they could acknowledge and what not, and what they still missed -, has probably been the most clumsy, the most unbecoming, the most unpardonable.

They thereby at the same time gave themselves the position, conversely towards the king, of demanding from him that he should accept without examination and unconditionally the constitution which they and the people meant to want, even that an act of acceptance no longer belonged to him at all, but that he was already in himself bound to it.

It matters little that they seemed to be free of the presumption of wanting to make, or having made, their own, since it was the old Württemberg constitution which they set against the royal one; they thereby only submitted themselves to the authority of something which could neither stand nor go in itself, and of which they afterwards declared, naively enough (Vol. XI, S. 282), that it was quite impossible for them for the time being to specify it in its full extent, - and why this? because the old archives of the land were still withheld from them! - That the scholar is at a loss when he has lost the key to his library is in order; but if the estates find it impossible to specify their constitution because they do not have the archives for use, what narrow conception of a constitution does this presuppose?

But in the same place it is stated more precisely what the sources are from which "the content of the fundamental laws of the constitution must be enumerated and developed"; this is characteristic enough to be singled out, namely not merely "from the Württemberg house and governmental ordinances, the landtag and committee recessions, the testaments of the regents",
zh: 符腾堡等级议会所采取的第三条路——径直拒斥王家的宪法，既不加以审查，也不把「它们能够承认什么、不能承认什么、还缺少什么」分辨出来——大概是最笨拙、最不得体、最不可原谅的一条路。
它们这样做，同时也反过来对国王摆出了一种姿态：要求他不加审查地、无条件地接受那部它们与人民自以为想要的宪法；甚至说接受这一行为的举措根本已不再属于他，而是他本来就对它负有义务。

它们似乎是免于那种「要自己制造僭越、或者已经制造了僭越」的嫌疑——其实它们拿来与王家宪法相对立的是老符腾堡的宪法；这样一来，它们不过是在服从某种本身既立不住也走不动的东西的权威；后来它们又天真地宣称（《会议记录汇编》第 11 卷，S. 282）：此刻要把它完整地列举出来对它们来说完全不可能；——而这是为什么呢？因为那个旧邦国档案馆还不许它们查阅！——一个文献学者在丢失了自己藏书的钥匙时一筹莫展，这本是理所当然的；但如果等级议会因为拿不到档案可供使用，就认为自己的宪法无法列举出来，那么这是预设了何等狭隘的「宪法」概念！
但在同一个地方还更具体地指明了：那应当据以「把宪法的基本法的内容逐条列举并加以展开」的来源究竟是什么；这一点足够有特色，值得挑出来说：并不只是「符腾堡的家产与政府法令、等级会议与委员会的决议、统治者的遗嘱」——

en: "but also from the various separate codes of law, e.g. the land law, the territorial ordinance, the so-called miscellaneous ordinances, the church and poor-fund ordinance, the marriage and marriage-court ordinance, the pulpit ordinance, the forestry ordinance, the municipal ordinance" etc.
zh: 「而且还要从各种单行的法典中，例如《地方法》《地方条例》、所谓《杂项条例》《教会与济贫金条例》《婚姻与婚姻法庭条例》《讲道条例》《森林条例》《市政条例》等等。」

en: "From countless (!!) individual rescripts and above all from the many resolutions which were issued on estates’ complaints, petitions and wishes."
zh: 「还要从无数（！！）单行的敕令、以及主要地从那些就等级的申诉、请求与愿望所作出的批复中取得。」

en: "Some important propositions can be proved only by the combination of various sources of the Württemberg state law, some only by induction, some only by the force of tradition confirmed in the laws."
zh: 「有些重要的命题，只能通过组合符腾堡国家法的不同来源来证明；有些只能通过归纳来证明；有些则只能通过法律所确认的惯例的力量来证明。」

en: In the same address, further on, the concern is expressed that without presupposing the continuing binding force of this positive constitution one would be led into the labyrinths of the natural state law.
But can there be a more annoying labyrinth than that indicated mass of sources?

A lawyer may well be pleased to have such an armoury, to draw consequences, combinations, inductions, analogies for his deductions in abundance; but how can an assembly of the estates fear reason, the source of the so-called natural state law, and seek help and security against such a fear in plunging deeper into such a paper labyrinth!
If the estates on the one hand demanded of the king that he acknowledge in advance their consequences, combinations, inductions etc. which they will bring to light in due course

(it says in the same place that it would be an undertaking of several years) to be acknowledged in advance from such sources as the rights of the Württemberg subjects, they wanted on the other hand to assert that this was the will of the people, which could not have known such an edifice of constitution which the estates themselves had declared impossible for them to specify!
zh: 在同一份陈情书中更靠后的地方，又表达了这样一种忧虑：如果不预设这部实定宪法持续具有的约束力，人们就会被引入自然国家法的迷宫。
然而还有什么迷宫比那堆所指示的来源更令人恼火呢？
一个律师有这样一座武器库，自然会心里高兴：他可以从中大量汲取推论、组合、归纳与类比，为自己的论证所用；可是，一个等级会议又怎么会害怕理性——那个所谓自然国家法的源头——并且为了抵御这种害怕，去在这样一座纸做的迷宫里越陷越深，以求帮助与安全呢！
如果等级议会一方面要求国王预先承认它们日后将揭示出来的那些推论、组合、归纳等等
（同一个地方说，这将是好几年的事业）从这类来源中预先承认为符腾堡臣民的权利，他们另一方面却又要主张：这就是人民的意志——而人民的意志不可能知道这样一座宪法的建筑，正是那座等级议会自己宣称它们无法列举出来的建筑！

en: One could, moreover, still have taken the view that the estates were not really so serious about their demand of the former constitution, and that they had only the sensible intention of obtaining an alteration of some points of the royal charter, above all a more comprehensive development of the principles, but had at the same time also sought an effective means for the achievement of this purpose.

One can admit that they could not have recourse to any means which would have been at least of a more outward violence than the evocation of the magic formula, as the name of the old Württemberg constitution is also called by them.
The so-called unanimity of the assembly on this point we have seen.

That high and low nobility which still put forward rights that stood in contradiction to the interest and right of the people and the state, yes, which even raised as a problematical question whether it already belonged to Württemberg at all, and spoke of conditions under which it would first be pleased to consent to enter into a relation of subjection, - had to find the magic formula "good old right" quite appropriate for its claims.

The so-called new Württembergers, who at first could not see the remedy for the manifold oppression under which they sighed directly in the royal constitution, attached their opposition to the present condition to that title in the first obscurity about the matter.
zh: 此外，人们本来还可以这样看：等级议会对自己要求恢复旧宪法这件事其实并不真的那么认真，它们只有一种可以理解的意图：争取对王家宪章若干点位的修改，尤其是争取对基本原则更为全面的展开；同时它们也在寻找一种手段，借以有效达成这一目的。
人们可以承认：它们无法诉诸任何一种手段——而这种手段至少要比唤醒那道魔法公式更具外在的强力；那个公式，正如它们自己所称呼的，正是老符腾堡宪法的名字。
会议在这件事上所谓的意见一致，我们已经见过了。
那些仍在主张某些与人民和国家的利益与权利相抵触之权利的上下贵族——它们甚至把「自己是否已经属于符腾堡」当作一个成问题的事情，并谈论在何种条件之下它们才乐意进入一种臣属关系——，就其诉求而言，必然觉得那道魔法公式「美好的旧法权」再合适不过了。
那些所谓的新符腾堡人——他们起初在王家宪法中直接看不出对他们在其下叹息的种种压迫的救济——在最初对这件事的迷惑之中，便把他们的反对挂在了那个名目之下。

en: Addresses and petitions came in from all sides from the towns and offices, deputations appeared which expressed the desire for the restoration of the hereditary constitution, and a great part of the sittings of the assembly was spent with the reading of the addresses.

As worn out and out of credit as the means of popular addresses is, so here it was not scorned; it was all the easier to apply, the greater the influence of the writing class among the people is, of which there will be speech later; but all the less substance and authority could that means have in the eyes of the more enlightened; it was rather suited to throw a shadow over the assembly.
zh: 各个城市与官署的陈情书与请愿书从四面八方涌来，代表团络绎而至，它们明确表达了恢复世袭宪法的要求；而会议的很大一部分会期都花在宣读这些陈情书上。
民众陈情书这一手段既已如此耗损、如此丧失信誉，在这里却仍然没有被弃置不用；文书阶层在人民中间的影响越大，它就越容易施行——关于这一点下文还会谈到；但在较为开明者的眼中，这一手段也就越缺乏实质与权威；它反而更适于给会议投下一层阴影。

en: - In any case it is the place of an assembly of the estates to be the mediating organ between prince and people; and under the predominating external circumstances of the new disturbances in France, with the ordinary lack of understanding of the so-called people when it comes to speaking about general affairs, and still more with the newness of the situation, the want of concepts in the people about a state constitution, since it had never had the thing, with the transition from its political nullity into a hitherto unknown share and influence on the whole of a state - it was all the more the position of the assembly of the estates to leave the people out of the game with its notions so far. - In the fifth sitting Count von Waldek found it necessary, since according to reliable reports the people were disturbed by the publication of the royal constitutional charter, to reassure the same, and proposed as the means of doing this without stir that the representatives should report to the people that they had placed themselves at the head of its prejudices.
Who would call that a reassurance of the people, when the assembly of the estates declares to it that in her - in contrast to the king - it is to see the support of its disquiet!

Incidentally, as so many petitions were read out and the assembly of the estates made so much of them, so one sees again that they have been very neglected, and one learns from the minutes precisely not by what the selection was determined, that one part was read out, the others, as it seems, not even mentioned and noted in the minutes.
Just a few examples: in a sitting of 20.
Dec.
1815 (Vol. XVII, S. 49), there occurs a motion that a number of addresses which had come in should at least be noted in the minutes, be taken as read and be entered into the files.
On 21.
Febr.
1816 a petition of the town of Riedlingen of 12. April 1815 comes up for reading.

On 5. April 1816 a representative asks permission to hand over to a section of the assembly a petition which had already been delivered on 11. June of last year; but under that date, when there was no sitting, and also on 12. June, when a sitting was held, that petition is not mentioned at all. - Many other data of the same kind show precisely that the assembly of the estates did not have an objective respect for the petitions of the people, that is, in so far as they were not simply serviceable for the intentions of the assembly.
zh: ——一个等级会议的本分，本来就是充当君主与人民之间的中介机构；而在法国新的动乱所造成的种种外在情势之下，在所谓的人民一旦谈起公共事务便表现出的、即使出于善意也属寻常的无知之下，更在时局的新奇之下，在人民对于一部国家宪法缺乏概念之下（他们从来没有过这个东西），在人民正从其政治上的虚位转入对一个国家整体的某种迄今未知的份额与影响之下——等级议会就更应当采取这样一种态度：让人民带着它迄今为止的想法退出这场博弈。——在第五次会议上，瓦尔德克伯爵认为有必要这样做——因为据可靠消息，人民因王家宪章文书的公布而感到不安——去使人民安心；而他提出的、不声不响地做到这一点的办法是：代表们应当向人民报告说，它们已经站到了人民种种偏见的头上去。
当等级会议向人民声明：人民必须看到，在它那里——与国王相对立地——有着自己不安的依靠所在，谁还会把这称作对人民的安抚呢！
顺便说一句：既然宣读了如此之多的请愿书，而等级会议又如此看重它们，人们却又看出它们被极其冷落；而恰恰是那些会议记录也看不出：这种取舍是按什么标准确定的——为什么一部分被宣读，另一些似乎连提都没提、在记录中也没有留下痕迹。
只举几个例子：在 20.
1815 年（《会议记录汇编》第 17 卷，S. 49），出现了一项动议：对若干送到的陈情书，至少应在会议记录中加以注明，视同已经宣读，并归入卷宗。
2 月
1816 年，里德林根城 1815 年 4 月 12. 日的一份请愿书付诸宣读。
在 1816 年 4 月 5 日，一位代表请求获准把一份早在去年 6 月 11. 日就已交付的请愿书转交给会议的一个分部；可是，在那个没有开会的日期，以及同样在 6 月 12. 日——那天是开过会的——那份请愿书却根本没有被提及。——还有许多诸如此类的日期同样清楚地表明：等级会议对人民的请愿书并没有一种客观的尊重，也就是说：并非仅仅因为它们对会议的意图有所助益。
